details.text: Each Chd row sets a scale interval from the root, above it when E3 is right of X and below it when E3 is left of X, up to 14 scale steps either way. Turn E3 two detents from X for 3rd, four for 5th, five for 6th and seven for 8th (the octave). In C major with root C these give E, G, A and C. The values follow the scale; they are not MIDI note numbers.
details.title: Chord values

details.text: Select a channel at (3,8), choose its row-1 channel number and open Channel tasks through E1. Use E2 to choose Device, Masks, Clock, Trig params or Harmony and K3 to open the page. On Device, E2 selects a row, E3 changes the named sound and K3 applies it. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel, Len or Chd1/Chd2 and E3 changes the value; hold a step while turning E3 for a local exception. Add a trig mask by holding K1, tapping the step and releasing K1. Steps 1–16 use grid row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7; each group begins at column 1. Hold the first step and tap the last to set a channel range. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination, release, then tap the destination to edit it. The length fader sets 13 steps at (3,7), 16 after three taps at (8,7), 32 at (4,7) and 64 at (7,7). In Song Tempo and feel, choose Tempo and set 90 with E3; set each channel Rate /1 on Clock and apply with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock; K2 clears a held-step lock.
details.title: Shared channel, Song and grid controls

features.musical_use: Set Chd1 to 3rd and Chd2 to 5th for a triad above each root. Use Chord Note Arpeggio so each chord tone has its own short gate, or Chord Note Strum to roll voices across the step. Compare these timing patterns while the scale-third mask keeps the same chord content.
features.prose:
Use chord masks to add up to four voices to the root note. Select a device that supports polyphony. Open Masks, hold the required step, then select and set each chord note.

Assign [Chord Strum](#chord-strum) to vary the timing of the chord components. Assign [Chord Velocity Modifier](#chord-velocity-modifier) to vary their dynamics.

recipes.text:
1. On Masks, set Chd1 to 3rd; play the phrase to hear each root with its scale third.
2. Hold step 1 and set Chd1 to 5th; release it and compare that step with the channel default.
3. Clear step 1 with K2 so it inherits 3rd again.
Outcome: Chord mask values are scale intervals. The step-specific fifth overrides the channel third only on step 1; clearing restores the third.
recipes.title: Add a scale-third chord voice and override it on one step

recipes.text:
Starting point: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major. Assign Doubledecker to channel 1, range 1–16. Set Note MIDI 60, Vel 80, Len 2 steps, Chd1=3rd and Chd2=5th; add trigs at 1, 5, 9 and 13 with roots MIDI 60, 57, 65 and 67. Use the Shared channel, Song and grid controls guide for navigation and coordinates.

**Slot 1 — block chords (bar 1).** In Song Editor set slot 1 length to 16. Leave Strum and Arpeggio locks unset. Play the slot, then stop. Check that roots C, A, F and G (MIDI 60, 57, 65 and 67) sound as block triads, with all three notes starting together.

**Slot 2 — speeding strum (bars 2–3).** Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and set slot 2 length to 32. In Trig params assign Chord Note Strum to slot 1, Chord Spread to slot 2 and Chord Accel Mod to slot 3. On steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 lock Strum to 1, Spread to 1 and Acceleration to -1. Play slot 2. Check that each chord’s notes arrive root, third, fifth, with the gaps shortening through the strum.

**Slot 3 — two-note arpeggio (bar 4).** Copy slot 2 to slot 3 and set slot 3 length to 16. Assign Chord Note Arpeggio to slot 4 and lock Arpeggio 1/2 on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. Arpeggio takes precedence over Strum in this slot. Play slot 3. Check the recorded MIDI event map for the notes of each chord. In C major the four audible pairs are MIDI 60→64, 57→60, 65→69 and 67→71; the fifth is absent.

Play all three slots, then Stop and select slot 1 to restore block chords. The four-bar map is bar 1 block chords, bars 2–3 speeding strum, and bar 4 two-note arpeggio.

On the Masks page, hold a step and press K2 to clear its step-mask overrides. With no grid keys held, hold K1 and press K2 to clear all step-mask overrides on the selected channel. Both actions preserve channel mask defaults, which apply wherever an explicit step override is absent. Held steps take precedence even while K1 is down. Other channels are unaffected.

details.text: Active and Pending identify accepted output, separately from the requested Strategy cursor. Foundation without a valid assigned anchor shows NEEDS ANCHOR and does not apply; the cursor remains at Foundation so the next forward choice reaches Fragments.
details.title: Accepted state and refusal

details.text: Foundation owns trigs only. Fragments owns trigs, notes, velocity and length. Its retained note, velocity and length settings are inactive and read, for example, AVERAGE SAVED; selecting Skip, Only or All restores them. The saved trig merge (Skip, Only or All) is kept while Foundation is Active and is restored from the Strategy selector.
details.title: Attribute ownership

features.musical_use: Choose a strategy, then compare channel playback. In a legacy strategy or Foundation, set the active note, velocity and length merge settings separately. In Fragments, compare its source fragments while the saved legacy settings remain inactive.
features.prose:
Use one shared Strategy selector for channel output. Press grid (14,8) to cycle Skip → Only → All → Foundation → Fragments, wrapping after Fragments. On Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 through the same choices; E3 stops at the first and last choice. A successful choice requests immediately, without K3 Apply.

Strategy is the requested choice. Active is what is sounding; Pending is an accepted change waiting for its boundary, or NONE. While stopped, a valid choice applies immediately. During playback, Boundary names NEXT CYCLE or NEXT PATTERN.

Foundation controls trigs only. Note, velocity and length merge settings remain active. Fragments controls all four attributes. Retained note, velocity and length settings are labelled inactive and their values read as the saved mode followed by SAVED, for example AVERAGE SAVED. Those rows and their grid buttons do not edit saved values while Fragments is active. Select Skip, Only or All to restore the retained settings.

Foundation needs a valid assigned anchor. A refused request leaves the cursor at FOUNDATION and shows NEEDS ANCHOR, while Active and Pending keep their accepted values. The next forward detent or grid press reaches Fragments.

[Merge modes demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=2065s)

features.musical_use: Select All to play trigs from any assigned pattern. Select Skip to exclude shared steps. Select Only to play steps shared by more than one pattern.
features.prose:
Skip, Only and All are the first three choices of the shared Strategy selector. They define how trigs are combined across assigned patterns:

* **All**: Trigs will apply if they appear on a step in any selected pattern.
* **Skip**: Trigs will apply only if they appear on a step in exactly one selected pattern. If a trig appears on a step in multiple patterns, it won't activate.
* **Only**: Trigs will apply only if they appear on a step in more than one selected pattern, ignoring those that appear in just one.

features.musical_use: Compare Average, Higher and Lower using the same source patterns. Check the resulting scale degrees: Higher and Lower are calculated from the mean and range, not the maximum and minimum alone.
features.prose:
These modes determine how note values are handled when steps overlap:

* **Average**: Average the contributing note values and round to the nearest integer, choosing the greater integer at an exact half (1.5 becomes 2; -1.5 becomes -1; -0.5 becomes 0). One contributor passes through unchanged. The result then uses the configured scale and pentatonic processing.
* **Higher**: Add the difference between the highest and lowest contributing note values to their rounded average. One contributor passes through unchanged; the result then uses the configured scale and pentatonic processing.
* **Lower**: Subtract the rounded average from twice the lowest contributing note value: `2 * lowest - rounded_average`. One contributor passes through unchanged; the result then uses the configured scale and pentatonic processing.
* **Pattern**: To prioritise a specific pattern's note values during conflicts, hold the note merge button and select the desired pattern. You can even select patterns that aren't current asigned to the active channel.

By default, notes will snap to the pentatonic version of the currently active scale to assist with avoiding unpleasant harmonic interactions. This can be disabled in _Mosaic_'s settings.

recipes.text:
Starting point: use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1, C major and playback stopped. If Polyperc 1 is missing from the Device picker, install and enable `nb_polyperc` in SYSTEM > MODS; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b). Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1, give it range 1–16 and assign patterns 1 and 2. Turn Lock merged to pent. Off.

Prepare the two-slot comparison with slot 1 selected. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then use E1 for tasks and E2 to choose a task; K3 opens it. In Pattern Trig and Pattern Note, choose patterns from row 1 and edit their steps. On Masks, E2 selects a value row and E3 changes it; hold K1 while tapping a step to add a trig. Open Song (6,8), leave slot 1 selected, and set its length to 32 with the length fader at (4,7). Keep slot 1 selected while preparing both patterns and setting Average. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 only after that setup, as described in step 5. Set Song tempo to 90 in Song tasks → Tempo & feel; set channel Rate to /1 on Clock and apply with K3.

Purpose: compare the same two source patterns under two note-merge rules. Average combines overlapping notes by their mean; Higher adds the range between their highest and lowest values to that mean. Notes from only one pattern should stay the same in both slots.

1. In Pattern Trig, pattern 1, tap steps 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 13. In Pattern Note, set degrees 0, 2, 4, 2, 0 and 4 at those steps.

2. In Pattern Trig, pattern 2, tap steps 1, 5, 9, 11, 13 and 15. In Pattern Note, set degrees 2, 6, 3, 3, 0 and 5. On the Note grid, row 7 is degree 0 and each row above is one degree higher.

3. On channel 1 Masks, leave Note and Trig at X so the patterns supply pitches and trigs. Set Vel to 80 and Len to half a step. These are the recorded channel masks.

4. Open Channel tasks → Merge modes. Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until the screen reads ALL. Select Note mode with E2 and turn E3 until the screen reads AVERAGE. Set Song slot 1 length to 32.

5. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and select slot 2. Keep its length at 32; on Merge modes choose Note mode and set it to UP (Higher). Select slot 1 at (1,1) to return to Average, then play the slots in order. Stop playback when you have heard the comparison.

Listen for: The trig pattern and notes from a single contributing pattern stay the same in both slots. Only notes where the patterns overlap change.

Restore: Select slot 1 for Average. Keep Lock merged to pent. Off and Trig Merge All for this recording, then return to the separate course project.

details.text: Two patterns play notes 2 steps and 4 steps long on the same steps. Average gives 3 steps (the mean). Longer gives 3 + (4 - 2) = 5 steps. Shorter gives 2 x 2 - 3 = 1 step. Longer is therefore not simply the longest source, and Shorter not simply the shortest. Hold K1 and tap grid (16,8) to cycle Average, Longer and Shorter; the cycle wraps back to Average.
details.title: Worked example: lengths 2 and 4

details.text: The numeric comparison starts with source lengths 2 and 4 channel steps. Average gives 3; Longer gives 5; Shorter gives 1. Keep pitch and velocity fixed and inspect the Note Off after each Note On: the interval between them is the played gate length. An ordinary nonpositive result releases in the same pulse. A receiving instrument’s envelope can change the audible tail, so use the MIDI gate to distinguish these settings.
details.title: Compare short and sustained notes

features.musical_use: Assign patterns with short and long notes. Compare Longer and Shorter. Nonpositive lengths send Note On then Note Off in one scheduler pulse; the receiving instrument determines the audible result.
features.prose:
These modes dictate how the duration of notes is calculated for overlapping steps:

* **Average**: Average the contributing lengths and round to the nearest integer, choosing the greater integer at an exact half. One contributor passes through unchanged. Source lengths account for interruption by the next trig in that pattern.
* **Longer**: Add the difference between the longest and shortest contributing lengths to their rounded average. One contributor passes through unchanged.
* **Shorter**: Subtract the rounded average from twice the shortest contributing length: `2 * shortest - rounded_average`. One contributor passes through unchanged. Only the mean is rounded at this stage, so fractional source lengths can still produce fractional Longer or Shorter results.
* **Pattern**: To apply a specific pattern's length values, hold the length merge button and press the pattern's select button.

Length merge modes are set by holding shift (K1) and pressing the velocity merge mode button. Numeric merging retains zero and negative length results. For ordinary note playback, including delayed strums, a nonpositive effective length sends Note On followed by Note Off in the same scheduler pulse, without advancing musical time. This describes MIDI event order, not the sound or response of a connected instrument.

features.prose:
Set the global composition tempo in Song tasks → Tempo / feel. Every Song slot uses this tempo. Open Channel tasks → Clock to set a division or multiplication for each channel; differing clock rates let channels run at different speeds relative to the shared tempo.

Set channel Swing to move notes closer together or farther apart. Swing ranges from -50 to 50. Use it to vary off-grid timing, including jazz or funk rhythms. Shuffle uses more complex patterns based on 21echoes’ [Cyrene](https://github.com/21echoes/cyrene), with selectable feel and basis. Channels can use independent settings.

If a channel's swing/shuffle settings are not set ("X"), they will take the global setting, which is set on the Song page's Tempo and feel screen. Selecting "X" again after choosing a local Swing or Shuffle mode restores global mode inheritance, just like an untouched channel; choosing either mode explicitly overrides the global mode. While playback is running, confirmed changes on this channel page take effect at the next global song-pattern boundary, including a repeat of the same pattern. They do not take effect immediately or at the next step of a shorter channel loop. While stopped, confirmed changes apply immediately.

[Clocks, swings and shuffle demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=2623s)

recipes.text:
Starting point: Use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and global Swing 0, with playback stopped. Assign Oilcan 1 to channel 1 and Polyperc 1 to channel 2. Set both channel ranges to 1-16 and turn Snap note masks to scale Off.

Controls used here: open Channel at (3,8), select the channel on row 1 and turn E1 to Channel tasks. Use E2 and K3 to open Device, Masks or Clock. On Device, E2 selects a row, E3 selects a value and K3 applies it. In Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel or Len and E3 changes the value; hold K1 and tap a step to add a trig, or hold a step and turn E3 for a local value. Open Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are on row 1. Hold slot 1 and tap slot 2 to copy. Set tempo through Song tasks → Tempo & feel. Each channel has its own Clock page; E2 selects Swing type or amount, E3 changes it and K3 applies it.

1. On channel 1 Masks, set Note MIDI 36, Vel 80 and Len half a step.

2. Add trigs at steps 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 10, 13 and 14.

3. Set steps 2, 6, 10 and 14 to MIDI 37; set steps 5 and 13 to MIDI 38. Steps 1 and 9 stay at MIDI 36.

4. On channel 2 Masks, set Note MIDI 48, Vel 60 and Len half a step.

5. Add trigs at steps 1, 4, 9 and 12.

6. Set steps 4 and 12 to MIDI 55 and step 9 to MIDI 52.

7. In Song Editor, set slot 1 length to 32 steps.

8. Copy slot 1 to slot 2; leave slot 2 at length 32.

9. With slot 2 selected, open Clock for channel 1. Select Swing type with E2, choose Swing with E3 and press K3.

10. On channel 1 Clock, select Swing with E2, set it to 25 with E3 and press K3.

11. Repeat steps 9–10 on channel 2. Leave slot 1 straight.

12. Play the two slots in order. Bars 1–2 are straight; bars 3–4 use Swing 25, moving only the second step in each pair. Stop and select slot 1 to restore the straight version.

Listen for: Bars 1-2 are straight. Bars 3-4 use Swing 25; only the second step in each pair moves.

Restore: Select slot 1 to hear the straight version again, then stop playback and return to the original project.

details.text: The counter shows the current position and the total, for example 2 of 2. 0 of 2 is the floor: the oldest state, before any retained edit. features.prose:
Memory retains all mask and trig-lock actions, including recorded actions. Use the norns encoder to navigate the selected channel’s history.

Open Channel Editor and choose History from Channel tasks. The Memory screen shows your position in the channel's memory, the selected action, and how many actions you can still undo and redo.

- Use E3 to step back through past actions or forward towards more recent ones.
- Press K3 to jump directly to the latest action.
- Press K2 to return to the beginning of the memory.

To jump to the latest action and erase all subsequent memory, hold shift (K1) and press K3. To jump to the first action and erase all memory recorded after it, hold K1 and press K2.

[Memory demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iGx5fmrbatA&t=202s)

controls.gesture: Hold start step → press and release a later end step → release start
controls.result: Commit the inclusive active range when the end step is released; brighter grid steps show it.

controls.gesture: Choose an end before the start
controls.result: Reject the reversed range with a message and preserve the previous range.

details.text: Choose a different end step after the start. The two-key gesture cannot select a one-step range or wrap to an earlier end step. Holding a step alone does not change the range.
details.title: Range restrictions

details.text: For channel 1 hold step 1 (grid (1,4)), tap and release step 16 ((16,4)), then release step 1. For channel 2 select it with (2,1), hold step 1, tap and release step 5 ((5,4)) and release step 1. Each channel needs notes to be heard. While one song pattern keeps playing, the ranges realign after the lowest common multiple of their lengths: 16 and 5 realign after 80 steps. A song pattern change resets the channels together unless Reset at Song Sequence Change is turned off in Options.
details.title: Setting two ranges

features.musical_use: Give a drum channel a sixteen-step range and a melody channel a five-step range. The five-step figure starts on a different drum step each bar, and both return to their shared start every eighty steps (see Run two channels at different lengths in Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops).
features.prose:
Set channels independently, including the global scale pattern, within the 64-step sequence.

To set a channel range, hold its start step in Channel Editor. While holding the start, press and release a different, later end step, then release the start. The range commits when the end step is released. Brighter buttons indicate the active range.

The gesture cannot select a one-step range. A long hold alone has no effect; the held step remains available for combinations with other buttons, including a subsequent end-step press. The end must follow the start. A reversed selection shows a message and leaves the previous range unchanged. Channel ranges do not wrap from the final step to the first. The same restrictions apply to the Scale Editor range. Pattern note-length wrapping is unchanged.

Use the norns parameter [options](#options) to configure sequencer handling of channels with different lengths.

[Channel length demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=2470s)

features.musical_use: Assign Fixed Note to a drum channel. Assign Trig Probability to another slot and reduce it on selected quieter steps.
features.prose:
Assign trig parameters to change sequencing or device sound values. Trig parameters belong to a song pattern, so different sections can use different parameter settings. Sequencer defaults such as Strum are saved with the project and restored per song pattern after loading; device patch values remain shared across patterns. Each channel has up to 10 assigned parameters. Set an individual [trig lock](#locks) on a step to override its parameter default. This per-step parameter method is also used on Elektron synthesizers.

The Trig params screen of the channel editor shows all ten slots at once. Each slot shows its parameter's two short names from the device definition, the first above the value and the second below, so together they name the parameter (for example `Quan` over `Note` for Quantised Fixed Note). The names stay still; one too long for its slot is cut short. A value too wide for its slot shows `...`, and while that slot is selected its full name and whole value take the last line. Use the following controls:

* **Screen Navigation**: Use E1 to open Channel tasks, then choose Masks, Trig params or another screen with E2 and open it with K3.
* **Changing Parameters**: To select a slot, turn E2. Adjust its value by rotating E3. To fine tune, rotate E3 whilst holding K1.
* **Activating Parameters**: To activate a different parameter within the same slot, press K2 to open the parameter list, turn E3 to browse, press K3 to assign, and press K2 to return.
* **Locking Changes**: As you adjust values, the system automatically saves your changes. You can also create "trig locks" on specific steps by holding down the step and turning E3. This allows you to set values that will override the default parameter for that step.
* **Default Parameter Values**: A pre-set parameter value is transmitted to your selected device on steps without a trig lock, unless the value is off or a parameter slide is active.
* **Handling Off Settings**: An explicit MIDI parameter lock set to "off" sends no value for that parameter on that step. It does not resend the previous lock or restore the default, so the device keeps its last received value. An off lock does not itself cancel a parameter slide that is already running; that slide may continue sending values.

[Params and trig locks demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=2235s)

details.text: Quantised Fixed Note moves the number to the nearest note of the active scale. In C major 63 (D sharp) lies between 62 and 64; ties go to the lower note, so it plays 62. Fixed Note would play 63.
details.title: Why 63 can play 62

features.musical_use: Set an absolute MIDI note in the required register. Change the active scale and check the nearest playable pitch.
features.prose: Quantised Fixed Note supplies an absolute MIDI pitch, 0–127, and selects the nearest playable note in the active scale at its configured root (or the song root when unset). Equally close notes select the lower pitch. The number includes its octave; channel/step octave, transposition, chord degree/rotation and pentatonic switches do not modify this override. It replaces pattern, note-mask and random pitch calculations for the ordinary root voice; separately generated chord/arp voices have their own processing. Fixed Note takes precedence. A step lock set to Off inherits the channel value; when both are Off, ordinary pitch processing resumes. Off does not silence the trig.

details.text: Random Note n adds a random scale-degree offset. n = 1 gives 0 or +1, 2 gives -1 to +1, 3 gives -1 to +2 and 4 gives -2 to +2. Random Twos Note uses the same ranges in steps of two degrees. When both are set the offsets add, so 4 and 4 can move a note by up to 6 degrees either way. Each pass draws new offsets; the manual examples use a fixed seed so that they repeat exactly.
details.title: How the value sets the range

features.musical_use: Set a small Random Note value on the last step of a repeated phrase. Leave the remaining steps unchanged.
features.prose: Set Random Note to add a random offset to the selected note. A value of 0 will leave the note unchanged. A value of 1 will randomly give your existing note or the note one higher in the scale. A value of 2 will randomly give your existing note, the note one higher in your selected scale, or the note one lower. A value of 3 will randomly select notes -1, 0, 1 or 2. A value of 4 will randomly select notes -2, -1, 0, 1 or 2. Higher values continue this range expansion. Apply step locks where required. Random Note can be combined with Random Twos Note. By default, random notes are quantised to the pentatonic version of the currently selected scale to limit dissonant intervals. This can be disabled in _Mosaic_'s param settings. With Lock random to pent. enabled, a nonzero sum of Random Note and Random Twos offsets triggers nearest-pentatonic snapping for ordinary notes and fully quantised note masks, in either direction. Zero sums, including cancellation, do not trigger this option; other applicable pentatonic options still apply. Equal-distance pitches choose the lower note. Snap-only and unquantised masks retain their chromatic random-offset behaviour. Fixed Note and Quantised Fixed Note retain their override precedence.

details.text: Arpeggio values are lengths in channel steps: 1/24 is the shortest and 128 the longest; X switches the arpeggio off. 1/2 repeats the chord slots at half-step intervals for the length of the note. Turning E3 down stops at X and turning it up stops at 128, as on the Chord Strum page.
details.title: Division values

features.musical_use: Set a long note and populate two chord slots. Leave another slot empty to include a rest in the repeating arpeggio.
features.prose:
Set Chord Arp to repeat the chord-mask slots at the selected step division for the current note’s length. Notes are quantised to the current scale. Empty chord masks are treated as rests, allowing for rhythmic patterns. Arpeggios also honour the Chord Velocity and Chord Shape modifiers. The Chord Arpeggio param overrules the chord strum param. Chord arpeggios can also be used as ratchets if no chord masks are set.

With Chord Spread at zero, the first arp interval is one full selected division of the channel step. For example, a half-step arp on a two-step note advances through its slots at 0, 1/2, 1 and 1 1/2 steps; it does not start another note at the two-step endpoint. Each arp note lasts one selected division from its own onset, shortened when necessary to finish at the original note's endpoint.

Starting another arp on the same channel cancels the old arp's future notes. Notes already sounding keep their remaining duration, capped by their original endpoint; the old arp's endpoint does not cut notes from its replacement. Pattern resets likewise preserve the remaining duration of sounding notes. Stop releases sounding notes and cancels future arp notes. Overlapping notes of the same MIDI pitch still send a corresponding Note Off for each Note On; how a receiving instrument handles overlapping voices is unchanged.

Chord Shape orders the root and four chord-mask slots. An empty mask slot, or a muted root slot, is a rest and keeps its position, including at the end of the sequence. Rest slots consume the same time and acceleration ordinal as sounding slots. If no chord masks are populated, an unmuted root instead forms a one-slot ratchet; if the root is also muted, the result is silence.

Slot 4 sounds at once; slot 3 is empty and follows 3/4 step later; slot 2 is empty and follows 1/2 step after that; slot 1 sounds 1/4 step after that, 1 1/2 steps after the trigger. features.musical_use: Set Arpeggio to half a step, Spread to a quarter step and Acceleration to +1. Each successive gap increases.
features.prose:
Chord Acceleration modifies the spacing of an enabled Strum or Arpeggio together with Chord Spread. Off (0) means no progressive change: every gap is the selected division plus Spread. A positive value lengthens each following gap; a negative value shortens it. With Spread at zero, Acceleration has no effect.

In channel-step units, let `d` be the Strum or Arp division, `s` be Spread, and `a` be Acceleration (zero when off). The gap before slot `k`, counting the first gap as 1, is `d + s * (1 + (k - 1) * a)`. The first slot occurs at trigger time; later slot times are the sums of these gaps. A new trigger restarts the ordinal. Wrapping an arp's slots does not restart it. These are the nominal musical times before swing and clock-pulse quantisation. An arp interval occupies at least one scheduler pulse, including after swing. At fast channel rates, this limits the resolution of very short gaps.

For a division of 1/2 and Spread of 1/4:

| Acceleration | Successive gaps | Slot times from the trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Off | 3/4, 3/4, 3/4, 3/4 | 0, 3/4, 3/2, 9/4, 3 |
| +1 | 3/4, 1, 5/4, 3/2 | 0, 3/4, 7/4, 3, 9/2 |
| +2 | 3/4, 5/4, 7/4, 9/4 | 0, 3/4, 2, 15/4, 6 |
| -1 | 3/4, 1/2, 1/4, then 0 | 0, 3/4, 5/4, 3/2, then stop |

When the next gap is zero or negative, scheduling ends before that slot. There is no extra simultaneous note or reversed time; notes already sounding retain their releases. Empty slots, including trailing rests, advance the same ordinal in both strums and arps.

details.text: A step On or Off overrides the channel. With no step lock, the channel applies; channel X follows the global Quantise note masks option. features.musical_use: Enable Quantise Note Mask for masks that should follow scale changes. Set a step OFF when it should not use full quantisation.
features.prose: The Fully Quantise Mask param controls whether note masks on a step are fully quantised to the current scale, including scale degree and rotation adjustments. On maps written note masks through the scale, including Degree and Rotation. Off leaves full mapping disabled; the separate Snap note masks to scale option may still snap accidentals. Set this parameter per channel or step to override global quantisation. Channel X uses the global Quantise note masks setting; explicit Off and On override it. An explicit step X uses the global setting directly, bypassing the channel value. Clearing that step lock instead restores the channel value (and therefore the global setting if the channel is X).

features.musical_use: Change the harmony of a melody without changing its rhythm or pattern degrees. Prepare a different scale in an unused slot, then apply it when you want to hear it.
features.prose:
The Scale Editor sets the harmony of the whole song and holds 16 scale slots. Changing the scale changes the pitches that pattern degrees produce; it does not change rhythm or pattern degrees.

Apply a scale:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor. The scale slots are the 16 buttons on Grid row 3. The applied slot is brightly lit.
2. Short-press a slot. It is applied to every channel and selected for editing.
3. To turn global scale off, short-press the applied slot again. The slot stays selected for editing. With global scale off and no scale lock, pattern degrees play as chromatic semitone offsets. Press the slot again to apply it.

A pattern uses the applied scale unless a global scale lock or a channel scale lock overrides it.

Edit a slot:

1. Turn E2 to select Root, Scale, Degree, Transpose or Rotation. Scale tasks are Scale, Scale clock and Overview.
2. Turn E3 to change the value of the selected row. The title row names the slot you are editing.
3. Release all grid keys, then press K3 to apply the changes or K2 to cancel. Tapping any grid key, including Play/Stop, cancels an unapplied edit, so press K3 first.

Edit a slot without playing it:

1. Hold K1 and press the slot, or long-press a slot that is not selected for editing.
2. Edit the slot as above and press K3. Playback does not change. A dim indicator marks the editing slot when it differs from the applied slot.
3. Long-press the slot already selected for editing to turn global scale off and clear the editing selection.

Applying changes to the slot that is playing changes the sound immediately.

Set a scale lock: hold a step and press a scale slot. On the Scale page the lock is global for channels without a channel scale lock; on a channel page it applies to that channel. See [Scale Locks](#scale-locks).

The global scale track has its own rate and length, so a chord progression can run over a different number of steps from the patterns. On the Scale clock task, E2 selects Rate and E3 changes it; K3 applies. The same screen shows the selected range, the global cap and the playable range as read-only values. To change the length, hold the first step of the range on the scale track and press its last step. The end must come after the start: a reversed selection is rejected with the tooltip End must follow start and the previous range stays, and ranges do not wrap from the last step back to the first.

Video: [Scale editor demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2741)

recipes.text:
Starting point: channel 1 has Pattern 1 assigned and plays a four-step melody in C major with Pattern Note degrees 0, 1, 2 and 3; its channel Note mask is X. It sounds MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 (C, D, E, F). To build it, follow [Dig Deeper](#dig-deeper): assign Pattern 1 to channel 1, add trigs on steps 1–4, set Pattern Note to degrees 0, 1, 2 and 3 in order, leave the channel Note mask at X, and apply C major in scale slot 1. The captured examples below start from the same setup: Save D major, then apply it follows steps 1 to 5, and Prepare a scale before applying it adds browsing a slot with a long press, editing the applied slot and turning the global scale Off.

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor. Slot 1, the left button on row 3, is bright.

2. Hold K1, press slot 2 at (2, 3), then release both. The title row names slot 2 and a dim indicator marks it. Playback is still in C major.

3. Prepare slot 2: turn E2 to Root and turn E3 two clicks to D. Release all grid keys and press K3 to save the draft. Checkpoint: tap Play (1,8), listen, then tap Stop. The melody still plays C, D, E, F because slot 1 remains applied.

4. Apply the draft: short-press slot 2 at (2, 3). It becomes the bright applied slot. Tap Play (1,8), listen, then tap Stop: the melody plays D, E, F sharp, G (MIDI 62, 64, 66, 67). The rhythm has not changed.

5. Restore the comparison: short-press slot 1 at (1, 3), tap Play and listen. C, D, E, F are restored.

features.prose:
Use the transposition fader on the Scale page to transpose every channel of the selected Song Sequence without editing any note. Rhythm and intervals stay the same.

Set global transposition:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.
2. Press a button on the transposition fader, Grid row 8, columns 8–16. The tooltip shows Transpose and the new value.

The fader buttons set these values: (9,8) is -12, (10,8) -8, (11,8) -4, (12,8) 0, (13,8) +4, (14,8) +8 and (15,8) +12. The end buttons, (8,8) and (16,8), lower or raise the value by one semitone each press.

The global value is added to the active scale slot's Transpose value. With scale slot 1 as C major and the melody 60, 62, 64, 65, +2 plays 62, 64, 66, 67.

You can change transposition while playing. A note that is already sounding keeps its pitch and length. The next notes use the new value.

To change transposition from a certain step onwards, use [transposition locks](#transposition-locks).

Video: [Global transposition demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2905)

recipes.text:
This recipe changes the transposition fader on a copy of a slot, so the copy plays a tone higher while the original stays put. It is a different workflow from the captured example below, which shows the fader being pressed while a note is sounding.

Start with Song slot 1 holding a finished sequence, such as a four-note melody on MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, with playback stopped and Song mode at its default (On).

1. Press Grid (6, 8) to open the Song Editor. Slot 1 at (1, 1) is lit: it is the slot you are working on.

2. Hold slot 1 at (1, 1) and press slot 2 at (2, 1), then release both. Slot 2 now holds a copy of slot 1 (copying overwrites whatever slot 2 held).

3. Press slot 2 at (2, 1) to select it while stopped.

4. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.

5. Press the right end of the transposition fader, (16, 8), twice. Each press adds one semitone and the tooltip shows Transpose: 2.

6. Press Play. Slot 2 plays 62, 64, 66, 67. With Song mode On, playback moves on to the next slot after the repeats set in Slot setup; to hold on one slot, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn Song mode Off (E3). Press Stop.

7. Press Grid (6, 8), then slot 1 at (1, 1), and press Play to hear the original at 60, 62, 64, 65, because slot 1 kept its transposition of 0.

Check that the raised notes are still inside the usable range of the sound you are playing.

features.prose:
The Song Editor contains 96 Song Sequence slots, arranged in six rows of 16. Slot 1 is grid (1,1), slot 2 is (2,1), slot 16 is (16,1), slot 17 is (1,2) and slot 96 is (16,6). Each slot stores one complete sequence: which patterns each channel plays, merge modes, masks, scales, mutes and the sequence length. Use a slot for each section of a song.

Press Song, grid (6,8), to open the editor. The norns shows Song Playback. Fill slots by copying a finished section into a new slot and editing the copy (see Interacting with Slots). Read slot brightness in Button Indicators. Let Song mode chain slots automatically with Song Mode Operations. Set how many steps a section plays with the fader on row 7 (Adjusting Song Sequence Length).

Watch: [Song editor demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2972)

recipes.text:
Starting point: slot 1 holds a four-step motif on channel 1 (C, D, E, F; MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). To build it, assign Pattern 1 to channel 1, add trigs on steps 1–4, set Pattern Note to degrees 0, 1, 2 and 3 in C major, and leave the channel Note mask at X; see [Dig Deeper](#dig-deeper) for the Pattern Editor reference. Playback is stopped and Song mode is On (the default; Song Playback shows it as AUTO). Slots 2 and 3 are empty and dim at (2,1) and (3,1).

1. Press Song (6,8). Slot 1 at (1,1) is bright because it is selected. A slot plays 64 steps by default, about eleven seconds at 90 BPM with Rate /1, so shorten the audition first: tap (2,7) to set the global length to 1 step, then tap (8,7) three times to make it 4 steps. The length belongs to the slot, so the copy in step 2 keeps it.

2. Hold slot 1 at (1,1), press slot 2 at (2,1), then release both. Slot 2 turns mid-bright: it is a full copy of slot 1.

3. Tap slot 2 at (2,1). It turns bright and slot 1 drops to mid-bright.

4. Press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Slot 2 now plays the motif an octave higher. Slot 1 is unchanged. Change a rhythm or a mask instead of the octave if you prefer.

5. Press Song (6,8) and look at slot 3 at (3,1). It stays dim because it is empty, and an empty slot ends the group after slot 2.

6. Tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Slot 1 plays the motif (60, 62, 64, 65), then slot 2 plays it an octave higher (72, 74, 76, 77), then playback returns to slot 1 and repeats.

Each slot plays for its global length times its Repeats, so with the length left at 64 a slot lasts about eleven seconds. Check or change Song mode in Song tasks > Slot setup (see Song Mode Operations). The captured example Loop a song group or hold one slot, below, plays two groups built this way (slots 1-2 and 4-5) and what happens when Song mode is turned Off.

features.prose:
Read Song slot status from the grid. The slots fill rows 1 to 6.

* Dim buttons indicate empty slots.
* Mid-glow buttons indicate slots containing rhythms and patterns.
* The brightly lit button identifies the Song Sequence that is selected, or playing.
* A slot you pressed during playback blinks (its light pulses down and back up) until the current sequence finishes and the slot takes over.

Example: copy slot 1 to slot 2 and select slot 2. Slot 1 is mid-bright, slot 2 is bright and slot 3 is dim. Press Play and slot 2 stays bright. Press slot 1 while slot 2 plays: slot 1 blinks until slot 2 finishes, then slot 1 turns bright and slot 2 returns to mid-bright. Copy empty slot 3 over slot 2 while stopped and slot 2 goes dim.

features.prose:
Press a slot button to select its Song Sequence. Slot 1 is grid (1,1), slot 2 is (2,1), slot 16 is (16,1) and slot 17 is (1,2). While stopped, the press selects the slot at once and the norns shows Slot setup for it. During playback, the press queues the slot until the current sequence finishes.

To copy a slot, press and hold the source slot, press the destination slot, then release both. The destination becomes a full copy of the source. Editing the copy leaves the source untouched. The destination’s previous contents are overwritten, so copy onto an empty slot unless you mean to replace it.

To erase a slot, copy an empty slot over it: hold the empty slot and press the slot to clear. There is no undo.

recipes.text:
Starting point: slot 1 holds a section you want to keep, for example the four-note motif C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Playback is stopped and the Song editor is open (Song, grid (6,8)).

1. Hold slot 1 at (1,1). While holding it, press an empty slot, slot 2 at (2,1). Release both. Slot 2 changes from dim to mid-bright: it is a full copy and slot 1 is untouched. Copying overwrites the destination, so choose an empty one.

2. Tap slot 2 at (2,1). It turns bright (selected) and slot 1 drops to mid-bright.

3. Edit the variation while stopped: press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Only slot 2 changes. (Changing a mask instead works too; either edit stays in the selected slot.)

4. Press Play (1,8). Slot 2 plays the motif an octave higher (72, 74, 76, 77); with Song mode On playback then carries on to slot 1, so press Stop when you have heard enough. Press Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play: the original section still plays 60, 62, 64, 65. Tap slot 2 to compare.

The destination is a full copy, so editing it never changes the original. To erase a slot you no longer need, hold an empty slot and press the slot to clear. There is no undo. The captured example [Copy a slot, then change the copy](#song-mode-operations/song-copy-and-compare) shows steps 1 to 3 (the copy and the octave edit); to hear slot 1 and slot 2 compare, follow [Build two song groups](#song-mode-operations/song-build-two-groups), which plays the copies. The captured example [Read Song slot lights](#button-indicators/song-slot-light-states) shows the lights for a copy and for the erase.
recipes.title: Copy a slot before editing

recipes.text:
1. Stop playback. In Song view, set the song length to two steps and copy slot 1 into slot 2. Select slot 2 at (2,1) before channel editing.
2. Select channel 1 and raise its octave for slot 2.
3. Compare the copied slot’s stored motif and octave setting with slot 1.
Outcome: Slot 2 begins as a copy of slot 1, then its channel octave is set to +1.
recipes.title: Copy a Song slot, then raise the copy by one octave

recipes.text:
Starting point: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major, with playback stopped. If Polyperc 1 or Doubledecker is missing from the Device picker, install and enable the corresponding `nb_polyperc` or `nb_doubledecker` mod in SYSTEM > MODS; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b). Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 and Doubledecker to channel 2. Give each channel range 1–16.

**Controls and map.** Press Channel at (3,8), select its number on row 1 and turn E1 to Channel tasks. Use E2 and K3 to open Device, Masks or Trig params. On Device, E2 selects a row, E3 selects the sound and K3 applies it. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel or Len and E3 changes the value. Hold a step while turning E3 for a local value; hold K1 and tap a step to add a trig. Steps 1–16 are row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7; the column is its position within that group (step 33 is (1,6), step 61 is (13,7)). Hold the first step and tap the last to set a channel range, then release. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination, release, then tap the destination to edit it. On the length fader, (3,7) gives 13 steps and three taps at (8,7) give 16; (4,7) gives 32 and (7,7) gives 64. In Song Tempo and feel (E1 tasks, E2 task, K3), set Tempo to 90 and press K3. Set each channel Rate /1 on its Clock page and apply with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock; K2 clears a held-step lock. Stop before copying or editing an independent comparison.

**Prepare the two patterns.** On channel 1, create pattern 1 with trigs 1, 5, 9 and 13; set their degrees to 0, 0, 4 and 0. Set channel 1 octave to -1, velocity to 70 and length to half a step. On channel 2, create pattern 2 with trigs 3, 7, 11 and 15; set their degrees to 4, 2, 4 and 6. Set channel 2 octave to 0, velocity to 60 and length to half a step. Checkpoint: in C major the bass is MIDI 48, 48, 55, 48 and the lead is MIDI 67, 64, 67, 71.
**Assign the patterns.** Before arranging, press Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap pattern slot 1 at (1,2). Select channel 2 at (2,1) and tap pattern slot 2 at (2,2).

**Slot 1 — intro.** In Song Editor set slot 1 length to 16 steps and mute channel 2 with K1 plus its selector (2,1). Check: slot 1 is one bar of bass with the lead muted.

**Slot 2 — verse.** Copy slot 1 to slot 2, set slot 2 length to 32 steps and toggle channel 2 back on. Check: the two-bar verse has both parts; bass remains 48, 48, 55, 48 and lead remains 67, 64, 67, 71.

**Slot 3 — outro.** Copy slot 2 to slot 3 and set slot 3 length to 16 steps. Set channel 2 octave to +1 and channel 1 Velocity to 40. Check: the one-bar outro keeps the same four bass pitches at lower velocity and raises the lead to MIDI 79, 76, 79, 83.

Play the three slots in order, then Stop and select slot 1. The arrangement is intro (bass only), verse (bass and lead), outro (higher lead and softer bass). This is a separate arrangement example; return to the continuing course project when finished.

features.musical_use: Separate Song groups with empty slots. Press a slot in another group to queue a change at the current sequence boundary.
features.prose:
Song mode plays your slots as an arrangement. It is on by default. With Song mode on, the sequencer advances to the next filled slot after the current slot has played its Repeats. Turn it on or off in Song tasks > Slot setup (select Song mode with E2, set it with E3, apply with K3) or in PARAMS > MOSAIC > Song mode.

A run of filled slots with no gap is a group. When playback reaches an empty slot, it returns to the first filled slot of its group. Slots 1 and 2 with slot 3 empty therefore play 1, 2, 1, 2 and so on. Use empty slots to separate groups.

Press another slot during playback to queue a change. The slot blinks, and the change takes effect after the current sequence, including its repeats, completes. This is how you move from one group to another.

With Song mode off, slots do not advance by themselves: the selected slot keeps repeating. A queued manual selection still takes over at the end of the current sequence.

recipes.text:
Starting point: channel 1 plays its default four-note motif (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) on slot 1, the first slot. Song mode is On (the default) and playback is stopped. Group A will be slots 1-2 and group B slots 4-5. Slots 3 and 6 stay empty.

1. Set the length: press Song (6,8) with slot 1 selected. Tap (2,7), which sets the global length to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once to add one step. The length is now 2 steps, so each slot plays only the first two notes, 60 and 62.

2. Copy slot 1 to slots 2, 4 and 5: hold slot 1 at (1,1) and press slot 2 at (2,1). Repeat for slot 4 at (4,1) and slot 5 at (5,1). The copies keep the two-step length.

3. Voice slot 2: tap slot 2 at (2,1), press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Slot 2 will play 72, 74.

4. Voice slot 4: press Song (6,8), tap slot 4 at (4,1), press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +2 at (12,8). Slot 4 will play 84, 86.

5. Voice slot 5 the same way: Song (6,8), slot 5 at (5,1), Channel (3,8), channel 1 at (1,1) and octave -1 at (9,8). Slot 5 will play 48, 50.

6. Check the lights: slots 1, 2, 4 and 5 are mid-bright, slots 3 and 6 are dim and the selected slot is bright.

7. Tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Group A loops: slot 1 plays 60, 62, slot 2 plays 72, 74, then empty slot 3 sends playback back to slot 1.

8. While slot 1 sounds, tap slot 4 at (4,1). It blinks, queued. When slot 1 finishes, group B plays: slot 4 plays 84, 86, slot 5 plays 48, 50, then empty slot 6 returns playback to the first slot of group B. To go back, tap slot 1 or slot 2 to queue a return to group A.

For a more musical version, replace the octave edits with a different bass rhythm or harmony in group B and keep one motif in both groups. The captured examples below build these slots: Build two song groups follows steps 1 to 7, up to the first group looping, and Loop a song group or hold one slot builds the same slots and goes on to the second group and queued selection (step 8).

features.musical_use: Shorten a section without changing channel endpoints. Increase global length to restore the remaining steps. Channel lengths and clock rates can differ within this limit.
features.prose:
Use the fader at the lower left of the Song Editor to set the global length of the selected Song Sequence from 1 to 64 steps. It is on row 7, columns 1 to 8. Press Song (6,8) to open the editor. A press on the fader opens Song Playback on the norns, where Global length shows the new value.

* (1,7) subtracts one step. (8,7) adds one step.
* The inner buttons jump to a coarse value: (2,7) sets 1, (3,7) sets 13, (4,7) sets 32, (5,7) sets 38, (6,7) sets 51 and (7,7) sets 64.
* To reach an exact value, jump to a nearby coarse value and finish with the end buttons. For 16, tap (3,7) and then (8,7) three times.

Channel start and end steps may lie outside the global-length range. A channel’s played length cannot exceed global length. The limit counts steps from the channel start: with channel range 2–4 and global length 2, playback repeats steps 2 and 3. Increase global length to restore the remaining selected steps.

The same limit applies to the scale track. Each track follows its own clock rate, and explicit song reset options still apply.

Watch: [Global pattern length demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=3160)

recipes.text:
Starting point: channel 1 plays a four-step motif on steps 1 to 4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Its channel range is steps 1 to 4 and the global length is 64 steps. Playback is stopped.
1. Press Song (6,8). The length fader is on row 7, columns 1 to 8.
2. Tap (2,7) to set the global length to one step (the buttons between the ends jump to 1, 13, 32, 38, 51 and 64), then tap (8,7) once to add one step. Song Playback shows Global length reading two.
3. Press Play (1,8). Only the first two steps play: MIDI 60, 62, 60, 62 and so on. The channel range is still steps 1 to 4, so nothing is deleted.
4. Press Stop (1,8). Tap (8,7) twice to set the global length to four steps, then press Play. All four steps return: 60, 62, 64, 65.
Use this to loop a short fragment of a longer motif without editing it, then restore the full phrase. The end buttons (1,7) and (8,7) change the length one step at a time. The captured example Set the global song length, below, uses the two end buttons on the Song Playback screen: it takes one step off 64 (63) and puts it back. Its later Play result auditions the chosen length; inspect that result to compare the shortened phrase. Stop before restoring the full length.

features.prose:
The Song page opens on Playback. This read-only screen shows the playing slot (Playing), the slot that follows (Next, or HOLD when Song mode is off), the current pass within its repeats (Pass, for example 1 / 2), the global pattern length and whether Song mode is advancing (AUTO) or off (MANUAL). Turn E1 to open Song tasks: Playback, Slot setup, Tempo / feel and Channel view.

Open Slot setup to set Repeats, the number of passes the selected Song Sequence plays before Song mode advances, and to see Song mode. With Song mode off, select slots manually.

Open Tempo / feel (the screen is titled GLOBAL FEEL) to set the global tempo and Swing or Shuffle. The tempo is shared by every slot.

Channel view opens the same screen as in Pattern tasks: the viewed channel on its own.

features.musical_use: Change one step without editing the pattern: lift a single bass note an octave, accent one hit, open a filter on the last note, or change the scale for one part of the phrase.
features.prose:
A lock stores a value on one step, so that step differs from the channel default. Hold the step on the grid, change the value, then release the step. The lock stays in place and the screen returns to the channel default.

Each lock type has its own control:

1. Parameter lock: on Channel tasks > Trig params, hold a step and turn E3. See [Trig Param Locks](#trig-param-locks).
2. Mask lock: on Channel tasks > Masks, hold a step and turn E3. See [Mask Locks](#mask-locks).
3. Octave lock: hold a step and press an octave button on Grid row 8, columns 8–12. See [Octave Locks](#octave-locks).
4. Scale lock: hold a step and press a scale slot on Grid row 3. On a channel page the lock affects that channel. On the Scale page it is global. See [Scale Locks](#scale-locks).
5. Transposition lock: on the Scale page, hold a scale-track step and press the transposition fader on Grid row 8. See [Transposition Locks](#transposition-locks).

Parameter, mask and octave locks change their own step only. A transposition lock stays in force on the steps that follow it until a later transposition lock replaces it. A channel scale lock lasts as set by Scales lock until ptn end (see [Scale Locks](#scale-locks)). A global scale lock lasts until another global lock replaces it or the scale track wraps.

To remove a lock, hold its step and press K2 on the screen where you set it. For octave, scale and transposition locks you can also press the same button again.

recipes.text:
Start with a routed four-note C–D–E–F phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65), pattern 1 on steps 1–4, stopped. Keep the line low but lift its second note.

1. On Channel, tap octave −2 at (8,8). Play and stop: the line moves down two octaves. The octave buttons (8,8) through (12,8) select −2, −1, 0, +1, +2.
2. Hold step 2 at (2,4), tap −1 at (9,8) and release. Play and stop: only the second note is one octave higher than its neighbours. A local −1 replaces the channel −2; it is not added to it.
3. Hold step 2 and press K2, then release. The step inherits −2 again.
4. Hold step 2 and tap 0 at (10,8), then release. This explicit zero plays the written register on step 2. Clear it with held-step K2 to restore the bass register.

Outcome: an octave exception changes one step, and clearing restores the channel register. Compare the authentic results at [Octave Locks](#octave-locks).
recipes.title: Use a channel octave for a bass line and a local octave exception

recipes.text:
Start with the four-note C–D–E–F melody. Setup A: on the Scale page, set global transpose to +4. Setup B: hold scale-track step 2, set its transpose lock to 0 with the fader, then release it. The zero lock persists until the next lock or the scale-track wrap. Now compare the lock on step 1 with inheritance.

1. Hold scale-track step 1 and move its transpose lock to 0 using the fader. The held-step tooltip shows zero: this is a chosen value, not an empty lock.
2. Release the step. Global +4 remains on the fader, while the step’s zero replaces it when that step is reached.
3. Hold step 1 and press K2 to clear only that lock, then release. Step 1 follows global +4; the separate zero lock at step 2 remains and restores the written pitch from step 2 onwards.

Outcome: clearing a zero lock restores inheritance; it does not erase the next step’s lock. See [Transposition Locks](#transposition-locks) for the direct-tap comparison.
recipes.title: Distinguish an explicit zero transpose lock from inheritance

recipes.text:
Comparison purpose: keep the note pattern fixed while only the Decay envelope changes. This recipe has two exercises: compare longer and shorter Decay tails with relative turns, then try the 0.1 s and 3.2 s endpoints. Use a separate project so neither changes your course arrangement.

Starting point: use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and playback stopped. Make sure n.b. PolyPerc is installed and enabled using [Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b); assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 with range 1–16. In Masks set default velocity 70 and Len ½. Add trig masks on odd steps by holding K1, tapping each odd step and releasing K1. Select Note with E2; for each odd step, hold it and turn E3 to set the absolute MIDI note: step 1=48, 3=55, 5=52, 7=55, 9=48, 11=55, 13=53 and 15=55. Press Channel at (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap Pattern 1 in the second-from-top grid row to assign it before playing; an empty project has no pattern assigned by default.

Controls and step map: press Channel at (3,8), select its number on row 1, then turn E1 to Channel tasks. Use E2 to highlight Device, Masks, Clock, Trig params or Harmony and K3 to open it. On Device use E2 for the row, E3 for the named sound and K3 to apply. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel, Len or Chd1/Chd2; E3 changes the value. Hold a step while turning E3 for a local exception, then release it. To add a trig mask, hold K1, tap that step and release K1. Steps 1–16 are row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7. Column is the position within that group. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination and release; then tap the destination to edit it. Set Song Tempo to 90 and each channel Rate to /1, applying changes with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock. K2 clears a held-step lock.

Relative-turn comparison — compare longer and shorter Decay tails while keeping the note pattern fixed. In Song, select slot 1 and set its length to 32 steps with no parameter locks; this is the two-bar straight reference. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and keep slot 2 at 32 steps. Tap slot 2 before editing its locks. Open Channel tasks → Trig params and assign Decay to slot 1. In slot 2, hold step 1 and turn E3 clockwise by 200 detents; release it. Repeat the 200-detent turn on step 9 and release. Then hold step 5 and turn E3 clockwise by 40 detents; release it. Repeat the 40-detent turn on step 13 and release. Check: steps 1 and 9 form the longer-tail group; steps 5 and 13 form the shorter-tail group, while the note pattern stays fixed. These turns are relative to the current setting; the absolute Decay value shown depends on its starting value and your device. Select slot 1 before comparing the two slots. Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1 to restore the plain line.

Separate endpoint practice — try the 0.1 s and 3.2 s endpoints. In Song set slot 1 to 32 steps with no parameter locks. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and set its length to 32. Tap slot 2 before editing its locks. In slot 2, hold step 1 and turn E3 anticlockwise until the displayed Decay reaches its 0.1 s minimum, then clockwise to the displayed 3.2 s maximum; release the step. Repeat the 3.2 s setting on step 9. Set Decay to 0.1 s on steps 5 and 13, releasing each step afterward. Check the Trig params readout for the long settings on 1 and 9 and short settings on 5 and 13. Select slot 1 before comparing the two slots. Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1. On your instrument, compare the tails while the notes stay in the same order.

Restore: Select slot 1 to restore the unmodified line. Stop and return to the separate course project when finished.
recipes.title: Practice longer and shorter Decay envelopes

features.musical_use: Change a sound on one step: a brighter filter on the last note of a phrase, a longer envelope on an accent, a different effect send on one hit.
features.prose:
Before you set a parameter lock, assign the parameter to one of the ten Trig params slots (see [Trig Parameters](#trig-parameters)). The value you set with no step held is the channel default that every step sends.

Set a parameter lock:

1. Open Trig params from Channel tasks with E1.
2. Turn E2 to select the assigned slot.
3. Hold a step on the channel sequencer.
4. Turn E3 to the value for that step. While the step is held, the cell shows the held value and an L marker.
5. Release the step. The cell shows the channel default again; the step keeps its lock.

Clear a step's parameter trig locks:

1. Open Trig params.
2. Hold the step and press K2.

Clear all parameter trig locks on the channel:

1. Open Trig params.
2. Release all steps.
3. Hold K1 and press K2.

Video: [Trig locks demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2235)

recipes.text:
Start with a channel that has trigs on steps 1 to 4 (see Build a phrase), sends to a device that lists a controller you can hear on a filter, and is stopped. This recipe uses CC 74, the usual filter cutoff controller: a generic CC device lists it as CC 74, and a device whose configuration names it shows it as Cutoff. The scenes on this page use CC 1 the same way.
1. Open Trig params: turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params, press K3.
2. Turn E2 to slot 1, press K2, turn E3 to CC 74 (Cutoff), press K3 to assign it, then press K2 to return to the slot view.
3. With no step held, turn E3 to 40, the channel default: every step sends CC 74 = 40 before its note.
4. Hold step 4, the last trig, and turn E3 to 100 (the cell shows 100 and the L marker). Release step 4 and the cell shows 40 again.
5. Press Play. Steps 1 to 3 sound with cutoff 40 and step 4 sends CC 74 = 100 just before its note, so the last note of each loop is brighter.
6. To remove the accent, hold step 4 and press K2.
On this page, the scene Lock a value, then clear just that step shows the same gestures with Fixed Note, the MIDI strip of Use the first and last Trig params slots shows CC values arriving just before their notes, and Keep a stored value while locking a step shows one locked CC value ahead of a step's note while the other steps send the stored value. For a smooth rise instead of a jump, see Param Slides.

features.prose:
A slide needs at least two parameter locks of the same parameter on the channel. Set them first (see [Trig Param Locks](#trig-param-locks)).

Slide a parameter across the whole channel:

1. Open Trig params and select the parameter with E2.
2. Release all steps and press K3. The cell shows S.

Between every pair of locks of that parameter the value now moves gradually. Press K3 again with no step held to switch it off.

Slide from one step only:

1. Hold the step that has the lock you want to slide from.
2. With the parameter selected, press K3.

The held step slides to the next lock of that parameter. Other locks of the parameter still jump.

Slides do not cross into a different song pattern. Turn on Wrap param slides to let the last lock of a repeating pattern slide back to the first lock (see [Parameter Slides Wrap](#parameter-slides-wrap)). Slides use extra processing, so use them only where you need them.

Video: [Param slides demo](https://youtu.be/iGx5fmrbatA?t=515)

recipes.text:
Starting point: Use a stopped four-step channel with trigs on steps 1–4 and a Trig params slot assigned to CC 1 (or the CC that controls your filter). See “Brighten the last note” on Trig Param Locks for slot assignment. The MIDI monitor or the linked event map is the check; no instrument sound is required.

**Make one two-step slide.** Open Trig params and turn E2 to the assigned slot. Hold step 1, turn E3 to 24, release; hold step 3, turn E3 to 96, release. Release all steps and press K3. The cell shows S. Play once: CC 1 leaves 24 at step 1 and reaches 96 as step 3 starts; the captured event map reads 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96. Press Play again to stop.

**Compare local and channel scope.** Hold step 4, turn E3 to 48, and release. This third endpoint distinguishes a slide on step 1 from a channel-wide slide. With no step held, press K3 to turn the channel-wide slide Off. Hold step 1 and press K3; its cell shows S while held. Play: 24 slides toward 96 between steps 1 and 3, then jumps to 48 at step 4. Stop. Check that this is the step-local slide while the channel-wide setting is Off.

**Wrap the channel slide.** Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn Wrap param slides On. Release all steps and press K3 to turn the channel-wide slide on again. The step 4 lock now slides back toward 24 across the loop boundary instead of holding at 48. Check the loop-boundary CC values on the monitor/event map.

features.prose:
A mask has a channel default and, for each step, an optional step lock. With no step held, E3 changes the channel default. With a step held, E3 changes the lock on that step only.

Set a mask lock:

1. Open Masks from Channel tasks with E1.
2. Turn E2 to the mask you want, for example Note or Vel.
3. Hold a step on the channel sequencer.
4. Turn E3 to the value for that step.
5. Release the step. The screen shows the channel default again; the step keeps its lock.

Clear a step's mask locks:

1. Open Masks.
2. Hold the step and press K2.

Clear all step-mask locks on the channel:

1. Open Masks.
2. Release all steps.
3. Hold K1 and press K2.
Channel default masks are retained.

Video: [Mask locks demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=1780)

recipes.text: This Masks note shows how a step Note exception differs from the channel G3 default. Complete canonical walkthrough: [Make one step override a channel Note default, then restore inheritance](#melody-composition/recipe/1).
recipes.title: Make one step override a channel Note default, then restore inheritance

recipes.text:
Starting point: channel 1’s phrase has active trigs on steps 1 and 2.

1. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. Select Vel with E2. With no step held, turn E3 to 50 for the channel default.
2. Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 clockwise to 90 and release. This exception makes the first hit louder.
3. Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 anticlockwise to 0 and release. Its note is silent while the first hit keeps the 90 accent. Play and stop to compare them.
4. Hold step 2 again, press K2 and release. It now inherits the default 50; the accent on step 1 remains.

features.prose:
Scale slots are the 16 buttons on Grid row 3. A scale lock applies a slot from a chosen step. Set it on a channel page for that channel only, or on the Scale page for every channel that has no channel scale lock.

Set a channel scale lock:

1. Select the channel and hold a step on the channel sequencer.
2. Press the required scale slot on Grid row 3. The norns screen shows Scale source.

Set a global scale lock:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.
2. Hold a step on the scale track and press the required scale slot on Grid row 3. The norns screen shows Scale overview.

Clear a step lock:

1. Hold the step.
2. Press K2, or press the same scale slot again.

A channel scale lock overrides the global scale and global locks.

With Scales lock until ptn end On (the default), a channel scale lock lasts until the channel wraps to its start or another channel scale lock replaces it.

With the option Off, the lock lasts until the next active trig that passes its probability check. A trig that fails its probability check does not clear it. A scale lock on the next accepted trig replaces the previous lock.

Global scale-track locks ignore this option. They last until another global lock replaces them or the global scale track wraps.

Video: [Scale locks demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2854)

features.prose:
Transposition locks belong to the global scale track on the Scale page. Reach the Scale page from the Channel editor with Grid (4,8) and set the lock on a scale-track step there, not on a channel step.

Set a transposition lock:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.
2. Hold a step on the scale track.
3. Press the required value on the transposition fader, Grid row 8, columns 8–16.
4. Release the step. The norns screen shows Scale overview.

From that step, the lock replaces the global transposition fader value. It is added to the selected scale's own Transpose value. It stays in force on the following steps until a later transposition lock replaces it.

A lock of 0 is a real lock. It cancels the global transposition from that step. It is not the same as having no lock.

Clear a transposition lock:

1. Hold the step on the Scale page.
2. Press K2, or press the same fader value again.

Set an octave lock:

2. Press an octave button on Grid row 8, columns 8–12: (8,8) is -2, (9,8) is -1, (10,8) is 0, (11,8) is +1 and (12,8) is +2.

details.text:
Open [Enter a project name and keep the arrangement](#save-and-load/lesson/save-named-arrangement) for the complete name-entry demonstration. The sequencer is stopped with SONG 01 selected. This separate demonstration loads a copy of the finished course arrangement and opens Slot setup through the public Song grid control. It begins with the first Save attempt already cancelled and < Save project selected. It is not a continuation of the original course recording.

1. Stop playback and select SONG 01. Open the Song editor with its grid control. Turn E1 clockwise to open Song tasks, select Slot setup with E2 and press K3. SLOT SETUP / SONG 01 is the starting screen.
2. Press K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and select Save project with E2. Press K3 to open name entry. Press K2 to cancel this first attempt. The Save project menu returns without creating a named file.
3. Press K3 to open name entry again. The suggested name is new, with OK selected.
4. Turn E2 left to DEL. Press K3 three times to remove the suggested name. The name is empty.
5. Turn E3 left to the character row. Turn E2 until F is the bright character, then press K3. F appears in the name.
6. Select o, u and r with E2, pressing K3 after each character. Select the blank space and press K3. Select n, o, t, e and s in the same way. The name reads Four notes.
7. Turn E3 right to the DEL / OK row, then turn E2 right to OK. Press K3 to save. Press K1 to return to Mosaic. SLOT SETUP / SONG 01 returns.
8. Press K1 to return to PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select Load project with E2 and press K3. Turn E2 until Four notes.ptn is selected. This confirms that the named project is available; leave it selected without loading a different project.
9. Press K2 to cancel the picker, then K1 to return to Mosaic. The same arrangement remains open.

Saved Four notes: the named project retains the complete arrangement and its parameter file. Four notes.ptn is available in the Load picker; cancelling the picker leaves SLOT SETUP / SONG 01 open.

Saving under an existing name replaces that save. Use a distinct name when retaining an earlier version. If loading leaves the norns tasks unresponsive, tap the Song editor grid control before opening Song tasks; the demonstration uses this explicit public starting navigation.
details.title: Enter a name: separate arrangement demonstration

features.musical_use: Save a named project before trying a change, so you can return to the earlier version. Autosave is a safety net, not a version history.
features.prose:
Save a named project:

1. Press K1 to open PARAMS and choose MOSAIC.
2. Choose Save project.
3. Enter a descriptive name on the text entry screen and press K3 to confirm. The suggested name is new.

Mosaic writes a project file (.ptn) and a parameter file under that name. Saving under a name that already exists replaces that save. Press K2 in the dialog to cancel; no file changes.

Load a project: open PARAMS > MOSAIC, choose Load, pick the file in the file picker and press K3.

Use named saves for versions that autosave must not overwrite. When playback is stopped, 60 seconds of inactivity normally saves the current project as autosave. Mosaic loads the most recent autosave at startup. Named saves are separate files and autosave does not change them.

Before replacing the current project, Mosaic checks saved song slots, global lengths, channel ranges and scale-track ranges. If a check fails, the screen identifies the problem. The current project and playback are retained.

A rejected load suspends autosave to protect the rejected file. Editing, playing and cancelling a dialog do not resume autosave. A successful valid load, a successful named save or New resumes the normal idle autosave interval. A failed save leaves autosave suspended.

Valid saved one-step ranges are supported. There is no one-step range gesture. Validation covers the saved range structure; it does not check every possible corrupted project field.

features.prose:
Mosaic keeps its settings in the norns PARAMS menu, not on the grid. Tap K1 to open the norns menu, choose PARAMS, then choose MOSAIC. Turn E2 to move between rows and turn E3 to change the selected value. Changes take effect at once; there is no apply step. Press K2 to step back and K1 to close the menu.

The MOSAIC list also holds the project actions (save, load, new). The settings are grouped as Sequencer, Parameter locks, Quantiser, Midi control and Screen. Every option is described in its own section below with its default, and every option starts at that default in a new project.

recipes.text:
Goal: make an accidental tap safe, confirm the deliberate stop gestures, then leave automatic Song playback enabled.

1. Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC.
2. Select Shift press to stop and turn E3 to On, so a stray tap cannot stop the sequencer.
3. Press K2, then K1, and start playback with Play/Stop at grid (1,8). A quick second tap is ignored, and so is a hold shorter than one second.
4. To stop, hold K1 and tap Play/Stop, or hold Play/Stop for one second or more. Shift press stop lists every stop gesture.
5. Leave Song mode On, its default, if the arrangement should advance on its own. [Decide whether a slow channel restarts](#reset-at-pattern-repeat/repeat-reset-policies) turns Song mode Off to show the difference, and [Set Song slot repetitions](#navigating-the-norns-display/song-slot-repeat-values) shows Song mode in Slot setup. The other option groups are described below.

recipes.text:
Goal: align the three-step phrase with each 64-step song section, then compare that with a phrase that carries its phase across sections.

1. Hold step 1 on the Channel editor and tap step 3 to give channel 1 a three-step range, shorter than the 64-step slot. In the Song editor (grid (6,8)) hold slot 1 at (1,1) and tap slot 2 at (2,1) to copy it, so the song has two slots.
2. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Leave Song mode On and Reset on song seq change On, close the menu and press Play. Watch the slot LEDs: slot 1 is bright.
3. After 10.7 seconds (64 steps at 90 BPM) the LEDs swap to slot 2. Because the reset is On, channel 1 starts its three-step line again on its first step at that moment, so it lines up with the section at every change.
4. Stop, turn Reset on song seq change Off and play again. The three-step line now carries on across the change and drifts against the sections, which is the right choice for evolving polyrhythms.
Reset at Song Editor Pattern Change shows the same lesson with the exact note times.

features.musical_use: Leave On for a finished arrangement; turn Off to stay on one section or move between sections by hand.
features.prose:
Song mode is On by default. With Song mode On, the song steps through its slots on its own, according to the Song Editor's global length and the groups of slots you filled. Playback moves from one slot to the next when the current slot reaches its global length, and a group of slots loops.

With Song mode Off, Mosaic keeps playing the selected slot and moves only when you select another slot yourself. Use Off to rehearse a single section or to move between sections by hand. Song mode also decides whether the repeat reset in Reset on pattern repeat applies: with Song mode Off, a repeating slot is not reset.

recipes.text:
Starting point: Song mode is On (the default) and the song has two filled slots, slot 1 and slot 2, so it would normally play 1, 2, 1, 2 and so on. Playback is stopped. This comparison rehearses one slot without stopping playback; a manual selection takes effect at the end of the current pass.

1. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC (tap K1), select Song mode and turn E3 to Off.

2. Press Song (6,8) to open the Song editor. The slots are the buttons on rows 1 to 6; slot 1 is (1,1) and slot 2 is (2,1). Tap the slot you want to rehearse, for example slot 1 at (1,1).

3. Press Play at (1,8). The slot repeats: with Song mode Off it never moves on to slot 2 by itself, so you hear the same section again and again.

4. To move to another section, tap its slot, for example (2,1) while the music plays. The press is queued and takes over when the current pass ends. Turn Song mode On again to run the whole arrangement.

For comparison, with Song mode On the same two slots play 1, 2, 1, 2. The captured example [Loop a song group or hold one slot](#song-mode-operations/song-mode-groups-and-selection) shows both: with Song mode On a group of slots loops, and with Song mode Off slot 1 repeats (60, 62, 60, 62) and a manual selection of slot 2 still takes over at the end of the pass.
