details.text:
Before starting: Start a new project with Record off. No output, patterns or masks have been entered yet. The walkthrough below begins by choosing an output for channel 1, so you can follow it from an empty project. [Configuring an Output](#setup) explains the choices.

### Choose the output

1. Tap Channel (3,8). The header reads CH01.
2. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, select Device with E2 and press K3.
3. Select a working output with E3: the basic MIDI device (CC Device), your own configuration, or Polyperc 1 for internal sound. Press K3 to apply.

Device shows the output you chose. A selection that has not been applied with K3 is only a draft.

### Enter four attacks

1. Tap Pattern (5,8) to Trig. The header names pattern 1.
2. Tap (1,4), (2,4), (3,4), (4,4).

Four active attacks light on row 4. Each lit step is a trig, a point where a note can sound. If you are editing another pattern, select pattern 1 on the top row first.

### Assign and shorten

1. Tap Channel (3,8).
2. Tap pattern slot (1,2).
3. Hold step (1,4), tap (4,4), release (1,4). To set a range, hold its first step, tap its last step, then release the first.

Pattern 1 feeds channel 1 across a four-step range, so the channel loops steps 1 to 4.

### Give the attacks a pitch and level

1. Open Channel tasks → Masks.
2. With no step held, select Note with E2 and set MIDI 60 with E3 (C3). The Masks screen labels MIDI 60 as C3.
3. Select Vel and set 80.
4. Select Len and set 1/2.

These are channel masks: all four attacks share one pitch, velocity and length. A step could override them later.

### Play and stop

1. Tap Play (1,8).
2. Listen for four equal C notes repeating, with a playhead moving along the grid. At 90 BPM and the default Rate /1 each step lasts one sixth of a second, so the loop repeats about every two thirds of a second.
3. Tap Play again to stop; hold K1 too if Shift press stop is enabled.

Four equal C notes repeat. Playback stops with notes released.

Resulting project: Pattern 1 attacks 1–4; CH01 assigned P1; range 1–4; Note 60/Vel 80/Len1/2; no step exceptions; stopped.

features.prose:
Use the loop in [Creating a First Loop](#first-sound). Check the following in order.

1. Check that the grid playhead moves. If it does not, press Play. For an external clock source, check that the source is running and sending clock. Use the internal clock for a standalone check.
2. Select the intended channel and check that it is unmuted. Assign a pattern or enter trig masks. An unassigned source pattern does not play through the channel.
3. Check that active attacks are inside the channel range. If several patterns are assigned, check whether Skip removes their overlaps. Compare one assigned pattern or All trig merge.
4. Open Masks. Check Trig, Note, Vel and Len at channel and held-step scope. An explicit step value overrides its default. Velocity 0 is silent. Clear an exception to restore inheritance.
5. Open Device. Apply the selection with K3; a draft is not the active destination. For MIDI, match output port and receive channel. For n.b., check that the player is installed, enabled and supported. Check norns audio level and the listening path.

For hanging notes, stop playback, then hold a non-selected page navigation key to invoke panic. Panic sends Note Off messages but does not stop playback. A running sequence can sound new notes after the sweep.

The examples on this page each show one of these checks. Keep each channel independent shows that Device belongs to one channel, so a channel with Device None makes no sound (check 5). Keep a valid range when a gesture is reversed shows the channel range in check 3: a range gesture whose end would come before its start is refused, the previous valid range stays, and only the attacks inside that range sound. Merge two patterns shows how Skip removes the trigs two patterns share (check 3). Set velocity and length masks shows that velocity 0 is silent and that X lets the pattern's own velocity through (check 4). Create a four-step loop from an empty project is the working loop to compare against.

review.native_gap: Native scoped scenes cover basic playback, device scope, mutes, ranges, mask silence and merge choices. Physical cabling/audio setup is external. Panic is documented in its separate guide and awaits its own scene.

details.text:
The first loop leaves CH01 Note C3 (MIDI 60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2 channel masks. These still override matching pattern values. Before editing relative pattern notes, stop playback. Tap Channel (3,8), turn E1 to Channel tasks, select Masks with E2 and press K3. With no step held, select Note with E2 and turn E3 until the field reads X. X is unset, not zero; on steps without a step-specific note mask, the merged pattern note now plays. Keep Vel and Len at 80 and 1/2, or set them to X if pattern values should control them too.
K1+K2 with no step held clears channel step overrides but preserves defaults; it does not clear Note C3. To clear all masks on one step, hold that step and press K2. See Masks: Unset values and precedence.

details.text:
Before starting: Use channel 1 with pattern 1 assigned, active attacks at steps 1–4 and range 1–4. Set channel Masks Note to MIDI 60, Vel to 80 and Len to 1/2; clear existing step exceptions. Stop playback. [Creating a First Loop](#first-sound) gives the complete preparation route.

### Extend the range

1. Tap Channel (3,8).
2. Hold (1,4), tap (16,4), release.
3. Turn E1 to Channel tasks; select Clock with E2 and press K3.
4. Select Rate with E2; set /1 with E3 (sixteenth notes, the default).
5. Press K3 to apply while stopped.

The channel traverses16 steps before repeating.

### Move the attacks

1. Open Pattern Trig, pattern 1.
2. Remove steps 2,3,4.
3. Add steps 5,9,13; keep step 1.

Four attacks now sit on the four beats. The old attacks have been removed explicitly.

### Hear the longer phrase

1. Play two bars.
2. Stop.

C–C–C–C remains the pitch sequence; the space between attacks has increased.

Resulting project: P1 attacks 1/5/9/13; CH01 range 1–16; sixteenth-note rate; Note 60/Vel 80/Len1/2 unchanged.

The examples below extend this phrase. Set channel and step note masks shows how a step's own note beats the channel default. Save D major, then apply it shows how a scale slot can be edited and saved without changing what plays until you apply it. The last three examples walk through the whole workflow in order: Add a second pattern in D major merges two patterns on channel 1, Add a second channel with its own output gives channel 2 its own MIDI port, and Chain song slots an octave apart plays two song slots.

details.text:
Before starting: Use any stopped project containing a named arrangement. The worked reload check uses slot 1 with channel 1 muted and another channel audible. For another project, make a reversible visible change before loading and confirm the saved state returns.

### Save the arrangement

1. Tap K1 briefly to enter the norns system menu.
2. Open PARAMS → MOSAIC → Save project.
3. Press K3 to open text entry. Turn E2 left to DEL and press K3 three times to remove new. Turn E3 left to the character row; use E2 to select each character of Four notes and K3 to enter it, including the space. Turn E3 right to the bottom row, turn E2 right to OK, and press and release K3. K2 cancels text entry.

The named project stores the two-section arrangement.

### Prove the saved version

1. Return to Mosaic, select Song slot 1, then open Channel.
2. Hold K1, tap channel 1 at (1,1), release K1 to unmute it temporarily.
3. With playback stopped, open PARAMS → MOSAIC → Load project.
4. Select Four notes and confirm.

Slot 1 returns to bass alone; the temporary change is removed.

### Replay the restored sections

1. Select slot 1.
2. Play four section passes and stop.

The saved bass-only/full-phrase alternation is restored. Continue with merge, recording or modulation task guides without replacing this saved version.

Resulting project: Named project Four notes contains both sections and restores their exact playback. Transport stopped with no held notes.

details.text:
Four bars at 90 BPM.

Channel 1, Oilcan 1, velocity 38: in every bar MIDI 36 on steps 1 and 9, MIDI 38 on steps 4 and 12 and MIDI 37 on steps 5 and 13.

Channel 2, Polyperc 1, velocity 42: in every bar MIDI 48 on steps 1, 5 and 13 and MIDI 55 on step 9.

Channel 3, Doubledecker, velocity 26, three steps long, Chd1 3rd and Chd2 5th: in bars 1 to 3 the chord roots are MIDI 60 on step 1 and MIDI 62 on step 9 of the bar. In bar 4 they are MIDI 67 on step 49 and MIDI 60 on step 57.

Play the loop and listen for the chord at the start of bar 4: the drums and bass are unchanged, while the chords move from C and D to G and C.

features.musical_use: Build the rhythm, bass and chords as separate channels and play the loop after each one. Then change only the chord roots in bar 4 and listen to the harmony move over an unchanged groove.
features.prose:
Build a four-bar loop on three channels: Oilcan 1 plays drums on channel 1, Polyperc 1 plays a bass line on channel 2 and Doubledecker plays chords on channel 3. The drum and bass phrases repeat unchanged in every bar. Only the chord roots change, in bar 4, so you hear the harmony move while the groove stays put. Play "Rhythm, bass and a changing chord" under Listen to hear the finished result first.

Before you start:

1. Set 90 BPM in Song tasks → Tempo & feel (E3, then K3). Keep the default Rate /1 on every channel: one step is a sixteenth note, 16 steps are one bar and 64 steps are four bars.

2. Set the range of channels 1–3 to steps 1–64.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Snap note masks to scale to Off, so that MIDI 37 (C#1) in the drum channel is not snapped to C major.

How notes are entered in these recipes: open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). E2 chooses the value (Trig, Note, Vel, Len, Chd1–Chd4). With no step held, E3 sets the channel default, which every step uses unless it has its own value. Hold K1 and tap a step to add or remove a trig on it. Hold a step and turn E3 to give that step its own value. Hold a step and press K2 to remove its own values. For Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. For example, step 33 is (1,6) and step 61 is (13,7). These screens do not page. Pattern Note and Velocity use 16-step pages.

If Oilcan 1, Polyperc 1 or Doubledecker is missing from the Device picker, install and enable its `nb_oilcan`, `nb_polyperc` or `nb_doubledecker` mod in SYSTEM > MODS; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b).
Build the channels in order: Percussion Channel, Bass Channel, Chord Channel. Press Play after each one to hear the loop grow before you add the next channel.

Finish with a contrasting section: open the Song Editor, copy the song slot and mute one channel in the copy (see Song Composition). Numeric MIDI notes are used throughout, because Masks shows MIDI 36, 48 and 60 as C1, C2 and C3 while other controls label octaves differently. Each n.b. player is unique: Polyperc 1 cannot be assigned to another channel once it is assigned to the bass.

recipes.text:
Starting point: the three settings under Before you start are done (90 BPM, steps 1-64, Snap note masks to scale Off) and channel 1 is empty. The steps below build a six-hit drum bar and repeat it in all four bars.

1. Select channel 1 (1,1). Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Oilcan 1 and press K3 to assign it. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign Pattern 1 to channel 1.

2. Open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). With no step held, turn E2 to Note and turn E3 to MIDI 36 (C1). Turn E2 to Vel and set 38. Turn E2 to Len and set ½ step. Every trig you add now plays MIDI 36 at velocity 38 for half a step. In the default Oilcan kit MIDI 36, 37 and 38 trigger three different drum timbres.

3. In bar 1 (steps 1-16), hold K1 and tap steps 1, 4, 5, 9, 12 and 13. Six trigs light on the grid.

4. Turn E2 back to Note. Hold step 4 and turn E3 to MIDI 38 (D1), then release. Do the same for step 12. Hold step 5 and turn E3 to MIDI 37 (C#1), then release, and do the same for step 13. Steps 1 and 9 keep the default MIDI 36.

5. Listen: press Play and hear bar 1, then three silent bars because bars 2–4 are still empty. In bar 1, MIDI 36 falls on beats 1 and 3, MIDI 37 on beats 2 and 4, and each MIDI 38 hit sounds one step before a MIDI 37 hit. Press Stop.

6. Repeat steps 3 and 4 in each of the other three bars, using the full grid: steps 17–32 are row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. Masks and Pattern Trig do not page. Each pair below is a step number and its MIDI note:
Bar 2: 17/36, 20/38, 21/37, 25/36, 28/38, 29/37.
Bar 3: 33/36, 36/38, 37/37, 41/36, 44/38, 45/37.
Bar 4: 49/36, 52/38, 53/37, 57/36, 60/38, 61/37.

The channel now has 24 trigs in a repeating one-bar (four-beat) drum figure. Press Play and listen before you continue: the same bar repeats four times. Press Stop.
recipes.title: Percussion Channel

recipes.text:
Starting point: channel 1 plays the drums and channel 2 is empty. Masks work as in the percussion recipe: E2 chooses the value, E3 sets it, and holding a step gives that step its own value.

1. Select channel 2 (2,1). Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Polyperc 1 and press K3 to assign it. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 2 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (2,2) to assign Pattern 2 to channel 2.

2. Open Masks. With no step held, turn E2 to Note and set MIDI 48 (C2), turn E2 to Vel and set 42, and turn E2 to Len and set ½ step.

3. In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13.

4. Select Note with E2, hold step 9 and turn E3 to MIDI 55 (G2), then release. Steps 1, 5 and 13 keep the default MIDI 48.

5. Listen: press Play. In bar 1, the bass plays C2 on beats 1, 2 and 4 and G2 on beat 3 under the bar-1 drums; bars 2–4 remain silent until you enter them. Press Stop.

6. Repeat steps 3 and 4 in bars 2 to 4, adding 16 to each step number of bar 1. Each trig list is followed by the step that takes MIDI 55:
Bar 2: trigs on 17, 21, 25, 29; 25 is MIDI 55.
Bar 3: trigs on 33, 37, 41, 45; 41 is MIDI 55.
Bar 4: trigs on 49, 53, 57, 61; 57 is MIDI 55.

Listen for the pitch pattern C, C, G, C repeating once per bar under the drums.
recipes.title: Bass Channel

recipes.text:
Starting point: channels 1 and 2 play the drums and bass; channel 3 is empty. Use Doubledecker for the chord because it plays several notes at once. On Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. These screens do not page. Pattern Note and Velocity use 16-step pages. Hold K1 and tap to add or remove a trig; hold a step and turn E3 to give it its own value.

1. Select channel 3 (3,1). Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Doubledecker and press K3 to assign it. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 3 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (3,2) to assign Pattern 3 to channel 3.

2. Open Masks. With no step held, set Note to MIDI 60 (C3), Vel to 26 and Len to 3 steps. Select Chd1 and set 3rd; select Chd2 and set 5th. Every chord now plays the root plus the notes a third and a fifth above it in the scale.

3. In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1 and 9. Select Note, hold step 9 and turn E3 to MIDI 62 (D3), then release. Step 1 keeps the default MIDI 60. Press Play: in bar 1 the chord alternates C-E-G and D-F-A, two chords a bar, quietly above the bass; bars 2–4 remain silent until you enter them. Press Stop.

4. Bar 2: add trigs on steps 17 and 25.

5. Set step 25 to MIDI 62 as in step 3.

6. Bar 3: add trigs on steps 33 and 41.

7. Set step 41 to MIDI 62.

8. Bar 4: hold K1 and tap steps 49 and 57.

9. Hold step 49 and set Note to MIDI 67 (G3). Step 57 keeps the default MIDI 60.

10. Result check: listen to the whole four bars: press Play and wait for bar 4. The drums and bass repeat unchanged, but the chords move to G-B-D and then back to C-E-G. The chord intervals follow the C-major scale, so the 3rd above D is F and the 3rd above G is B. Press Stop.

details.text: The ghost-note comparison uses Oilcan 1. Every bar has four main attacks at velocity 90. Bars 3 and 4 each add one velocity-35 hit. The "Three sounds, one pocket" recording is an independent pattern at a constant velocity of 48. MIDI note mappings can differ on another instrument.
details.title: Comparison settings

features.musical_use: Add one quiet hit just before an accent and compare the bar with and without it. Use a ghost note to add movement to a drum pattern without changing the main hits.
features.prose:
Compare two ways of playing the same four-beat drum figure on Oilcan 1. Bars 1 and 2 contain only the main hits (MIDI 36 on steps 1 and 9, MIDI 37 on steps 5 and 13, all at velocity 90). Bars 3 and 4 add one quiet hit, MIDI 38 at velocity 35, on step 12 of the bar, just before the accent on step 13. This is a ghost note: a soft hit that adds movement without changing the main hits.

Settings: 90 BPM, Rate /1 (the default, one step is a sixteenth note), range 1–64 and length ½ step on all notes. Play "Adding a Ghost Note" under Listen to hear the target, then build it with the first recipe.

Two further recipes follow: an optional probability variation of the ghost notes, and a separate, denser drum pattern at velocity 48 (the "Three sounds, one pocket" recording) that does not use ghost notes.

recipes.text:
Starting point: an empty project with playback stopped and channel 1 selected. If Oilcan 1 is missing from the Device picker, install and enable `nb_oilcan` in SYSTEM > MODS; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b). The numbers 1–64 are step numbers across four bars: bar 1 is steps 1–16, bar 2 is 17–32, bar 3 is 33–48 and bar 4 is 49–64. For Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. These screens do not page.


Setup (steps 1 to 3 prepare the instrument; do them once).

1. Assign Oilcan 1 to channel 1 and set its range to steps 1–64 (see Channel Length). Leave Rate at /1.

2. Set 90 BPM: open Song tasks, choose Tempo & feel, turn E3 to 90 and press K3.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Snap note masks to scale to Off, then return to Mosaic. MIDI 37 (C#1) is not in C major and would otherwise be snapped to a scale note. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign pattern 1 to the channel.


Main hits (steps 4 to 7 build and audition the bar without ghost notes).

4. Add the main hits. Open Pattern Trig on pattern 1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 in each bar: bar 1 uses 1, 5, 9, 13; bar 2 uses 17, 21, 25, 29; bar 3 uses 33, 37, 41, 45; bar 4 uses 49, 53, 57, 61. Sixteen trigs are lit.

5. Open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). With no step held, select Note and set MIDI 36 (C1), select Vel and set 90, select Len and set ½. All sixteen hits now play MIDI 36 at velocity 90.

6. Select Note. Hold step 5 and turn E3 to MIDI 37 (C#1), then release. Do the same for steps 13, 21, 29, 37, 45, 53 and 61, so that the second and fourth beat of each bar play MIDI 37.

7. Press Play and listen to four bars of main hits only, then press Stop. You hear two timbres alternating on beats 1 to 4 of every bar.


Ghost notes (steps 8 to 10 add the quiet hit to bars 3 and 4).

8. Return to Pattern Trig and tap step 44 (step 12 of bar 3) and step 60 (step 12 of bar 4).

9. Open Masks and hold step 44. Select Note and turn E3 to MIDI 38 (D1), then select Vel and set 35, then release step 44. Repeat both edits on step 60: first Note 38, then Vel 35.

10. Press Play. Bars 1 and 2 are unchanged. In bars 3 and 4 you hear a quiet third timbre one step before each MIDI 37 accent. Press Stop.


Undo (step 11 returns to the main-only phrase).

11. Open Masks, hold step 44 or 60 and press K2 to remove the values you set, then remove its trig on Pattern Trig.
recipes.title: Make the recorded ghost-note comparison

recipes.text:
Starting point: Finish the ghost-note comparison above with ghost trigs on steps 44 and 60. This is an optional, player-run probability exercise, not a reconstruction of the recording. At probability 50, each ghost onset may play or be skipped on each pass, so evaluate the range of outcomes over several loops instead of expecting a fixed recording.

**Set a dependable main beat.** Select channel 1 and open Channel tasks → Trig params. Turn E2 to a slot, press K2, turn E3 to Trig Probability, press K3. With no step held, set the channel default to 100. Check: every main hit remains eligible on every pass.

**Check both boundaries.** On the full Trig Params grid, hold step 44 at (12,6), set its probability to 0, and release. Hold step 60 at (12,7), set it to 0 the same way. Play: neither ghost note sounds in bars 3 or 4; the main hits continue. Stop. Set both ghost steps to 100 and play again: both ghost notes play on every pass, matching the fixed comparison. Stop.

**Try the optional variation.** Set steps 44 and 60 to 50 and play several loops. The musical result to listen for is a quiet pickup that appears on some passes and leaves space on others, while the main hits stay present. Which ghost hit appears can differ each loop; no particular pass or captured result is promised.

Restore the fixed comparison by setting both steps to 100, or remove a lock by holding its step and pressing K2. For a captured 0/100 probability example, see Trig Probability, “Turn chance into explicit rests.”
recipes.title: Optional probability variation

recipes.text:
This is the "Three sounds, one pocket" recording. It is a different, denser four-bar drum pattern and does not use ghost notes. It teaches one idea: a third sound (MIDI 38) fills the gaps between the two accents. Every hit is at velocity 48, a constant quiet level chosen so you hear rhythm and timbre only, with no accent or quiet ghost hit. Starting point: the ghost-note comparison recipe's steps 1 to 3 (Oilcan 1 on channel 1, range 1–64, 90 BPM, Snap note masks to scale Off) and an empty channel.

The bar template, as step/MIDI note: 1/36, 4/38, 5/37, 7/38, 9/36, 12/38, 13/37 and 15/38.

Step:  1   4   5   7   9   12  13  15

Note:  36  38  37  38  36  38  37  38

1. Open Masks. With no step held, set Note to MIDI 36, Vel to 48 and Len to ½.

2. Enter the trigs. In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 13 and 15 to add eight trigs.

3. Edit the notes. Select Note and give steps 4, 7, 12 and 15 MIDI 38, and steps 5 and 13 MIDI 37, holding each step and turning E3. Steps 1 and 9 keep MIDI 36.

4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 in bars 2 to 4, adding 16 to each step number.

Play four bars. Listen for MIDI 36 on beats 1 and 3, MIDI 37 on beats 2 and 4, and the MIDI 38 hits filling the gaps between them. Unlike the ghost-note comparison, every hit has the same velocity, so nothing sounds accented or quiet. Listen to "Three sounds, one pocket" under Listen to compare.

details.text: Start at [Changing Harmony with Scale Slots](#tilting-harmony). Follow its Before you start instructions and recipes in order. This is an independent project; save your course piece before trying it.
details.title: Complete example

details.text: For the phrase and bass you already made, open [Change harmony without changing the rhythm](#harmony-design/course). The independent comparison below uses Doubledecker for the upper phrase and Polyperc 1 for the bass, with two bars per key. Its voice assignments and section lengths differ from the course.
details.title: Continue your course piece

details.text: This comparison uses relative pattern notes (scale degrees) with the Note masks left at X. A Note mask would replace the pattern note and fix the pitch, so no scale change could move it. Polyperc 1 is assigned once, to the bass. Numeric MIDI notes are used for expected results because the controls label octaves differently.
details.title: Pitch and output scope

features.musical_use: Change the applied scale slot to move a whole phrase and bass to a new key while keeping its rhythm. Use it to make a simple pattern sound like a chord progression.
features.prose:
Hear one pair of relative-note patterns in two keys. Doubledecker on channel 1 plays an upper phrase and Polyperc 1 on channel 2 plays a bass. For bars 1 and 2 the global scale is C major (scale slot 1); for bars 3 and 4 it is D major (scale slot 2). The patterns hold scale degrees, not fixed pitches, and the Note masks stay X (unset), so changing the applied scale moves every pitch while rhythm, velocity and length stay the same. Play "Changing Harmony with Scale Slots" under Listen to hear the target.

Settings: 90 BPM, Rate /1 (the default, one step is a sixteenth note) and a 16-step range that loops once per bar. The bass velocity is 60 and its notes last ½ step in this comparison. The "A bass with room above it" recording is a different example, in fixed notes in C major.

recipes.text:
Starting point: an empty project with playback stopped. If Doubledecker or Polyperc 1 is missing from the Device picker, install and enable its corresponding `nb_doubledecker` or `nb_polyperc` mod in SYSTEM > MODS; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b). Part 1 builds the upper phrase on channel 1, part 2 builds the bass on channel 2, part 3 prepares the second key and part 4 performs the change. In the note page, the column is the step and the row is the degree: y=7 is degree 0 (I), y=6 is degree 1 (II) and y=3 is degree 4 (V).

Part 1: upper phrase

1. Set 90 BPM (Song tasks, Tempo & feel, E3, K3). Leave Rate at /1.

2. Open the Scale editor (4,8). Slot 1 at (1,3) is the applied slot. Check Root C and Scale Major on the Scale screen; if you change either, press K3 to save it.

3. Assign Doubledecker to channel 1. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1 and tap pattern slot (1,2) to assign pattern 1 to the channel. Open Pattern Trig, select pattern 1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13.

4. Open Pattern Note (tap Pattern (5,8) until Note is shown) and set the degrees: tap (1,7), (5,7) and (9,7) for degree 0, and (13,6) for degree 1. Set the channel range to steps 1-16.

5. Open Masks. Leave Note at X. Set Vel to 80 and Len to ½. Hold step 13 and set Vel to 50, then release. The phrase ends with a softer last note. Checkpoint: press Play and listen. In C major the upper phrase is MIDI 60, 60, 60, 62. Press Stop before building the bass channel.

Part 2: bass

6. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 2 and select pattern 2 for the channel. On pattern 2, tap steps 1 and 9 on Pattern Trig, then on Pattern Note tap (1,7) for degree 0 and (9,3) for degree 4. Set the range to steps 1-16 and the channel octave to -1 with (9,8).

7. Open Masks with channel 2 selected, leave Note at X, set Vel to 60 and Len ½. Checkpoint: press Play. The bass adds MIDI 48 on beat 1 and MIDI 55 on beat 3 under the upper phrase. Press Stop before preparing slot 2.

Part 3: prepare the second key

8. While stopped, open the Scale editor. Hold K1 and press slot 2 at (2,3) to select it for editing without applying it. On the Scale screen set Root to D and Scale to Major with E2 and E3, and press K3 to save the slot. Slot 1 stays applied, so playback is still C major.

Part 4: perform the change (choose one)

9a. Stopped: play two bars in C major and stop. Short-press slot 2 at (2,3) to apply D major and play two more bars.

9b. Live: while playing, short-press slot 2 at (2,3) at the end of bar 2.

Result check: in D major the upper phrase becomes MIDI 62, 62, 62, 64 and the bass becomes MIDI 50 and 57: the same rhythm moved up a whole tone. Short-press slot 1 at (1,3) to restore C major.
recipes.title: Make the relative-note scale comparison

recipes.text:
Goal and contrast: this example uses fixed Note masks, so its pitches do not move when the scale changes. It is the counterpart of the scale-slot comparison above, where the notes are relative degrees that move with the scale, and it shows how to layer quiet chords above a bass. It is the "A bass with room above it" recording and stays in C major.

Starting point: an empty project, 90 BPM, Rate /1, Snap note masks to scale at its default, and channels 1 and 2 with their range set to steps 1-16 (hold step 1 and tap step 16 on the channel page).

1. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1. Open Masks and set Note to MIDI 48, Vel to 48 and Len to ½.

2. Hold K1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. Hold step 9 and set Note to MIDI 55.

3. Assign Doubledecker to channel 2. Open Masks and set Note to MIDI 60, Vel to 32 and Len to 3 steps. Set Chd1 to 3rd and Chd2 to 5th.

4. Hold K1 and tap steps 1 and 9, then hold step 9 and set Note to MIDI 62.

5. Result check: press Play. The bass plays C2, C2, G2, C2 on beats 1 to 4; the chords sound C-E-G on beat 1 and D-F-A on beat 3. Chord velocity 32 is quieter than bass velocity 48. If the chord is missing, verify channel 2 uses a polyphonic device and Chd1=3rd and Chd2=5th.

details.text: Start at [Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops](#loops-that-meet). Follow its Before you start instructions and recipes in order. This is an independent project; save your course piece before trying it.
details.title: Complete example

details.text: The four-against-three lesson below uses ranges 1–4 and 1–3. Its screen/grid demonstration and MIDI output show that small example. The separate recording Sixteen steps against twelve uses longer phrases; open its named extension recipe for the matching setup. Both illustrate loops meeting, but their note sequences and lengths differ.
details.title: Example Scope

features.musical_use: Give two channels different lengths so a short and a long phrase drift apart and realign. Use it for evolving rhythmic patterns from simple loops, and use song reset options when each section should restart together.
features.prose:
Run two channels at the same clock rate with different lengths: channel 1 loops a four-step phrase and channel 2 loops a three-step phrase. Both channels start together on step 1, drift apart, and meet again after 12 steps, the smallest number that both 4 and 3 divide into. At the default Rate /1 and 90 BPM, 12 steps last two seconds. Playback is continuous: each channel simply starts its own loop again when it reaches the end of its range.

1. On channel 1, assign a pattern with active steps 1–4. Using the default C-major scale, set relative pattern notes 0, 1, 2 and 3, which produce MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Set the velocities to 127, 117, 107 and 97 and each note length to one step. Set the range to steps 1–4 (hold step 1, tap step 4, release step 1).

2. On channel 2, assign the same pattern and set the range to steps 1–3.

3. Open channel 2 Masks. With no step held, set the channel defaults to Note MIDI 79, Vel 40 and Len ½.

4. Hold step 2 and set Note MIDI 81, Vel 60 and Len 1¼. Release the step. Channel 2 now repeats MIDI 79, 81, 79, independent of the four notes on channel 1.

5. Start playback. Both channels begin together. Compare their first steps again after 12 steps (about two seconds).

6. Stop playback before changing the arrangement.

Use separate MIDI routes for the two instruments. For internal sound, assign different supported players, for example Polyperc 1 for channel 1 and Doubledecker for channel 2. Song transitions and reset options can restart channels earlier than 12 steps; the second recipe shows how.

recipes.text:
Starting point: the numbered setup in Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops is complete and playback is stopped. Both channels run at the same rate. At 90 BPM and Rate /1 one step is a sixth of a second, so you can count 12 steps in two seconds.

1. Press Play and count steps. Channel 1 plays MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 and then repeats, so it completes three phrases in 12 steps. Channel 2 plays MIDI 79, 81, 79 and repeats, so it completes four phrases in the same 12 steps.

2. Listen at step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together. This same pitch pair also occurs at step 9, so it is not unique. Count phrase starts: after step 1, the two loops next realign at step 13. On step 4, channel 1 plays MIDI 65 while channel 2 starts a new phrase with MIDI 79.

3. Listen at step 13, two seconds after step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together again, and the pattern repeats every 12 steps. Press Stop when you have heard the alignment.

4. Optional extra check, unrelated to the alignment: with both channels playing, try a reversed range on channel 1. Hold step 4 as the start, press step 2 as the end and release both. The reversed range is rejected with a message, the ranges stay 1–4 and 1–3, and neither phrase changes timing.
recipes.title: Comparing the Loop Alignment

recipes.text:
Starting point: the two looping channels above (channel 1 range 1–4, channel 2 range 1–3), with Song slot 1 holding them and playback stopped. Song mode is On by default, so the slots play in turn, and Reset on song seq change (PARAMS > MOSAIC) is On by default while Reset on pattern repeat is Off. This comparison hears how the first option changes both channels at a slot boundary.

1. Set slot 1 to ten steps before copying it. Open the Song Editor and tap slot 1 at (1,1). On the length fader, tap (2,7) to jump to 1, then tap (8,7) nine times to reach 10. This length belongs to the selected slot and applies to both its channels. Ten is not a multiple of 4 or 3, so each channel is part-way through its loop when the slot ends.

2. Copy the ten-step slot. Hold slot 1 at (1,1), tap slot 2 at (2,1), then release slot 1. Slot 2 inherits slot 1's patterns and length 10. Leave slot 3 empty and select slot 1 again: the two ten-step sections will play in turn.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and check that Reset on song seq change reads On. Play both slots. At the start of slot 2 both channels restart from step 1: channel 1 plays MIDI 60 and channel 2 plays MIDI 79. The 4-against-3 pattern starts again from the beginning in every slot. Press Stop.

4. Set Reset on song seq change to Off and play both slots again. Now neither channel restarts: at the start of slot 2 channel 1 continues with MIDI 64, the third note of its phrase (10 steps is two phrases and two steps), and channel 2 continues with MIDI 81, the second note of its phrase (10 steps is three phrases and one step). The two channels no longer meet at the slot boundary. Press Stop.

5. Set Reset on song seq change back to On to restore the default.

Use Off when you want the 12-step relationship to carry across slots without a restart; use On when each slot should begin with both loops on their first step.
recipes.title: Comparing Song Boundary Resets

recipes.text:
Starting point: two channels with audible notes. Give each channel a voice (for example Oilcan 1 on channel 1 and Polyperc 1 on channel 2, or any two MIDI outputs) and set Note, Vel and Len on each channel's Masks page as in Make your first loop (a channel needs at least one audible note to be heard).

Enter the two patterns. Tap Pattern (5,8) for the Trig view. In pattern 1 tap steps (1,4), (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4): a drum pattern with trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. In pattern 2 tap steps (1,4), (3,4) and (4,4): a short figure with trigs on steps 1, 3 and 4.

1. Channel 1: tap (1,1) and assign pattern 1 at (1,2). Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)), tap step 16 ((16,4)), then release step 1. Steps 1-16 on row 4 are now brighter.

2. Channel 2: tap (2,1) and assign pattern 2 at (2,2). Hold step 1, tap step 5 ((5,4)), then release step 1. On this channel only steps 1-5 are brighter.

3. Tap Play at (1,8). The drum channel repeats every 16 steps (four hits per bar) and the figure repeats every 5 steps, so its three notes slide across the drum hits. Listen for the figure landing on a different drum beat each bar.

4. Keep listening until the start of drum bar 6. After 80 steps (five drum bars, sixteen figure passes) both channels start together again. 80 is the first step count that both 16 and 5 divide. Tap Play again to stop.

If the song moves to another song pattern, channels are reset together while Reset at Song Sequence Change (on by default) is enabled, so the 80-step cycle only completes while the same song pattern keeps playing. Use the Options page to change how channels of different length behave. The captured example [Play sixteen steps against five](#loops-that-meet/loops-sixteen-against-five) builds this setup and plays the 80 steps until both channels start together again. The captured example "Keep a valid range when a gesture is reversed" shows the range gesture and what happens when the end comes before the start.
recipes.title: Run two channels at different lengths

recipes.text:
Start from an empty independent project at 90 BPM and Rate /1, with Song mode off so the channel loops run continuously. This is the separate Sixteen steps against twelve recording.

1. Assign Oilcan 1 to channel 1 and set its range to steps 1–16. In Masks, set channel Vel 80 and Len 1/2. Add trigs on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15. Set their Note masks to MIDI 36, 37, 36, 37 and 38 respectively.
2. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 2 and set its range to steps 1–12. In Masks, set channel Vel 60 and Len 1/2. Add trigs on steps 1, 4, 7 and 10. Set their Note masks to MIDI 48, 55, 52 and 55 respectively. Keep Snap note masks to scale Off so the drum note numbers stay unchanged.
3. Press Play. The loops meet every forty-eight steps: listen for the bass phrase landing differently against the drums in bars 2 and 3, then both returning to their first step at the beginning of bar 4.
4. Stop after four bars to match the recording. The bass ends four steps into its next twelve-step loop. This setup has different notes, sounds and loop lengths from the four-against-three lesson; keep the projects separate.
recipes.title: Listening extension: sixteen steps against twelve

learning_path.goal: Learn what a pattern, a channel and a song slot each do, and how this manual names grid buttons and norns controls, before you change anything.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Nothing in the project has changed. You can find a grid button from its (column,row) coordinates, tell the norns keys K1-K3 from the encoders E1-E3, and say what a pattern, a channel and a song slot do.
learning_path.prerequisite: Mosaic is running on norns with a 128 grid connected. Start a new project (PARAMS > MOSAIC > + New) so the course begins from an empty project. Have a MIDI instrument ready for chapter 2, or install and enable `nb_polyperc` before chapter 2 if you plan to use Polyperc 1 (see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b)).
learning_path.recovery: If a tap opens the wrong page, tap Channel (3,8) to return to the channel page. If the grid does not respond, check the grid connection in the norns menu. If playback later makes no sound, open [No Sound](#no-sound).

stages.action:
Read these three ideas first. Nothing changes until the last line.
1. A pattern holds a rhythm of trigs (steps that play a note) and relative notes. You write patterns on the Pattern page.
2. A channel plays patterns through one sound: a MIDI instrument or a norns voice. Its masks are values that override pitch, velocity and length, for the whole channel or for single steps.
3. A song slot stores one section of the song. You arrange slots in chapter 9.
Then do one thing: tap Channel (3,8) on the grid to open channel 1.
stages.goal: Know what a pattern, a channel and a song slot are for before you edit any of them.
stages.result: The norns screen reads NOTE MASKS with CH01 in the title row. Its eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4) all show X, which means no value is set: the new channel has no pattern, pitch or sound yet. On the grid, (1,1) is lit because channel 1 is the channel you edit, and (3,8) is lit because you are on the Channel page. In chapter 3 you give channel 1 a pattern and a pitch.

On the grid, (1,1) is lit because channel 1 is the channel you edit, and (3,8) is lit because you are on the Channel page. In chapter 3 you give channel 1 a pattern and a pitch.

stages.title: Learn the three objects

stages.action:
1. A grid position is written (column,row). Columns count from 1 at the left to 16 at the right; rows count from 1 at the top to 8 at the bottom. (3,8) is column 3 on the bottom row.
2. The bottom-left buttons open the main pages: Play (1,8), Record (2,8), Channel (3,8), Scale (4,8), Pattern (5,8) and Song (6,8). Row 1 selects the channel on the channel page, the pattern on the Pattern page and the song slot on the Song page.
3. On the norns, K1-K3 are the three keys and E1-E3 the three encoders, numbered as printed on the norns. "Tap" means a short press. "Hold K1" means keep K1 down while you act: it is the shift key.
4. Tap Pattern (5,8) on the grid to try a button. Chapter 2 starts by tapping Channel (3,8), so you can leave the Pattern page that way.

2. Turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens. This list holds everything you can do with the channel: Masks, Trig params, Output, Clock, Merge modes, Merge Shape, Harmony, Device and History.
3. Turn E2 until Device is highlighted.

stages.title: Open the Device page

stages.action:
1. Turn E3 one detent to choose a Device. The first entry after None is CC Device, a generic MIDI device that suits any MIDI instrument. If your instrument has its own entry, choose that instead. With no external instrument, choose Polyperc 1 only if `nb_polyperc` is installed and enabled; see [Norns Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b) for setup.
2. The MIDI channel and MIDI port rows now appear. CC Device reads CC1 and OUT 1, so notes leave on port 1, MIDI channel 1. If your instrument listens elsewhere, turn E2 to a row and E3 to the value it needs. A device entry that fixes a value does not let you change it, and Polyperc 1 needs neither row.
3. Press K3 to apply. Until K3 the page only shows a draft and the channel keeps its old routing; K2 cancels the draft.

build_steps: Start with slot 1 at length 16 and the four block chords. Leave Strum and Arpeggio locks unset. Check: all three notes of each chord start together.

Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and set slot 2 length to 32. In Trig params assign Chord Note Strum to slot 1, Chord Spread to slot 2 and Chord Accel Mod to slot 3. On steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 lock Strum to 1, Spread to 1 and Acceleration to -1. Check: the roots sound first, then the 3rds, then the 5ths; the gaps get shorter.

Copy slot 2 to slot 3 and set slot 3 length to 16. Assign Chord Note Arpeggio to slot 4 and lock Arpeggio 1/2 on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. Arpeggio takes precedence over Strum in this slot. Check: each chord becomes the root followed by the 3rd, with the 5th absent.
Play all three slots, then Stop and select slot 1 to restore block chords. The bar map is: bar 1 block chords; bars 2-3 speeding strum; bar 4 two-note arpeggio.

lesson_relations.explanation: This recipe follows the recording’s setup in a separate project, apart from the course project.

listen_for: Bar 1 has block chords; bars 2–3 open into a speeding strum; bar 4 changes to a sparse two-note arpeggio.
harmony-strum-arp.purpose: The four chord roots and progression stay fixed. Chord Strum spreads chord notes over time; Spread controls their spacing, and Acceleration changes that spacing as the strum goes on. Chord Arpeggio plays the selected chord notes in sequence. Only these per-slot behaviors change.
restore_steps: Select slot 1 to restore block chords, then stop. Keep the recipe in its own project while the course project remains open.
harmony-strum-arp.starting_point: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major. Assign Doubledecker to channel 1 and set range 1-16. Set Note MIDI 60, Vel 80, Len 2 steps, Chd1=3rd and Chd2=5th; add trigs at 1, 5, 9 and 13 with roots MIDI 60, 57, 65 and 67.
harmony-strum-arp.title: Block chords, strummed, then arpeggiated

build_steps: Channel 1 bass, bars 1-2: in Masks set default Note MIDI 48, Vel 70 and Len 1/2. Add trigs at steps 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25 and 29. Set steps 9 and 25 to MIDI 43; the other bass trigs stay MIDI 48. Check: each bar has four bass notes.
Channel 1 bass, bars 3-4: add trigs at steps 33, 37, 41, 45, 49, 53, 57 and 61. Set steps 41 and 57 to MIDI 43; the others stay MIDI 48. Check: the four-bar bass phrase now has all sixteen notes.

Channel 2 chords, bars 1-2: in Masks set default Note MIDI 60, Vel 45 and Len 3 steps; set Chd1=3rd and Chd2=5th. Add trigs at 1, 9, 17 and 25; keep each root at MIDI 60. Check: two C-major chord masks sound per bar.
Channel 2 chords, bars 3-4: add trigs at 33, 41, 49 and 57, all with root MIDI 60. Check: the chord layer repeats on beats 1 and 3 over the bass.
Play four bars. Hold K1 and tap channel 2 selector (2,1) to mute the chords; tap it again with K1 held to restore them. Stop playback.

restore_steps: Unmute channel 2 and stop. Keep this four-bar extension in its separate project; the course Masks phrases use different notes.
masks-small-hours.starting_point: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major. Set channel 1 to Polyperc 1 and channel 2 to Doubledecker; set both ranges and Song slot 1 length to 64 steps. The event positions below come from the Masks feature’s frozen audio track definition.

build_steps: Checkpoint 1 — Pattern 1. In Pattern Trig tap steps 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 13. In Pattern Note set degrees 0, 2, 4, 2, 0 and 4 on those steps. Check the six notes on pattern 1 before you build pattern 2.

Checkpoint 2 — Pattern 2. In Pattern Trig tap steps 1, 5, 9, 11, 13 and 15. In Pattern Note set degrees 2, 6, 3, 3, 0 and 5. On the Note grid, row 7 is degree 0 and each row above is one degree higher. Check that both patterns overlap on 1, 5, 9 and 13, while 3, 7, 11 and 15 belong to only one pattern.

Before merging, verify the overlap: both patterns trigger on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. Only one pattern triggers on steps 3, 7, 11 and 15. The comparison changes the shared-step pitches; the single-pattern pitches stay put.

On channel 1 Masks leave Note and Trig at X so the patterns supply pitches and triggers. Set Vel to 80 and Len to half a step. The recorded setup uses these channel masks; it does not leave Vel and Len unset.

Checkpoint 3 — common channel and Average. Open Channel tasks > Merge modes. Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until ALL reads. Select Note mode with E2 and turn E3 until AVERAGE reads; these controls apply immediately. Set Song slot 1 length to 32. Check that Strategy reads ALL and Note mode reads AVERAGE before copying the slot.

Checkpoint 4 — compare Higher. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and select slot 2; keep its length 32. In Merge modes select Note mode with E2 and turn E3 to UP (the Higher comparison). Play both slots, then stop and select slot 1 to restore Average.

lesson_relations.explanation: This recipe follows the recording’s setup in a separate project, apart from the course project.
lesson_relations.recipe_title: Build the recording: Average, then Higher

lesson_relations.explanation: The linked lesson shows Lock merged to pent. Off, the setup used here to isolate the Note Merge modes.

listen_for: Shared steps 1, 5, 9 and 13: MIDI 62, 69, 64 and 64 under Average; MIDI 65, 72, 69 and 71 under Higher.
Single-pattern steps 3, 7, 11 and 15 do not change: MIDI 64, 64, 65 and 69.
note-merge-modes.purpose: When both patterns trigger on the same step, Note merge chooses the pitch they produce together. Average uses the midpoint of the two pattern pitches; Higher raises that midpoint using the gap between the inputs. Trig merge All combines the triggers from both patterns. Lock merged to pent. is a separate pitch restriction, kept Off here so the comparison isolates the two Note modes.
restore_steps: Select slot 1 for Average. Keep Lock merged to pent. Off and Trig Merge All for this recorded comparison; return to the separate course project when finished.
note-merge-modes.starting_point: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1, scale C major, playback stopped. Assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1, range 1-16. Turn Lock merged to pent. Off before comparing, then assign patterns 1 and 2 to channel 1.
note-merge-modes.title: Average, then Higher

build_steps: Open Masks. With no step held, set Note to MIDI 36, Vel to 48 and Len to ½ step.
In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 13 and 15 to add the eight trigs.
Select Note. Hold steps 4, 7, 12 and 15 in turn and set each to MIDI 38; set steps 5 and 13 to MIDI 37. Steps 1 and 9 keep MIDI 36.
Repeat those positions in bars 2–4, adding 16, 32 and 48 to each step in the bar template.
Press Play for four bars, then Stop. To hear the stated contrast, clear the trigs on the four MIDI 38 positions in each bar; Play again, then re-add those trigs to restore the full pattern.

build_steps: Slot 1 is two bars (32 steps) with no parameter locks. Keep the eight-note MIDI line unchanged; this is the straight comparison.
Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and keep its length at 32 steps, covering bars 3–4. Open Channel tasks > Trig params and assign Decay to slot 1.

In slot 2, hold step 1 and replay the captured +200-detent E3 gesture, then release the step. Repeat the same +200-detent gesture on step 9 and release it. Check: steps 1 and 9 are the longer-tail group.
Hold step 5 and replay the captured +40-detent E3 gesture, then release the step. Repeat on step 13 and release it. Check: steps 5 and 13 are the shorter-tail group; the note pattern stays fixed.
Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1 to restore the no-lock line. The +200 and +40 turns adjust Decay relative to its current setting; the absolute value shown depends on your device.
Play slots 1 and 2, then Stop and select slot 1 to restore the no-lock line. The note pattern remains the same throughout.

lesson_relations.explanation: The Locks recipe replays the +200/+40-detent comparison from this recording, then offers a separate endpoint-practice contrast. The recording does not show absolute Decay values; use the values displayed by your device for the separate practice.
lesson_relations.recipe_title: Practice longer and shorter Decay envelopes

limits: The retained trace records E3 event 126 followed by +200 and +40 detents while steps are held. It does not record the displayed Decay values, so those raw input counts do not establish the recording’s exact Decay settings. The endpoint recipe is a contextual comparison, not a reconstruction of those unseen values.
listen_for: From bar 3, the on-beat plucks ring longer than the notes between them; the line returns to an even sound at the end.
param-lock-comparison.purpose: A parameter lock sets a device parameter for one trig only. A Decay lock changes how long that note's sound fades; it does not change the note pattern. In this example, longer Decay locks are on steps 1 and 9; shorter Decay locks are on steps 5 and 13.
restore_steps: Select slot 1 to restore the unmodified line. Stop and return to the separate course project when finished.

build_steps: Set channel 1 range to steps 1-16. In Masks set Note MIDI 36, Vel 80 and Len 1/2; add trigs at 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15. Set step 5 to MIDI 37, step 13 to MIDI 37 and step 15 to MIDI 38.

In Song Editor, set slot 1 length to 16 steps and mute channel 2 with K1 plus its selector (2,1).

build_steps: On channel 1 Masks, set Note MIDI 36, Vel 80 and Len ½. Add trigs at 1,2,5,6,9,10,13,14. Set steps 2,6,10,14 to MIDI 37 and steps 5,13 to MIDI 38; steps 1 and 9 stay MIDI 36.
On channel 2 Masks, set Note MIDI 48, Vel 60 and Len ½. Add trigs at steps 1,4,9,12; set steps 4 and 12 to MIDI 55 and step 9 to MIDI 52.
In Song Editor, set slot 1 length to 32 steps. Copy slot 1 to slot 2, leaving slot 2 length 32.
With slot2 selected, open Clock for each channel. Select Swing type with E2, chooseSwing with E3 and press K3. Select Swing with E2, set 25 with E3 and press K3. Leave slot 1 straight.
Play the two slots in order, then Stop and select slot 1 to restore the straight version.

build_steps: Before: build slot 1 at length 32 with Harmony Mode Off. It plays C, A minor, F and G in root position on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 of each bar. Play twice to hear the written voicing.

After: copy slot 1 to slot 2 and select slot 2; keep length 32. Open Channel tasks > Harmony. Select Mode with E2, choose REVOICE with E3 and press K3. Select Register with E2 and press K3; select Bass Mode with E2, choose ROOT with E3 and apply as the page indicates.

Compare bars 1-2 with bars 3-4: the same four chords, notes and rhythm return, but some notes move to other octaves and each chord root is lowest. Play both slots, then Stop and select slot 1 to restore Harmony Off.

voice-leading-revoice.purpose: Harmony Off keeps each chord in its written root-position voicing. Revoice moves those same chord notes to different octaves while preserving their pitch classes, note count and rhythm; ROOT keeps each chord root lowest.
restore_steps: Select slot 1 to restore Harmony Off, then stop and return to the separate course project.

steps.caption: In a new empty project with playback stopped and Record off, tap Pattern (5,8), then tap the third algorithm button (14,2). The five algorithm buttons on row 2 are, from the left: Drum (12,2), a library of classic bass, snare and hi-hat patterns; Tresillo (13,2), a 3-3-2 grouping; Euclidean (14,2), trigs spread as evenly as a mathematical rule allows; Numeric (15,2), patterns from Noise Engineering's Numeric Repetitor; and Rhythm Doctor (16,2). The Trig Algorithm screen marks Euclidean as SELECTED and the fader on grid row 2 lights its third position.
steps.title: Choose Euclidean

steps.caption: Turn E2 left. The screen passes Tresillo and stops on Drum, the first algorithm (a further turn stays on Drum). Drum shows no SELECTED mark and the third fader position stays lit: turning E2 only browses. Euclidean is still the algorithm in use until you press K3.
steps.title: Browse without applying

steps.caption: Press K3. Drum now reads SELECTED and the fader lights its first position. Drum draws on classic drum patterns, so it suits a kick, snare or hi-hat lane, where Euclidean suits an even pulse.
steps.title: Apply Drum

steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8). The Paint Preview screen opens on Algorithm Drum with Shift 0, but no step flashes on the pattern grid: at its default settings Drum previews no steps. Prime previews whichever algorithm is selected.
steps.title: Prime with Drum selected

steps.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8). The preview closes and nothing was painted.
steps.title: Cancel the empty preview

steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Pattern tasks, turn E2 to Algorithm and press K3. The Trig Algorithm screen returns (a Painting cancelled tip may still show) and Drum is still SELECTED.
steps.title: Return to the algorithm list

steps.caption: Turn E2 two detents right, past Tresillo. Euclidean is highlighted but carries no SELECTED mark yet, and the fader still shows Drum.
steps.title: Browse back to Euclidean

steps.caption: Press K3. Euclidean reads SELECTED and the fader lights its third position again.
steps.title: Apply Euclidean

steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8) again. Now every step on the pattern grid flashes and Paint Preview reads 64 trigs: at the default settings Euclidean fills all 64 steps, where Drum previewed none. Prime always previews the algorithm that is selected, so changing the algorithm changes what Prime shows.
steps.title: Prime now previews Euclidean

steps.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8) to close the Euclidean preview and tap Tresillo (13,2), the second algorithm button. Like Drum, Tresillo previews nothing until you choose a pattern: tap drum bank 1 at (12,3), then tap both ends of the first fader on row 2, (2,2) and (10,2), and of the second fader on row 3, (2,3) and (10,3). Tap Prime (16,8). The algorithm fader lights its second position and Paint Preview reads Algorithm Tresillo with 8 trigs. The flashing steps are spaced 9, 9 and 6 steps apart, over and over: the 3-3-2 grouping, scaled up. Nothing is painted yet.
steps.title: Prime Tresillo for a 3-3-2 preview

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Its Device page is open, so the header reads CH01, and Device shows CC Device, Mosaic's built-in generic MIDI device. Channel 2 is not set up yet. Both channels run at the default clock Rate /1 (one step per sixteenth note).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Device page stays open but now reads CH02 and Device shows None: channel 2 has no output yet, and setting up channel 1 did not change it. The channel buttons choose which channel the screen edits.
steps.title: An unused channel has no output

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1). The header returns to CH01 and Device shows CC Device again: each channel keeps its own device.
steps.title: Return to channel 1

steps.caption: Device was the first of a channel's own settings; Rate is the second. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Clock and press K3. The Clock page for CH01 shows Rate /1, the default: one step per sixteenth note. Rate divides the clock, so /2 will run half as fast and make each step twice as long.
steps.title: Open the Clock page

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Clock page stays open and now reads CH02, with its own Rate /1.
steps.title: Select channel 2

steps.caption: Turn E3 down two detents to Rate /2 and press K3 to apply. Channel 2 now runs at half the speed of channel 1: each of its steps lasts two sixteenth notes.
steps.title: Give channel 2 a different rate

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1). Its Clock page still reads Rate /1: changing channel 2's rate left channel 1 alone.
steps.title: Channel 1 keeps its rate

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1) again. Its Clock page reads Rate /2. Each channel remembers its own settings, so channels can run at different speeds against one tempo.
steps.title: Channel 2 remembers its rate

steps.caption: Open the Device page for channel 2, give it its own MIDI output, give it pattern 1 with the range steps 1-4 and open its Clock page again. Select channel 1 and press Play. Channel 1 plays one note every sixteenth note; channel 2 plays one note every two sixteenth notes, so its notes are twice as far apart. Look at the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", where the second port's notes arrive at half the pace of the first. Press Play again to stop.
steps.title: Hear channel 2 at half speed

channel-routing-visible-scope.title: Each channel keeps its own device and rate

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8): the Masks page opens for CH01. Turn E1 one detent. From any page, E1 opens Channel tasks, with the page you came from highlighted, here Masks. The nine tasks, top to bottom, are 1 Masks, 2 Trig params, 3 Output, 4 Clock, 5 Merge modes, 6 Merge Shape, 7 Harmony, 8 Device and 9 History.
steps.title: Open tasks

steps.caption: With the list open, E1 and E2 both scroll it, one row per detent. Turn E1 two detents to row 3, Output, then turn E2 four detents: Clock, Merge modes, Merge Shape, and Harmony, row 7, is highlighted.
steps.title: Scroll down to Harmony

steps.caption: Turn E2 four detents back up the list to Output (row 3), then turn E1 four detents the same way. The highlight stops on Masks, row 1, and the list does not wrap.
steps.title: Scroll back up to Masks

steps.caption: Turn E2 one detent down to Trig params (row 2) and press K3. The Trig params screen opens for CH01.
steps.title: Open Trig params

steps.caption: Turn E1 one detent. Channel tasks reopens with Trig params highlighted, the page you came from, so E1 always brings you back to the task list at your current page.
steps.title: Return to the list with E1

steps.caption: Press K3 to open Trig params again. The header reads TRIG PARAMS CH01.
steps.title: Open Trig params again

steps.caption: Turn E1 to reopen Channel tasks, then turn E2 down to row 9. History, the last row, is highlighted and its value reads OPEN >.
steps.title: Scroll to History (row 9)

steps.caption: Press K3. The History screen opens. Every task in the list opens its own screen this way.
steps.title: Open History

steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Channel tasks from History, scroll up to row 4, Clock, and press K3. The Clock screen opens for channel 1.
steps.title: Open Clock (row 4)

steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Channel tasks again, then turn E2 to row 8. Device is highlighted and its value reads OPEN >.
steps.title: Scroll to Device (row 8)

steps.caption: Press K3. The Device screen opens for channel 1, where its output is chosen.
steps.title: Open Device

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Only Chd1 (E, 64) and Chd4 (C, 72) are set, so Chd2 and Chd3 are empty slots; the output is polyphonic. Chord Note Strum is 1/2, Chord Pattern is <- (reverse: slot 4, 3, 2, 1, then the root), Mute Chord Root is assigned and left at X, and Chord Velocity Mod is +10. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Spread; Spread and Chord Accel Mod are not assigned yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/4. Each gap is now 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4 step. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Accel Mod.
steps.title: Set a quarter-step Spread

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Accel Mod and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent up to +1: each gap is a quarter step (Spread x 1) longer than the one before. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The gaps are 3/4, 1, 1 1/4 and 1 1/2 steps, so slot 4 (C4, 72) sounds at once, empty slots 3 and 2 pass in silence at 3/4 and 1 3/4 steps, slot 1 (E3, 64) sounds at 3 steps and the root C3 (60) at 4 1/2 steps. Look at the MIDI strip "MIDI sent in this step": the three notes arrive further and further apart.
steps.title: A positive Accel makes each gap longer

chord-acceleration-slowing.title: Slow the strum down with Accel +1

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Only Chd1 (E, 64) and Chd4 (C, 72) are set, so Chd2 and Chd3 are empty slots; the output is polyphonic. Chord Note Strum is 1/2, Chord Pattern is <- (reverse: slot 4, 3, 2, 1, then the root), Mute Chord Root is assigned and left at X, and Chord Velocity Mod is +10. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Spread; Spread and Chord Accel Mod are not assigned yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/4. Each gap is now 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4 step. Acceleration works on Spread, so with Spread at zero it would do nothing. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Accel Mod.
steps.title: Set a quarter-step Spread

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Accel Mod and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent down to -1: each gap is a quarter step (Spread x 1) shorter than the one before. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The gaps are 3/4, 1/2 and 1/4 step, and the gap after that would be 0, so scheduling stops. Slot 4 (C4, 72) sounds at once, empty slots 3 and 2 pass in silence at 3/4 and 1 1/4 steps, and slot 1 (E3, 64) sounds 1 1/2 steps after the trigger. The MIDI strip lists only those two notes; the root C3 (60) never sounds.
steps.title: A faster reverse strum can end early

chord-acceleration-termination.title: Stop when the next gap closes

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Note Arpeggio. No slot is assigned yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Arpeggio to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/2. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Pattern.
steps.title: Set a half-step Arpeggio

steps.caption: An arpeggio gives every note its own gate: each note lasts one division, here half a step, from its own start. A strummed note is held to the end of the step. Assign Chord Pattern and turn E3 one detent to -> (forward); Assign Mute Chord Root and leave it at X so the root still sounds; then assign Chord Velocity Mod and turn E3 to +10 (E2 moves to the next slot, K2 opens the list, E3 browses, K3 assigns, K2 returns). Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip the five voices start half a step apart: C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72).
steps.title: Hear a gate on every voice

chord-arpeggio-timed-gates.title: Give every arp voice its own gate

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Pattern. Chord Note Strum is already assigned and set to 1/2, half a step.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Pattern and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent to -> (forward). Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Mute Chord Root.
steps.title: Choose forward order

steps.caption: Assign Mute Chord Root and leave it at X so the root still sounds; then assign Chord Velocity Mod and turn E3 to +10 (E2 moves to the next slot, K2 opens the list, E3 browses, K3 assigns, K2 returns). Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The five slots are the root and Chd1 to Chd4. The MIDI strip lists them in that order, half a step apart, root first: C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72).
steps.title: Hear the root first

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 127, with Chd1 to Chd4 set to 64, 67, 69 and 72; the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Note Strum. Nothing is assigned yet. This is a slow comparison at 90 BPM and Rate /9: each channel step lasts 1.5 seconds. The long note lets all five voices finish before Stop.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Strum to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/2: the notes will be half a step apart. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Spread.
steps.title: Set a half-step Strum

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/4. Chord Accel Mod is not assigned, so every gap stays the same. Each gap is now 3/4 step (1/2 + 1/4) instead of 1/2. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The MIDI strip lists the root C3 (60) and then E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69), C4 (72), evenly spaced 3/4 step apart. Here 3/4 of a channel step is 1.125 seconds, so the five onsets are evenly separated; every voice retains velocity 127.
steps.title: Widen each gap for a slow, harp-like roll

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Note Strum. No slot is assigned yet, so the five notes would sound together.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Strum to slot 1 and K2 to return. Turn E3 to 1/2. Slot 1 now shows 1/2 with no L or S marker; pause here before moving to another slot.
steps.title: Verify the half-step Strum value

steps.caption: From the half-step Strum slot, turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Pattern.
steps.title: Choose the chord pattern slot

steps.caption: Finish the setup the next examples reuse: assign Chord Pattern and turn E3 one detent to -> (forward); Assign Mute Chord Root and leave it at X so the root still sounds; then assign Chord Velocity Mod and turn E3 to +10 (E2 moves to the next slot, K2 opens the list, E3 browses, K3 assigns, K2 returns). Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip the notes arrive one after another, half a step apart: C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72). With Strum at X they would all start together.
steps.title: Hear the strummed chord

chord-strum-a-timed-chord.title: Separate a chord into timed voices

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Velocity Mod. Chord Note Strum (1/2), Chord Pattern (-> forward) and Mute Chord Root (X, off) are already assigned, so the root and four chord notes strum half a step apart.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Velocity Mod and K2 to return, then turn E3 up ten detents to +10. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip the notes C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72) carry velocities 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90: each note is 10 louder than the one before, so the chord swells upward.
steps.title: Raise each voice by 10

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major. The sequencer is stopped. Channel 1's output is a example MIDI device whose parameter Control 1 sends MIDI CC 1 from 0 to 127 and has an Off position shown as X. No value is stored for Control 1 yet. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Choose the example MIDI device on channel 1's Device screen. Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, go to MOSAIC, open channel 1's device parameters and turn E2 to Control 1. It reads X: Off, so no CC is sent.
steps.title: Select Control 1

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent right from X. Control 1 reads 0 and sends MIDI CC 1 with value 0.
steps.title: Turn up from X to 0

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent right. Control 1 reads 1 and sends MIDI CC 1 with value 1. Each detent moves the value by one.
steps.title: One more detent

steps.caption: Keep turning E3 right until Control 1 reads 64, passing 63. In the MIDI strip, CC 1 shows 63 and then 64.
steps.title: Turn up to the middle

steps.caption: Keep turning E3 right until Control 1 reads 126, one below the highest value.
steps.title: Turn up to just below the top

steps.caption: Turn E3 right once more: Control 1 reads 127, the highest value, and sends MIDI CC 1 with 127. One more turn leaves it at 127.
steps.title: Turn up to the top and stop

steps.caption: Turn E3 left: the value falls to 64, then 1, then to X, which means Off: no CC is sent. One more turn down stays at X. The last frame shows Control 1 back at X.
steps.title: Turn down to X

steps.caption: Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1 to 4 and is assigned to channel 1, which loops steps 1 to 4. Channel 1's Masks are Note C3 (60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2, and the tempo is 90 BPM. Playback is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4): the range is now 16 steps, one bar. On row 4, steps 5 to 16 now glow dimly because they are inside the loop (they were dark at range 4), and the trigs are still on steps 1 to 4. Then open the Clock page for the next step: turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Clock and press K3.
steps.title: Loop all 16 steps

steps.caption: On CLOCK CH01, check that Rate reads /1 before pressing K3.
steps.title: Read the selected rate

steps.caption: Select Rate (the top row of the CLOCK page; turn E2 up if it is not highlighted) and press K3. CLOCK CH01 shows Rate /1, the default sixteenth-note rate: each step lasts 1/6 s at 90 BPM and the 16 steps last 2.7 s. Nothing changes here; this confirms the rate that every timing in the course relies on.
steps.title: Check the rate

steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8), tap (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4) to remove those trigs, then tap (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4) to add trigs. Keep (1,4). PATTERN TRIG PAT01 CH01 shows trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13: four steps apart is one beat at 90 BPM.
steps.title: Move the trigs onto the beats

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 as before, and row 4 of the grid shows the four trigs one beat apart inside the 16-step range. Masks stays open so chapter 5 starts on the page it needs.
steps.title: Open Masks for the next chapter

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two 16-step passes run (about 5.3 s), then tap Play to stop. While it plays the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4, one beat at a time over the four trigs. The MIDI strip shows note 60 (C3) at velocity 80 once per beat, about 667 ms (2/3 s) apart: the same note as chapter 3, spread over a bar instead of 167 ms apart. Stop leaves no note sounding.
steps.title: Hear the longer phrase

course-build-a-phrase.title: 4. Spread the rhythm across a bar

steps.caption: The project from chapter 2: channel 1 sends to a MIDI instrument on port 1, MIDI channel 1 (its Device page shows CC Device, MIDI channel CC1, MIDI port OUT 1), and the tempo is 90 BPM (GLOBAL FEEL shows Tempo 90). No pattern has trigs yet, nothing is assigned to a channel and playback is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1), then tap (1,4), (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4). Row 4 holds steps 1 to 16, so these are the first four steps. PATTERN TRIG PAT01 CH01 shows four bright trigs at the left of row 4. Four neighbouring trigs are a deliberately plain rhythm to hear first; chapter 4 spreads them out.
steps.title: Enter four trigs

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then tap (1,2), the first pattern slot on row 2, to give channel 1 pattern 1. Mosaic opens MERGE MODES for CH01 because assigning a pattern always shows it, and the tooltip reads Pattern 1 added to ch. 1. Patterns reads 01; ignore the other rows for now.
steps.title: Assign pattern 1

steps.caption: Row 4 of the channel page is the range row: hold (1,4), tap (4,4) and release (1,4) to loop only steps 1 to 4. Steps 1 to 4 stay bright, the rest go dark, and the tooltip reads Channel 1 length changed.
steps.title: Loop four steps

steps.caption: Turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. NOTE MASKS CH01 lists eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4), all X: no mask is set, so the channel has no pitch, velocity or length yet. With no step held, E2 chooses a cell and E3 sets that cell for every step of the channel.
steps.title: Open Masks

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Note and E3 until the channel default reads C3.
steps.title: Set the channel note

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Vel and E3 until the channel default reads 80.
steps.title: Set the channel velocity

steps.caption: Select Note with E2 and turn E3 right until it reads C3 (it starts at X, so about 60 detents), select Vel and turn E3 right to 80 (about 80 detents), then select Len and turn E3 right to 1/2 (8 detents). NOTE MASKS CH01 now lists Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2, the defaults for every step.
steps.title: Give the trigs a pitch, level and length

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), listen for two repeats of the four-step loop, then tap Play again. While it plays the screen stays on NOTE MASKS, the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows note 60 (C3) at velocity 80 about every 167 ms (1/6 s): four notes per repeat, so you hear a fast stutter rather than a tune. Stop leaves no note sounding. This confirms the whole chain (pattern, channel, masks, output) before you shape the rhythm.
steps.title: Play and stop

steps.caption: Stop playback. The note, velocity and length settings remain C3, 80 and 1/2.
steps.title: Stop and confirm the note setup remains

steps.caption: A new, empty project is open on NOTE MASKS for channel 1 before the first course action. No mask is set.
steps.title: Empty project start

steps.caption: You start from a new, empty project: transport stopped, nothing set up, channel 1 selected. Tap Channel (3,8), the third button on the bottom row. The screen opens NOTE MASKS for CH01 with eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4) that all read X: no value is set, because a new channel has no pattern, pitch or sound yet. On the grid, (1,1) is lit because channel 1 is the channel you edit, and (3,8) is lit because it is the page you are on.
steps.title: Open channel 1

steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8), the fifth button on the bottom row. The grid and screen switch to the pattern editor: the title row reads PATTERN TRIG with PAT01 CH01, and every step is dim because pattern 1 has no trigs yet. (1,1) is lit because pattern 1 is the pattern you edit, and (5,8) is lit because you are on the Pattern page.
steps.title: Try the Pattern button

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 alone, C, C, C, D, from channel and step masks: Note C3 (60), Vel 80, and on step 13 Note D3 (62) at Vel 50; NOTE MASKS CH01 is open. Channel 2 plays pattern 2 (degrees 0 and 4, octave -1) as MIDI 48 and 55. The merge Strategy is still All, which changes nothing with one pattern. Scale slot 1 is C major and the tempo is 90 BPM.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Note and turn E3 left until it reads X (no mask). NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X: the channel no longer decides the pitch, the pattern notes will.
steps.title: Let the pattern notes through

steps.caption: Hold (13,4) and press K2: the tooltip reads Masks for step 13 cleared, and K2 removes every mask on the step, so its Note 62 and Vel 50 both go. Then select Vel, turn E3 left 30 detents to 50 while still holding: NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note X and Vel 50, the quiet ending back on step 13 alone. Release (13,4).
steps.title: Restore the quiet ending

steps.caption: Release (13,4). NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X and Vel 80 (the channel defaults); step 13's own Vel 50 only shows while you hold it.
steps.title: Back to the channel defaults

steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1), tap Pattern (5,8) again for the note view and tap (1,7), (5,7), (9,7) and (13,6): degree 0 on steps 1, 5 and 9, and degree 1, one row up and the next note of the scale, on step 13. PATTERN NOTE PAT01 CH01 shows the tooltip Step 13 note set to 1.
steps.title: Write the melody as degrees

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), play two passes and stop. While it plays the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding 60, 60, 60, 62 from the pattern's own notes, step 13 at velocity 50, and channel 2 sounding 48 and 55.
steps.title: Play it from the pattern

steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8) to open the scale page, tap scale slot 2 at (2,3), then play two passes and stop. While it plays the screen shows SCALE SLOT 02 with Root C and Scale Major. Slot 2 holds C major like slot 1, so nothing changes: the MIDI strip shows 60, 60, 60, 62 on channel 1 and 48 and 55 on channel 2. Ignore the Degree and Transpose rows on this page; they stay at I and 0.
steps.title: Prepare a second scale
