steps.title: The device setting does not change

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-note phrase through a MIDI device. The tempo is 130 BPM, the sequencer is stopped, the norns shows channel 1's Device screen and the PARAMS menu is closed. No trig params are assigned yet, so no CC values are sent.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4) and tap step 5 at (5,4) to extend the channel range to steps 1 to 5. Then on Channel tasks > Trig params assign CC 1 to a slot with E3 and K3, so steps can carry CC lock values. The phrase plays from the internal clock at 130 BPM.
steps.title: Assign CC 1 to a Trig params slot

steps.caption: On Trig params, hold each of steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 in turn and turn E3 to give it its own CC 1 lock value. Then tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, choose MOSAIC and select Lock lead time (ms) in the Parameter locks section. Turn E3 to 0. At 0 each lock value is sent at the same moment as its step, together with the note. This is the original timing.
steps.title: Give steps CC values, set lead to 0

steps.caption: Close the menu and press Play (1,8), listen to the phrase and press Play again to stop. In the MIDI strip every CC 1 value sits at the same millisecond as its Note On.
steps.title: Hear it at 0 ms

steps.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Lock lead time (ms) and set it to 25, the default. At 130 BPM each lock value will now leave about 29 ms before its step (25 ms rounded up to a whole clock pulse of 4.8 ms). The notes keep their exact times.
steps.title: Set 25 ms lead

steps.caption: Close the menu, press Play (1,8) and Stop. In the MIDI strip each CC 1 value now arrives about 29 ms before its Note On, which still falls at its usual time. A synth that smooths incoming CC changes has already reached the new value when the note starts.
steps.title: Hear it at 25 ms

steps.caption: Tap K1, reopen Lock lead time (ms) and set it to 50. At 130 BPM lock values will leave about 53 ms (11 pulses) ahead of their step, and the notes still sound at their usual times. Use the larger lead for slow filters or effects that need longer to settle.
steps.title: Set 50 ms lead

steps.caption: Close the menu, press Play (1,8) and Stop. In the MIDI strip each CC 1 value arrives about 53 ms before its Note On, so the change lands before the note rather than gliding through it. The notes do not move.
steps.title: Hear it at 50 ms

lock-lead-menu-values.title: Send lock values before their notes

steps.caption: A new project with playback stopped, the default C major scale and Rate /1 (one step is a sixteenth note) on every channel. Channel 1 is set up and its Device page is open: it plays range 1-4, MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, to its own MIDI output. Channel 2 is not set up yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1), turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device and press K3. The header reads CH02: this second channel will play a three-step loop.
steps.title: Select channel 2

steps.caption: Give channel 2 its own MIDI output on the Device page. Give it pattern 1 and the range steps 1-3 (hold step 1 and tap step 3), then open Masks and set its values: Note 79, Vel 40 and Len ½ on every step, with step 2 locked to Note 81, Vel 60 and Len 1¼. Select channel 1 and press Play. Both channels start together on step 1. At step 4 channel 1 plays its fourth note, 65, while channel 2, whose three-step loop has wrapped, plays 79 again: look for 65 beside 79 in the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step".
steps.title: Build channel 2, then play both loops

steps.caption: Keep playing. Channel 1 loops four steps on its own MIDI port and channel 2 loops three on another, so their notes fall out of step and the MIDI strip shows two different phrases running side by side.
steps.title: Both channels keep looping

steps.caption: Keep playing. Hold step 4 and tap step 2 on channel 1: the reversed range (start 4, end 2) is refused and both loops carry on. Twelve steps after the start, the first step count that both 4 and 3 divide into, both phrases begin again from their first notes at the same moment: channel 1 plays 60 as channel 2 plays 79, and the next step plays 62 with 81. Look for that sequence in the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", two seconds after the loops started.
steps.title: Both loops restart together at step 13

steps.caption: Press Stop. The refused reversed range changed nothing: both phrases keep the same timing, notes, velocities and lengths. Channel 1 still plays 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97 over steps 1 to 4, and channel 2 plays 79, 81, 79 over steps 1 to 3. Playback is stopped and the Masks screen is showing.
steps.title: Both loops stay locked

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device on OUT 1 and channel 2 to a second output, MIDI port 2 on MIDI channel 2. Each channel has its Masks defaults set so that every step sounds: channel 1 plays a low drum note, C1 (MIDI 36), at velocity 100 and channel 2 plays MIDI 72 at velocity 90, both half a step long. Channel 1's Masks screen is open. The Rate is /1 at 90 BPM, so one step lasts a sixth of a second, and playback is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8) for Pattern Trig and choose pattern 1 at (1,1). Tap steps 2, 3 and 4 off at (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4), then tap steps 5, 9 and 13 on at (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4). Pattern 1 now has trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13: four hits per bar.
steps.title: Enter the drum pattern

steps.caption: Choose pattern 2 at (2,1) and tap steps 1, 3 and 4 at (1,4), (3,4) and (4,4): a figure with trigs on steps 1, 3 and 4.
steps.title: Enter the short figure

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8) and channel 1 at (1,1); pattern 1 is already assigned to it. Hold step 1 at (1,4), tap step 16 at (16,4) and release step 1. The footer reads Channel 1 length changed: channel 1 now loops steps 1 to 16, and its four drum steps stay lit.
steps.title: Give channel 1 sixteen steps

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1) and assign pattern 2 at (2,2). Hold step 1, tap step 5 at (5,4) and release step 1. The footer reads Channel 2 length changed: channel 2 loops steps 1 to 5, and its three figure steps are lit.
steps.title: Give channel 2 five steps

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap Play (1,8). The drum channel repeats every 16 steps and the figure every 5, so the figure's three notes slide across the drum hits. Both channels start together on step 1 and only start together again on step 81, 80 steps or 13 and a third seconds later, because 80 is the first step count that both 16 and 5 divide into. Look at the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step": channel 1 plays MIDI 36 four times in every 16 steps and channel 2 plays MIDI 72 three times in every 5. Tap Play again to stop.
steps.title: Play 80 steps

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97 on steps 1 to 4. Channel 2 does not play yet; in the next step you set it up on MIDI port 2, channel 2 with the same pattern. A saved MIDI map is loaded with two relative controls that both accumulate: CC 20 edits the velocity mask of the selected channel and CC 21 edits the velocity mask of channel 2. Both velocity masks are Off (X) and the norns shows channel 1's Device page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Set up channel 2: select it (2,1), open its Device page and set its output to port 2, MIDI channel 2 with E2 and E3, press K3, give it pattern 1 with (1,2) and hold step 1 then tap step 4 to loop four steps. Select channel 1 (1,1), tap Play (1,8) and listen, then tap Play to stop. Channel 1 (port 1) and channel 2 (port 2) both play velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97: no control has been moved yet.
steps.title: Hear both channels before any CC

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Masks for channel 1 and select the Velocity cell, which reads X. Channel 1 is selected. Send CC 20 with value 65 eleven times (the strip shows eleven control changes). For a relative (binary offset) control, 65 means one step up, 63 means one step down and 0 also counts as down. The velocity mask starts at X, so the first step reaches 0 and the eleventh reaches 10: the Velocity cell now reads 10.
steps.title: CC 20 on the selected channel 1

steps.caption: Tap Play. Channel 1 now plays every note at velocity 10. Channel 2 is unchanged.
steps.title: Hear channel 1 at velocity 10

steps.caption: Send CC 20 with value 63 twice and tap Play: channel 1 comes down from 10 to 8 and plays every note at velocity 8. Channel 2 is still unchanged.
steps.title: CC 20 down twice

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Masks screen stays open and its Velocity cell reads X for channel 2. Send CC 20 with value 65 three times: the cell reads 2. A selected-channel control follows the channel you select.
steps.title: Select channel 2, CC 20 follows

steps.caption: Tap Play. Channel 2 now plays at velocity 2 and channel 1 stays at 8.
steps.title: Hear channel 2 at velocity 2

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) to select it. Its Velocity cell still reads 8. Send CC 21 with value 65 twice, then tap channel 2 at (2,1) to look: its Velocity cell reads 4, up from 2. CC 21 is mapped to channel 2 itself, so it ignores which channel is selected.
steps.title: CC 21 ignores the selection

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) again and tap Play. Channel 2 plays at velocity 4 and channel 1 stays at 8.
steps.title: Hear channel 2 at velocity 4

steps.caption: Send CC 21 with value 0, then tap channel 2 at (2,1) to look. Any value below 64 is a decrease, so its Velocity cell drops from 4 to 3.
steps.title: CC 21 value 0 steps down

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) again and tap Play. Channel 2 plays at velocity 3 and channel 1 stays at 8.
steps.title: Hear channel 2 at velocity 3

mapping-child-selected-and-fixed.title: A loaded map follows the selected or fixed channel

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and no masks are set. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Chd1. The four chord rows Chd1-Chd4 add voices above each step's root, and X means no voice.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads 3rd (two detents). Every step now plays its root and the scale third above it: 60+64, 62+65, 64+67, 65+69. Chord values are scale intervals, not MIDI numbers. Read the MIDI strip: each step sends its root and its chord note together.
Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)) and turn E3 right until the screen reads 5th (two more detents). Step 1 now plays 60 and 67; the screen shows 5th while the step is held.

Release step 1. The screen shows the channel default 3rd again, but step 1 keeps its own fifth: the phrase is 60+67, then 62+65, 64+67, 65+69. Read the MIDI strip: step 1 sends 60 and 67 together, the other steps their roots and thirds.
Hold step 1, press K2 and release the step. The fifth is cleared and step 1 returns to the channel third: 60+64, then 62+65, 64+67, 65+69.

Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, scroll to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Vel. The value reads X: there is no channel velocity mask, so every step plays the velocity it has in pattern 1. X means inherit.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads 50. This channel velocity mask replaces the pattern's velocities: every note now plays at 50, so the whole phrase is softer. Pitch and timing are unchanged.
Hold step 1 at (1,4) and turn E3 right until the screen reads 90. While a step is held, the screen shows that step's own velocity.
Release step 1. A step mask overrides the channel mask, so step 1 plays at 90 as an accent while steps 2 to 4 keep the channel velocity of 50. The screen goes back to the channel value, 50.

Hold step 2 at (2,4) and keep holding it. Turn E3 left until the screen reads 0. Velocity 0 is a silent step, which is different from X: X means inherit and still plays. Step 2 is now muted, so a pass plays steps 1, 3 and 4 only. Step 2 is still held in this frame.
Release step 2. The screen returns to 50, but step 2 stays silent: read the MIDI strip, where the loop plays C3 (60) at 90, then E3 (64) and F3 (65) at 50, and step 2's D is missing.
Hold step 2 again, press K2 to clear its masks and release it. The step mask is gone, so step 2 plays at the channel velocity of 50 again and step 1 keeps its accent at 90: velocities 90, 50, 50, 50.
With no step held, turn E2 to Len and turn E3 right until the screen reads 1/2. All four notes now have a half-step gate. The velocities stay at 90, 50, 50 and 50.

Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Vel. The value reads X.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads 80. The channel velocity replaces the pattern's velocities: every note plays at 80. This loop plays C, D, E and F, not one repeated note, so read the pitches in the MIDI strip.
Hold step 3 at (3,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads 100 and release. Step 3 is the accent: the MIDI strip shows 80, 80, 100, 80.
Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 left until the screen reads 35, and keep holding. The ST02 readout shows this step exception before you release it.
Release step 2. The screen returns to the channel default 80, while the step exception remains. The MIDI phrase is 80, 35, 100, 80: the quiet ghost note leads into the accent.

mask-ghost-note.title: Set a ghost note and an accent

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. The Masks page (Channel tasks, then Masks) is open on Note. The channel's Note mask default is 67 (G3), step 1 has its own mask 72 and step 2 has 74, so the MIDI strip reads 72, 74, 67, 67.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4), press K2 and release. Step 1 falls back to the channel default, 67, but step 2 keeps its 74. Play, then stop: the strip reads 67, 74, 67, 67.
steps.title: Clear step 1 only

steps.caption: Hold step 1 again, hold K1 and press K2, then release. With a step held, only that step is cleared, even while K1 is down, and step 1 has nothing left to clear. Play, then stop: the strip still reads 67, 74, 67, 67.
steps.title: A held step wins over the shift clear

steps.caption: With no step held, hold K1 and press K2. Every step exception clears but the channel default stays. Play, then stop: the strip reads 67, 67, 67, 67.
steps.title: Clear every step mask on the channel

mask-locks-clear-neighbours.title: Clear a note mask without clearing its neighbour

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The value reads X.
With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads C3 (MIDI 60). The channel note replaces the pattern's notes, so the MIDI strip shows C3 four times; the velocities stay the pattern's.
Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 right until the screen reads C4 (12 detents) and release the step. The screen goes back to C3, and the loop now starts on C4 (72) before three C3 notes.
Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 right until it reads D4 (14 detents) and release. The MIDI strip shows 72, 74, 60, 60.
Hold step 3 at (3,4), turn E3 right until it reads G4 (19 detents) and release. The MIDI strip shows 72, 74, 79, 60.
Hold step 4 at (4,4), turn E3 right until it reads E4 (16 detents) and release. The melody ends on E4: 72, 74, 79, 76.
Hold step 4 and turn E3 left until it reads D4 (two detents).
Release step 4. Only step 4 changed: the phrase now ends 72, 74, 79, 74.
Hold step 4 and turn E3 left two more detents until it reads C4, then release. The phrase ends on the root: 72, 74, 79, 72.

mask-melody-ending.title: Change the ending of a four-note melody

steps.caption: Starting point: pattern 1 plays C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Open Channel tasks → Masks → Note. With no step held, the Note value is X, so each step uses its merged pattern note.
With no step held, turn E3 right until Note reads G3 (MIDI 67). All four steps now play G3 while retaining the source-pattern velocities.
With no step held, turn E3 left until Note reads X. The channel mask is unset, so MIDI returns to the pattern's C3, D3, E3 and F3 notes at their original velocities.

Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1-4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, and no masks are set. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The header reads NOTE MASKS CH01 and the value reads X, which means no mask is set, so each step plays its own pattern note.

With no step held, turn E3 right until the screen reads G3 (MIDI 67). The screen shows the note name, so stop on the readout. This is the channel note mask: all four steps now play G, and their velocities stay as they were.

Hold step 1 at (1,4). The header gains ST01, which means edits now apply to that step only. Turn E3 right until the screen reads C4 (MIDI 72, five detents up from G3). Step 1 has its own note, which overrides the channel default.
Release step 1. The header loses ST01 and the screen returns to the channel default, G3. Playback now starts with C4 (72) and continues G, G, G: a step mask beats the channel mask.
Hold step 2 at (2,4) and turn E3 right until the screen reads D4 (MIDI 74). While a step is held, the screen shows that step's own note.
Release step 2. Steps 1 and 2 each have their own note (C4, D4), and steps 3 and 4 still play the channel note G.
Hold step 1 and press K2, then release the step. Step 1's mask is cleared, so it plays G3 again from the channel default, and step 2 still plays D4.
With no step held, hold K1 and press K2. Every step exception is cleared at once and the channel default stays: the screen still reads G3 and all four steps play G again.

mask-precedence.title: Set channel and step note masks

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 in an eight-step loop. Steps 1-4 hold four notes and steps 5-8 are empty. No masks are set. Open Channel tasks with E1, turn E2 to Masks and press K3, then turn E2 to Note. The value reads X.

With no step held, turn E3 right until Note reads C3 (MIDI 60). The channel default replaces the pattern's notes on every step, so all four steps now play C3: read the MIDI strip, which shows C3 four times at the velocities the pattern already had (127, 117, 107, 97).
Turn E2 to Vel and turn E3 right until it reads 80. The channel velocity replaces the pattern's velocities too: the MIDI strip now shows C3 at velocity 80 four times.

Turn E2 to Len and turn E3 right until it reads 1/2. The four notes now have a half-step gate. A trig mask has no pattern note of its own, so a trig you add next will use these three channel defaults.
Return to the channel Note field before setting Step 5.
Hold Step 5 and set its stored note to E3.
Release Step 5. Its E3 note is stored, but the step still has no trig, so the loop keeps playing the four C3 notes.

Turn E2 back to Note. Hold step 5 at (5,4), turn E3 right four detents until the screen reads E3 (MIDI 64) and release it. Step 5 now has its own note, but it still has no trig, so nothing new sounds. Then hold K1 and tap step 5, release the step, then release K1. A trig mask now forces step 5 on, so the loop plays a fifth note after the four notes on steps 1-4: E3 (64) at velocity 80, shown in the MIDI strip and by the new lit step 5 on the grid.

Hold K1 and tap step 5 again, release the step, then release K1. The same gesture toggles the trig mask off, so the loop returns to four C3 notes on steps 1-4. Step 5 keeps its note mask but has no trig, so it stays silent.
In Matrix, choose Control 1, select Macro 1, and set its depth to 0.10. With Macro 1 at zero, the selected CC stays at 32.
steps.title: Set a small route

steps.caption: Start the same C3, D3, E3, F3 phrase. The notes and their one-sixth-second spacing stay the same, and CC 1 remains at 32 while the macro is at zero.
steps.title: Hear the unchanged phrase

steps.caption: Set Toolkit Macro 1 to 0.50 and replay. Mosaic sends CC 1 at 38 as playback starts, and the four notes keep their pitches, velocities, timing and gates.
steps.title: Move CC 1 modestly

steps.caption: Clear the Matrix depth and replay. Playback starts by sending CC 1 at 32 while the same four-note phrase continues unchanged.
steps.title: Restore the authored value

steps.caption: With the Matrix route still clear, return Toolkit Macro 1 to 0.0 so the setup is left at its starting value.
steps.title: Leave Macro 1 at zero

matrix-macro-modest-cc.title: Make a small CC move with Macro 1

steps.caption: The norns matrix and toolkit mods are installed and enabled. Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a CC device with Rate /1, the sequencer is stopped, and the Matrix has no routes yet. The Device page for CH01 is showing.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open MODS > MATRIX. Choose MOSAIC CH 1: CC DEVICE and select Fixed Note, which forces the channel to one MIDI note number (not quantised). Its row shows dashes: no source and no depth yet.
steps.title: Open the Matrix and choose Fixed Note

steps.caption: Press K3 to open Fixed Note's sources and turn E2 down to macro 1. A macro is a knob in the toolkit mod that you set by hand. The macro 1 row still shows dashes.
steps.title: Choose macro 1

steps.caption: Hold E3 turning right until the depth reads 1.00. Depth is how strongly the macro drives Fixed Note: 1.00 is the full effect.
steps.title: Set full modulation depth

steps.caption: Open toolkit macro 1's parameters (E1 to the parameter list, then macro 1) and select Value. It reads 0.0: the macro is at rest, so nothing sounds different yet.
steps.title: Find the macro Value

steps.caption: Turn E3 right until Value reads 1.0, the macro at full strength. The macro now drives Fixed Note at the depth you set.
steps.title: Raise the macro to its full value

steps.caption: Press K1 to leave the menu, and press Play, then Play again to stop. Every note is now MIDI 127, the Fixed Note the macro forces, while the velocities stay 127, 117, 107, 97, as the MIDI strip lists.
steps.title: Hear the phrase follow the macro

steps.caption: Press K1 to return to the menu and open the Matrix again. The Fixed Note route for macro 1 is selected.
steps.title: Return to the macro's route

steps.caption: With macro 1 selected in the Fixed Note source list, press K3 to clear that route. Its depth returns to a dash. The macro no longer overrides the phrase’s written pitches.
steps.title: Clear the depth

steps.caption: Press K1 and Play, then Play again to stop. The phrase is back to its authored notes, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, with velocities 127, 117, 107, 97.
steps.title: Recover the authored pitches

matrix-macro-route-clear.title: Route a macro and remove its depth

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. Channel tasks is open on channel 1. Nothing has been edited yet, so the channel's memory (its list of remembered edits) is empty.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E2 down to History and press K3. The Memory screen shows your position in the channel's remembered edits, as 'position of total'. It reads 0 of 0 because nothing has been edited yet.
steps.title: Open History

steps.caption: With nothing remembered, K2, K3 and E3 in History do nothing: the counter stays at 0 of 0. Tap Play (1,8): channel 1 plays C D E F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65. Tap Play again to stop.
steps.title: Hear the original phrase

steps.caption: Open Masks (E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). Any MIDI keyboard or controller connected to the norns can write onto a held step: hold step 1 and play note 72 at velocity 90, release, then hold step 2 and play note 76 at velocity 80. Each is one edit that Memory keeps. Reopen History: the counter reads 2 of 2, meaning you are at edit 2 of the 2 remembered.
steps.title: Record two step edits

steps.caption: Tap Play: the phrase is 72, 76, 64, 65 at velocities 90, 80, 107, 97, because steps 1 and 2 carry your edits. Now, in History, turn E3 one detent left. The counter reads 1 of 2: the second edit is undone.
steps.title: Undo the second edit

steps.caption: Tap Play: step 1 keeps your recorded note 72 at velocity 90, and step 2 is back to its original note 62 at velocity 117.
steps.title: Hear the undone state

steps.caption: Turn E3 left again: the counter reads 0 of 2, the oldest state, before either edit. (K2 jumps straight here.)
steps.title: Return to the first state

steps.caption: Tap Play: the original four-step phrase 60, 62, 64, 65 is back. Then turn E3 left three more times. The counter stays at 0 of 2: you cannot go further back than the first state.
steps.title: Stop at the oldest state

steps.caption: Tap Play: still the original phrase. Then turn E3 right once. The counter reads 1 of 2: step 1 has its edit back.
steps.title: Redo the first edit

steps.caption: Tap Play: 72, 62, 64, 65, so only the first edit is back. Then turn E3 right once more. The counter is back at 2 of 2.
steps.title: Redo both edits

steps.caption: Tap Play: 72, 76, 64, 65, both recorded edits are back.
steps.title: Hear both edits again

steps.caption: Turn E3 right three times: the counter stays at 2 of 2, the newest state. Tap Play for 72, 76, 64, 65, press K2 to jump all the way back (0 of 2, the original phrase when you play), then press K3 to jump forward to 2 of 2 (both edits again). Now turn E3 left once: the counter reads 1 of 2 and the second edit is undone, so a new edit will replace it.
steps.title: Undo one step again

steps.caption: Open Masks, hold step 3 and play MIDI note 79 at velocity 70, release, then reopen History. The counter reads 2 of 2 again, but it is a different second action: the new edit replaced the undone one.
steps.title: Replace the undone action

steps.caption: Tap Play: 72, 62, 79, 65. Step 1 keeps its edit, step 2 is back to its original 62 and step 3 plays your new note 79. The old second edit (76) is gone.
steps.title: Hear the new branch

memory-undo-redo-and-branch.title: Undo, redo and replace a remembered edit

steps.caption: Channel 1 has two patterns assigned. Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F: MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) and pattern 2 has trigs on steps 1 and 2 (note C, velocity 100). The Merge modes screen is showing at 90 BPM with every merge mode at its default and playback stopped. The Patterns row reads 01 02: it only shows which patterns the channel plays, and turning E3 on it changes nothing. Assign patterns with the pattern slot buttons on the grid.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K2, turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Merge modes and press K3 to return to the Merge modes screen, then turn E2 down to Strategy, the trig merge. It reads SKIP, the default: a step plays only if exactly one pattern has a trig there. Steps 1 and 2 are in both patterns and drop out; only steps 3 and 4 remain.
steps.title: Skip overlap

steps.caption: Press Play at (1,8), then Stop. The loop plays only steps 3 and 4: MIDI 64 (velocity 107) and 65 (velocity 97), over and over.
steps.title: Hear Skip

steps.caption: Turn E3 up once: Strategy reads ONLY, with the footer ONLY APPLIED. (Turning E3 down first does nothing: SKIP is the lowest choice.) Only keeps steps that have a trig in more than one pattern, so steps 1 and 2 play and steps 3 and 4 drop out. The (14,8) button follows the choice.
steps.title: Keep overlap

steps.caption: Turn E3 up once more: Strategy reads ALL, footer ALL APPLIED. Every trig from either pattern plays. The change applies immediately; there is no K3 apply. The (14,8) button follows the choice.
steps.title: Play the union

steps.caption: Press Play, then Stop. All four steps sound: MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 114, 109, 107, 97. Steps 1 and 2 are in both patterns, so their notes and velocities are averaged: C and C stay C, and (127 + 100) / 2 = 114.
steps.title: Hear All

steps.caption: Turn E2 down to Note mode, the pitch merge. It reads AVERAGE, the default. The screen's labels map to the manual's modes: UP is Higher, DOWN is Lower, and PAT 1 and PAT 2 take the note from that pattern.
steps.title: Open Note mode

steps.caption: Turn E3 up one detent at a time and watch Note mode: AVERAGE, then UP (Higher), DOWN (Lower), PAT 1, and finally PAT 2. At PAT 2 each step takes its note from pattern 2, which is C everywhere. The rhythm still comes from the ALL strategy.
steps.title: Turn through the note modes

steps.caption: Press Play, then Stop. The four steps still sound, now all at MIDI 60, pattern 2's note, with the same velocities (114, 109, 107, 97).
steps.title: Hear Pattern 2 notes

steps.caption: Turn E3 down four detents: PAT 1, DOWN, UP, then AVERAGE (one more turn down stays on AVERAGE). Press Play, then Stop. The phrase is back to MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65.
steps.title: Restore the average and hear it

steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps at 90 BPM on the example MIDI device and is set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) is the Anchor; pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100 on steps 5 and 7) offers additions. Both patterns are assigned, Add amount is 100 and Add accent is 70. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Channel (3,8), turn E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Merge modes and press K3. Strategy reads FOUNDATION: Foundation, not the saved trig merge, is choosing this channel's trigs.
steps.title: Open Merge modes

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Active. Strategy and Active both read FOUNDATION and Pending reads NONE. The Strategy key (14,8) glows at its brightest, the sign that Foundation is in charge: the four anchors on steps 1 to 4 plus additions on steps 5 and 7.
steps.title: Foundation decides the trigs

steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. You hear C D E F (60, 62, 64, 65) followed by the additions, a C on steps 5 and 7. Look at the strip below: the additions are quieter, velocity 70, because Add accent 70 scales pattern 2's velocity of 100.
steps.title: Hear Foundation

steps.caption: Reopen Merge modes, select Strategy and turn E3 to ALL. Strategy and Active read ALL and the Strategy key (14,8) dims: the saved trig merge is deciding again, with every trig of both patterns.
steps.title: Switch the Strategy to All

steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. The same notes sound, but the additions on steps 5 and 7 now keep pattern 2's own velocity, 100, so they are louder than Foundation's 70 in the strip below.
steps.title: Hear All

steps.caption: Reopen Merge modes, select Strategy and turn E3 to SKIP. The footer reads SKIP APPLIED, Strategy and Active read SKIP and the Strategy key (14,8) dims further. Skip, Only and All hand the trigs back to the saved legacy merge; Foundation's protection and accent no longer apply.
steps.title: Return to Skip

merge-shape-owns-trigs.title: Foundation and All: who decides the trigs

steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps at 90 BPM on the example MIDI device and is set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) is the Anchor; pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100) has trigs on steps 3 and 7, so step 3 is a step both patterns trig. Both patterns are assigned. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 4 and 7.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Channel (3,8), turn E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Merge modes and press K3. Strategy reads FOUNDATION: Foundation, not the saved trig merge, is choosing this channel's trigs.
steps.title: Open Merge modes

steps.caption: Turn E3 left to SKIP. The footer reads SKIP APPLIED and the Strategy key (14,8) dims. Skip applies a trig only if it appears in exactly one selected pattern, so step 3, where both patterns trig, will not sound.
steps.title: Hand the trigs back to Skip

steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. The strip below lists C D F (60, 62, 65) from pattern 1 on steps 1, 2 and 4, then a C at velocity 100 on step 7, which only pattern 2 trigs. Step 3 is silent: there is no E and no merged note.
steps.title: Hear Skip

steps.caption: Reopen Merge modes, select Strategy and turn E3 to ALL. Strategy and Active read ALL. All applies a trig if it appears in any selected pattern, so step 3 now sounds.
steps.title: Switch the Strategy to All

steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops run, then tap Stop. Step 3 now sounds, merged from both patterns: the Average note merge puts the E (degree III) and the C (degree I) on degree II, a D (62), and the Average velocity merge turns 107 and 100 into 104. Look for D at velocity 104 between 62 and 65 in the strip below; step 7 is still a C at velocity 100.
steps.title: Hear All

merge-shape-skip-shared-step.title: Skip and All on a step both patterns trig

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 (the channel range) with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen and every Mosaic option is at its default. Lock merged to pent. is at its default On. Only pattern 1 exists and is assigned to channel 1; patterns 2 and 3 are built in the next steps.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock merged to pent. and turn E3 left to Off. The default is On. The row shows Off; this option only affects notes produced by merge modes.
steps.title: Turn Lock merged to pent. Off

steps.caption: Close the menu. Press Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1) and tap (1,7), (2,5), (3,3) and (4,1) to rewrite its four notes as scale degrees I, III, V, VII (C E G B). The four notes light on the grid.
steps.title: Enter pattern 1

steps.caption: Choose pattern 2 at (2,1), add four trigs on steps 1 to 4 and tap (1,5), (2,3), (3,1) and (4,7): degrees III, V, VII, I (E G B C). Pattern 2 is a second voice that overlaps pattern 1 on every step.
steps.title: Enter pattern 2

steps.caption: Choose pattern 3 at (3,1), add four trigs on steps 1 to 4 and put their notes on the top row, (1,1) to (4,1); the four top-row notes light. Pattern 3 will never be assigned to the channel. It is only a velocity source: every trig has the default velocity 100, and its notes are ignored by the merge, so the notes you hear come only from patterns 1 and 2.
steps.title: Build pattern 3 as a velocity source

steps.caption: Press Channel (3,8), tap pattern slot 2 at (2,2) so patterns 1 and 2 are both assigned, then press the trig merge key at (14,8) twice. Strategy moves from Skip to Only to ALL and the key lights at medium brightness. With Skip every step both patterns share would be silenced; ALL lets every trig sound.
steps.title: Choose Strategy ALL

steps.caption: Hold the velocity merge key (16,8), tap pattern slot 3 at (3,2) and release. Slots 1 and 2 stay lit as the assigned patterns and slot 3 stays dim because it is not assigned: it only supplies the velocity of the merged notes. Note merge stays on its default, Average.
steps.title: Take velocity from pattern 3

steps.caption: Press Play (1,8), listen to two loops and press Play again to stop. The average of each step's degrees is II, IV, VI, IV, which in C major is D, F, A, F. With Lock merged to pent. Off the merged degrees play unchanged: 62, 65, 69, 65 (D F A F) at velocity 100, taken from pattern 3. Compare the On lesson, where the F steps snap to E.
steps.title: Hear the averaged phrase unchanged

steps.caption: Tap the note merge key at (15,8) once; it brightens as Note merge moves from Average to Higher. Press Play (1,8), listen to two loops and press Play again to stop. Higher adds the spread (the highest minus the lowest degree) to the rounded average, so the four steps become degrees IV, VI, VIII and X: F, A, C and E in C major. Lock merged to pent. Off leaves the F alone, so the MIDI strip "MIDI sent in this step" shows 65, 69, 72, 76 at velocity 100. Compare the On lesson, where the first step snaps to E (64).
steps.title: Switch Note merge to Higher and listen

merged-pentatonic-off.title: Lock merged notes to pentatonic: Off

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 (the channel range) with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen and every Mosaic option is at its default. Lock merged to pent. is at its default On. Only pattern 1 exists and is assigned to channel 1; patterns 2 and 3 are built in the next steps.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock merged to pent. and turn E3 right to On (the default). The row shows On.
steps.title: Check Lock merged to pent.

steps.caption: Close the menu. Press Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1) and tap (1,7), (2,5), (3,3) and (4,1) to rewrite its four notes as scale degrees I, III, V, VII (C E G B). The four notes light on the grid.
steps.title: Enter pattern 1

steps.caption: Choose pattern 2 at (2,1), add four trigs on steps 1 to 4 and tap (1,5), (2,3), (3,1) and (4,7): degrees III, V, VII, I (E G B C). Pattern 2 is a second voice that overlaps pattern 1 on every step.
steps.title: Enter pattern 2

steps.caption: Choose pattern 3 at (3,1), add four trigs on steps 1 to 4 and put their notes on the top row, (1,1) to (4,1); the four top-row notes light. Pattern 3 will never be assigned to the channel. It is only a velocity source: every trig has the default velocity 100, and its notes are ignored by the merge, so the notes you hear come only from patterns 1 and 2.
steps.title: Build pattern 3 as a velocity source

steps.caption: Press Channel (3,8), tap pattern slot 2 at (2,2) so patterns 1 and 2 are both assigned, then press the trig merge key at (14,8) twice. Strategy moves from Skip to Only to ALL and the key lights at medium brightness. With Skip every step both patterns share would be silenced; ALL lets every trig sound.
steps.title: Choose Strategy ALL

steps.caption: Hold the velocity merge key (16,8), tap pattern slot 3 at (3,2) and release. Slots 1 and 2 stay lit as the assigned patterns and slot 3 stays dim because it is not assigned: it only supplies the velocity of the merged notes. Note merge stays on its default, Average.
steps.title: Take velocity from pattern 3

steps.caption: Press Play (1,8), listen to two loops and press Play again to stop. The average of each step's degrees is II, IV, VI, IV, which in C major is D, F, A, F. With Lock merged to pent. On, F is not in the C D E G A selection and snaps to the nearer E, so you hear 62, 64, 69, 64 (D E A E) at velocity 100, taken from pattern 3. Compare the Off lesson, which plays F (65) on steps 2 and 4.
steps.title: Hear the averaged phrase snap to pentatonic

steps.caption: Tap the note merge key at (15,8) once; it brightens as Note merge moves from Average to Higher. Press Play (1,8), listen to two loops and press Play again to stop. Higher adds the spread (the highest minus the lowest degree) to the rounded average, so the four steps become degrees IV, VI, VIII and X: F, A, C and E in C major. Lock merged to pent. On snaps F to the nearer E, so the MIDI strip "MIDI sent in this step" shows 64, 69, 72, 76 at velocity 100. Compare the Off lesson, which plays F (65) on the first step.
steps.title: Switch Note merge to Higher and listen

merged-pentatonic-on.title: Lock merged notes to pentatonic: On

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to the example MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. No channel is muted, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press channel button (1,1) and let go after about half a second, well before one second is up. A short press only selects the channel, so the button stays bright and nothing is muted.
steps.title: Select channel 1 without muting

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen: channel 1 plays C, D, E, F (60, 62, 64, 65), and the strip below lists the four notes. Tap Play again to stop.
steps.title: Hear channel one

steps.caption: Hold (1,1) for a full second, then let go. The button dims to show channel 1 is muted; a muted channel still counts as selected.
steps.title: Mute with a long press

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen for about a second and a half: the dimmed channel sends no notes, and the strip below stays empty. Playback keeps running, so the other channels would carry on.
steps.title: Listen to the muted channel

steps.caption: Tap Play to stop. Hold K1 and tap (1,1): the button brightens again, so channel 1 is unmuted.
steps.title: Unmute with K1

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8): with channel 1 unmuted, C, D, E, F (60, 62, 64, 65) sound again. Tap Play to stop.
steps.title: Hear it again

steps.caption: Tap Play. While the phrase sounds, hold (1,1) for a full second: the button dims and the notes stop. The clock keeps running, but no new notes sound for the next second and a half.
steps.title: Mute while it plays

steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap (1,1): the button brightens and the phrase comes back in time with the running pattern, picking up wherever the loop has reached rather than starting over.
steps.title: Bring channel one back

mute-live-resume.title: Mute a channel and bring a running phrase back

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Mute Chord Root. Chord Note Strum (1/2) and Chord Pattern (-> forward) are already assigned; Mute Chord Root is not.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Mute Chord Root and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent to On. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Velocity Mod.
steps.title: Switch Mute Chord Root On

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Velocity Mod and K2 to return, then turn E3 to +10. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The MIDI strip lists four notes, not five: the root C3 (60) is silent, but the chord notes keep their places, E3 (64) half a step in at velocity 60, G3 (67) at one step (70), A3 (69) at 1 1/2 steps (80) and C4 (72) at two steps (90). With Mute Chord Root at X, 60 would sound first at velocity 50.
steps.title: Play without the root

mute-root-retains-slot.title: Remove the root without collapsing time

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI notes 60, 62, 64 and 65. The sequencer is stopped and the Device page for CH01 is showing. The project has never been saved under a name, so no new or newB file exists.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Play (1,8), listen, and press it again to stop. The melody is C, D, E, F: MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65.
steps.title: Hear the original melody

steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns menu, choose PARAMS, then MOSAIC, and scroll to Save project.
steps.title: Find Save project

steps.caption: Press K3 to open the name entry. It starts on the suggested name, new, with OK selected, so press K3 again to accept it. Mosaic writes the project file and its parameter file under that name. Tap K1 to close the menu.
steps.title: Save the default name

steps.caption: Tap K1 and scroll to MOSAIC > Save project once more.
steps.title: Open Save project again

steps.caption: Press K3 to open the name entry. Turn E3 left to the letter row, turn E2 one detent to B and press K3 to add it, so the name reads newB. Turn E3 right to the bottom row, turn E2 right to OK and press K3. A second, separate save is created, and both saves, new and newB, now hold the melody C, D, E, F. Tap K1 to close the menu.
steps.title: Save another name

steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) twice: the first press shows the trig page and the second the note page. Press (4,3) to raise step 4 from F to G. Tap Channel (3,8) to return to the Channel editor and press Play (1,8): the melody is now C, D, E, G, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 67. Press Play again to stop before the idle autosave wait.
steps.title: Edit the melody

steps.caption: Leave Mosaic stopped and untouched for about a minute until the idle autosave runs. A third file, autosave, is written. The saves new and newB are not touched.
steps.title: Let autosave preserve both names

steps.caption: Tap K1 and scroll to MOSAIC > Save project. Press K3 to open the name entry, then press K2 to cancel. No project file changes. Tap K1 to close the menu.
steps.title: Cancel a save

steps.caption: Open Save project again, press K3, then K3 again to accept the name new and confirm replacing it. The save new now holds the edited melody C, D, E, G. The save newB is unchanged and still holds C, D, E, F.
steps.title: Overwrite only the chosen name

steps.caption: Tap K1, then scroll to MOSAIC > Load project.
steps.title: Find Load project

steps.caption: Press K3 to open the file picker, choose newB.ptn and press K3. The original melody returns. Close the menu and press Play to hear MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65.
steps.title: Load the preserved phrase

steps.caption: Load new.ptn the same way. The edited melody plays MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 67. The save newB is still in the file list.
steps.title: Load the overwritten phrase

named-project-roundtrip.title: Keep a named project and recover it

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The sequencer is stopped. A MIDI controller on input port 1, channel 1 is connected and sends relative CC 20: a value of 63 means one step down and 65 one step up. Nothing is mapped yet and the velocity mask is Off (X).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1, choose PARAMS, open Mosaic Midi Mapping and turn E2 to the selected-channel velocity parameter. The selected row reads Selected Ch. Velocity.
steps.title: Find the velocity mask parameter

steps.caption: Hold K1 and press K3 to switch from EDIT to MAP mode. The list now names each parameter by its id, sel_ch_vel for this one, and nothing is mapped yet.
steps.title: Switch to MAP mode

steps.caption: Press K3 to open the map editor. Learn is selected, and the editor lists cc 100, ch 1, dev 1 EMIDI, in 0 to 127, out -1.0 to 1.0, accum no and echo no.
steps.title: Open the map editor

steps.caption: Press K3 on Learn. The row reads LEARNING while the editor waits for the controller.
steps.title: Arm Learn

steps.caption: Move the controller so it sends CC 20. The editor learns it and the cc row reads 20, with input port 1 and channel 1.
steps.title: Move the controller

steps.caption: Turn E2 five clicks to the first number of the in row, Input low, and turn E3 one click right. It reads 1.
steps.title: Set Input low to 1

steps.caption: Turn E2 one click to the second number of the in row, Input high, and turn E3 left until it reads 2. Inputs 1 and 2 are the two steps a relative controller sends.
steps.title: Set Input high to 2

steps.caption: Turn E2 three clicks to accum, past the out row, and turn E3 one click right. Accum reads yes and out still reads -1.0 to 1.0, so each message adds to the value instead of setting it.
steps.title: Turn Accum on

steps.caption: Press K2 to assign. Back in the list, sel_ch_vel now shows 20:1:1, the controller's CC 20 on channel 1 of input port 1.
steps.title: Assign the map

steps.caption: Hold K1 and press K3 to return to EDIT mode, press K2 twice to leave the group, then tap K1 to return to Mosaic. The controller is now mapped to the velocity mask.
steps.title: Return to EDIT mode and leave PARAMS

steps.caption: Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Masks with E2 and press K3, then turn E2 to the Vel cell. It reads X, Off, because nothing has moved it yet.
steps.title: Open the Masks page

steps.caption: Send CC 20 with value 63 once, which leaves Off where it is, then value 65 five times: each message steps the velocity mask up one. The Vel cell rises from X to 4.
steps.title: Turn the controller up

steps.caption: Press Play and stop. The MIDI strip shows all four notes at velocity 4.
steps.title: Hear velocity 4

steps.caption: Send CC 20 with value 63 once more. The Vel cell drops to 3.
steps.title: Turn the controller down

steps.caption: Press Play and stop. The MIDI strip shows all four notes at velocity 3.
steps.title: Hear velocity 3

steps.caption: Patterns 1 and 2 are assigned to channel 1, so channel 1 merges them. Pattern 1 plays scale degrees 1, 3, 5, 7 (C E G B) and pattern 2 plays degrees 3, 5, 7, 1 (E G B C). Note merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (15,8). Pentatonic snapping of merged notes is off: before you try this, tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Lock merged to pent. to Off. Left On (the default), merged notes snap to the five-note pentatonic version of the scale and you hear different pitches.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8). Each note is the mean of the two patterns' degrees (2, 4, 6, 4): D, F, A, F = MIDI 62, 65, 69, 65. Velocity comes from pattern 1.
steps.title: Average note merging

steps.caption: Tap (15,8) once. The button lights brighter and Note mode on the screen reads UP, which is the manual's Higher: the mean plus the gap between the two degrees.
steps.title: Choose Higher

steps.caption: Tap Play. The notes are F, A, C, E = MIDI 65, 69, 72, 76, wider than either source. Velocity still comes from pattern 1. Use Higher to spread the two lines apart for a wider, brighter contour.
steps.title: Higher note merging

note-merge-numeric-output.title: Compare Average and Higher note merging

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI notes 60, 62, 64 and 65. The channel octave is 0 and no step has an octave lock. The Device page is showing. The octave buttons sit along the bottom row, (8,8) for -2 up to (12,8) for +2, with (10,8) the written octave.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Trig params with E2 and press K3. With no step held, tap octave -2 at (8,8): the channel octave is -2 and the whole melody will drop two octaves. Hold step 2 and tap (8,8) too, then keep holding step 2: (8,8) is lit, showing that step's octave.
steps.title: Drop the channel two octaves, and lock step 2 to the same

steps.caption: Release step 2, press Play (1,8), then Stop. The MIDI strip reads 36, 38, 40 and 41 (C1, D1, E1, F1). A lock equal to the channel octave changes nothing you can hear. A low channel octave suits a bass line.
steps.title: A lock equal to the channel octave sounds the same

steps.caption: Hold step 2 and press K2 to clear its lock; play and stop, and all four steps follow the channel octave again. Then hold step 2 and tap octave -1 at (9,8), and keep it held: (9,8) lights while the step is held. Play, then Stop: step 2 sounds at MIDI 50, one octave above the channel setting, and the other steps stay at 36, 40 and 41.
steps.title: Lock step 2 one octave higher

steps.caption: Hold step 2, press K2 to clear its lock, play and stop. Then hold step 2 and tap octave 0 at (10,8). 0 is a lock like any other: step 2 returns to its written octave and sounds two octaves above its neighbours. MIDI 36, 62, 40 and 41.
steps.title: A local octave overrides the channel

steps.caption: Hold step 2 and press K2 to clear its octave lock. All four steps follow the channel octave -2 again: MIDI 36, 38, 40 and 41.
steps.title: K2 restores the channel octave

steps.caption: Hold step 2 and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Step 2 sounds at MIDI 74, an octave above its written note, while the other steps stay at 36, 40 and 41.
steps.title: Lock a step above the written octave

octave-local-over-global.title: Place one step in another octave

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. The Output screen is open on channel 1. Playback has not started, so no note has played yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). Output follows the selected channel and the header changes to CH02. Channel 2 has not played a note, so every row, including Note and Vel / Len, reads NO EVENT.
steps.title: Select channel 2

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1): Output returns to CH01, still NO EVENT because nothing has played. Then tap Play (1,8), let the loop run, and tap Play again to stop. Output now shows the last note channel 1 played. In this run: Note C3 (MIDI 60), Vel / Len 127 / 1.0 (velocity 127, one step long), Step STEP01 (the step it came from), Degree 0 (the first scale degree), Pitch C3 (the pitch in the scale) and Sent C3 (the note actually sent).
steps.title: Play channel 1 and read the rows

output-channel-selection.title: Read Output after selecting a channel

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. Channel tasks is open on channel 1. Playback has not started, so no note has played yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Output and press K3. Six rows describe the last note channel 1 played: Note (the note, and any chord voices), Vel / Len (velocity and length), Step (the step it came from), Degree (the pattern degree, and what merging made of it), Pitch (the pitch in the scale, and the harmony's pitch if Harmony moved it) and Sent (the note actually sent, or why none was: MUTED or REST). Nothing has played yet, so every row reads NO EVENT and there is no cursor; this screen only displays. Play a loop and the rows fill in: see Read Output after selecting a channel.
steps.title: Open Output

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale. Channel tasks is open on channel 1 and playback has not started, so no note has played yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Output and press K3. Six rows describe the last note channel 1 played: Note (the note, and any chord voices), Vel / Len (velocity and length), Step (the step it came from), Degree (the pattern degree, and what merging made of it), Pitch (the pitch in the scale, and the harmony's pitch if Harmony moved it) and Sent (the note actually sent, or why none was: MUTED or REST). Nothing has played yet, so every row reads NO EVENT and there is no cursor; this screen only displays.
steps.title: Open Output before anything has played

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let the loop run, then tap Play again to stop. Output now shows the last note channel 1 played: Note C3 (MIDI 60), Vel / Len 127 / 1.0 (velocity 127, one step long), Step STEP01 (the step it came from), Degree 0 (the first scale degree), Pitch C3 (the pitch in the scale) and Sent C3 (the note actually sent). Look at the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", for the notes behind it.
steps.title: Play, then read the rows

steps.caption: Turn E2 or E3 or press K3: nothing changes, because Output has no cursor. Now hold step 2 at (2,4) without tapping it. Step reads STEP02 HELD and the rows show what step 2 plays: Degree +1, Pitch D3 and Sent D3. Note and Vel / Len still show the last note played. Release the step to return to the latest note.
steps.title: Hold a step to see what it plays

steps.caption: Hold step 40 at (8,6), a step with no trig. Every row reads NO EVENT and Step reads STEP40 HELD: a step without a note borrows nothing from the last note played. Release the step to return to the latest note.
steps.title: A step with no note shows NO EVENT

output-latest-event.title: Read the latest note on Output

steps.caption: In a new empty project with playback stopped and Record off, tap Pattern (5,8), then tap the fourth algorithm button (15,2) for Numeric. The Trig Algorithm screen marks Numeric as SELECTED. Numeric gives a sparse pattern, which makes shifts easy to see. The controls you will use on grid row 8 are Prime (16,8), Move left (10,8), Reset (11,8), Move right (12,8) and Cancel (14,8).
steps.title: Choose Numeric

steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8). The Numeric pattern flashes on the grid and Paint Preview reads Preview PAINTING, Algorithm Numeric, Shift 0 and 8 trigs, on steps 5, 13, 21, 29 and so on. Nothing is painted yet.
steps.title: Prime the pattern

steps.caption: Tap Move right (12,8). Every flashing step moves one step to the right, from step 5 to step 6 and so on, and the Paint Preview screen reads Shift +1.
steps.title: Shift right

steps.caption: Tap Move left (10,8) twice. The first tap takes the flashing steps back to where Prime put them (Shift 0); the second moves them one step left of that, from step 5 to step 4 and so on. The screen reads Shift -1.
steps.title: Two taps left

steps.caption: Tap Reset (11,8). The shift returns to 0 in one tap and the flashing steps are back where Prime put them.
steps.title: Reset the shift

steps.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8). Paint Preview reads Preview OFF and Trigs NONE, and no flashing steps remain. Nothing was painted, so the pattern is unchanged. To keep a shifted rhythm instead, tap Prime again while the steps are flashing; the next two steps do that.
steps.title: Cancel the preview

steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8) again. The same Numeric steps flash again at Shift 0. Prime always starts a new preview, so you can try a rhythm, cancel it and come back to it.
steps.title: Prime again

steps.caption: Tap Move right (12,8) so the preview reads Shift +1, then tap Prime (16,8) while the steps are flashing. Paint Preview now reads Preview OFF and the footer says Pattern painted. The steps stay lit on the pattern grid, one step to the right of where Prime first put them: the shifted rhythm is painted into the pattern.
steps.title: Press Prime again to paint the shifted rhythm

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Pattern 1 is assigned to channel 1 over steps 1 to 4. The sequencer is stopped, so no note is sounding, and three MIDI ports are connected. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen; the next step opens Song.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Song (6,8). The Song page opens (Song Playback, SONG 01) and Song is the lit page button. Panic only works from the button of a page you are not on, so every other page button, including Channel (3,8), is a panic button from here.
steps.title: Open the Song page

steps.caption: From Song, hold the Channel button (3,8) for about two seconds, then release it. Panic sends Note Off to the connected MIDI outputs to release stuck notes. This example starts silent, so you hear no change and the screen stays on Song. Panic leaves playback running. Holding the button of the page you are already on does nothing.
steps.title: Hold Channel for two seconds

panic-from-song-channel.title: Panic by holding Channel while on Song

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Pattern 1 is assigned to channel 1 over steps 1 to 4. The sequencer is stopped, so no note is sounding, and three MIDI ports are connected. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen; the next step opens Song.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Song (6,8). The Song page opens (Song Playback, SONG 01) and Song is the lit page button. Panic only works from the button of a page you are not on, so every other page button, including Pattern (5,8), is a panic button from here.
steps.title: Open the Song page

steps.caption: From Song, hold the Pattern button (5,8) for about two seconds, then release it. Panic sends Note Off to the connected MIDI outputs to release stuck notes. This example starts silent, so you hear no change and the screen stays on Song. Panic leaves playback running. Holding the button of the page you are already on does nothing.
steps.title: Hold Pattern for two seconds

panic-from-song-pattern.title: Panic by holding Pattern while on Song

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The sequencer is stopped and three MIDI ports are connected. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: On Channel, hold step 1 at (1,4) and tap step 24 to set the channel range to steps 1 to 24. Open Pattern (5,8) and tap steps 2, 3 and 4 to clear those trigs, then hold step 1 and tap step 24 to give the one remaining trig a length of 24 steps: four seconds. Press Song (6,8), then Play (1,8). C (MIDI 60) starts and keeps sounding; the MIDI strip "MIDI sent in this step" shows only its Note On.
steps.title: Start one long note

steps.caption: While C sounds, hold Channel (3,8), a page you are not on. Keep holding until Panic cuts the note, then release the key. Allow about two seconds for the hold. Here the note is cut off 1.26 seconds after it starts, before its natural four-second end. That interval starts at note onset, not at the start of the hold. Song playback continues, so C sounds again when the loop comes round. Press Stop at (1,8) to stop the sequence.
steps.title: Hold Channel to panic

panic-stops-sounding-note.title: Panic silences a note that is still sounding

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the test device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97. No Trig params slot is assigned yet, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page. Assign slots in two batches; after each Show result, check the last visible CC before continuing.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Open Trig params, press K2 to enter the slot list and turn E3 to CC 1, press K3, then K2. Check the visible list: slot 1 holds CC 1.
steps.title: Batch 1 — assign CC 1 to slot 1

steps.caption: Turn E2 one slot right, press K2, turn E3 to CC 2 and press K3, then K2. Check the visible list: slot 1 holds CC 1 and slot 2 holds CC 2.
steps.title: Batch 1 — assign CC 2 to slot 2

steps.caption: Repeat for slots 3, 4 and 5 (E2 to the next slot, K2, E3 to the next controller, K3, K2). Check the list shows CC 1 through CC 5 in order; slot 5 holds CC 5.
steps.title: Finish batch 1 — slots 3 to 5

steps.caption: Repeat for CC 6 up to CC 10 on slot 10. Check the list shows CC 1 through CC 10 in order; the final slot holds CC 10.
steps.title: Finish batch 2 — slots 6 to 10

steps.caption: Select slot 10 and keep turning E2 right: it stops at slot 10. Hold step 1 (1,4) and turn E3 to set the value to 0. Turn E2 left well past slot 1: it stops at slot 1. Hold step 2 (2,4) and set the value to 1. Tap Play (1,8). Check the strip below: before its note, step 1 sends CC 10 and step 2 sends CC 1. Tap Play again to stop.
steps.title: Check both ends

parameter-slot-endpoints.title: Use the first and last Trig params slots

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). A pattern has four step pages of 16 steps; here only page 1 has trigs and the Pattern editor has not been opened. Each channel plays a range of steps (start step to end step), which you will set at the end to hear one page at a time.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) to open Pattern Trig and tap steps 17-20, 33-36 and 49-52 (grid rows 5-7, columns 1-4) so each step page holds four steps. All twelve steps light.
steps.title: Add trigs on pages 2 to 4

steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) again to open Pattern Note. Hold K1 and tap (1,7), the root, C: degree 0 for step 1. The cell lights.
steps.title: Hold K1 and set the first note

steps.caption: Keep K1 held and tap (2,6), (3,5) and (4,4): degrees 1, 2 and 3, which are D, E and F. All four notes are lit. Release K1 after entering the values, before browsing the pages.
steps.title: Set the other three notes

steps.caption: Press the first page button (9,8): the four notes are lit on page 1.
steps.title: Check page 1

steps.caption: Press the page buttons (10,8), (11,8) and (12,8) in turn. Each page shows the same four notes lit. Holding K1 while you entered them copied each note to all four pages.
steps.title: Check pages 2 to 4

steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) again to open Pattern Velocity. Hold K1 and tap (1,2), (2,2), (3,2) and (4,2): the second level, velocity 117, on steps 1-4. Press the first page button (9,8): the four cells are lit on page 1. Release K1 after entering the values, before browsing the pages.
steps.title: Copy the dynamics to every page

steps.caption: Press the page buttons (10,8), (11,8) and (12,8) in turn: the same four cells are lit on every page.
steps.title: Check velocity pages 2 to 4

steps.caption: Press Channel (3,8). Hold step 1 and tap step 4 to set the channel range to steps 1-4. Press Play at (1,8), then Stop: C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65), each at velocity 117.
steps.title: Hear page 1

steps.caption: Hold step 17 and tap step 20 to move the range to steps 17-20. Play, then Stop. Then hold step 33 and tap step 36, play and stop again. Both pages play the same four notes at velocity 117.
steps.title: Hear pages 2 and 3

steps.caption: Hold step 49 and tap step 52. Play, then Stop: page 4 plays C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocity 117 too, so every page matches.
steps.title: Hear page 4

pattern-copy-groups.title: Copy notes and dynamics across the four step pages

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Channel editor is open and the Pattern editor has not been opened. On Pattern Note the range buttons on row 8 are range-up (14,8), centre (15,8) and range-down (16,8). A press moves the window one degree up or down, a long press jumps to the top or bottom, and the centre button returns to the root page. Pattern Velocity has only two range buttons, (15,8) toward the top page and (16,8) toward the lower page, as the next lesson shows.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) twice to open Pattern Note for pattern 1. The seven rows are scale degrees, with the root on the bottom row. Tap (4,1), the top row of step 4's column. Press Play at (1,8), then Stop: step 4 now plays degree 6, MIDI 71, while steps 1-3 stay 60, 62, 64.
steps.title: Choose a scale degree

steps.caption: Tap range-up (14,8), then tap (4,1): step 4 is now MIDI 72, the next C. Play to check, then Stop. Tap range-up once more, then tap (4,1): step 4 is MIDI 74. Play to check, then Stop.
steps.title: Move the range up twice

steps.caption: Tap range-down (16,8): the window moves down one degree. Tap (4,1): step 4 is MIDI 72 again. Play, then Stop. Tap range-down once more, then tap (4,1): step 4 is back to MIDI 71. Play, then Stop.
steps.title: Move the range down twice

steps.caption: Hold range-up (14,8) for about a second: the window jumps to its highest position. Tap (4,1): step 4 plays MIDI 83. Tap range-up again: the window cannot go higher, so (4,1) still plays MIDI 83.
steps.title: Jump to the top, which is a limit

steps.caption: Hold range-down (16,8) for about a second: the window jumps to its lowest position. Tap (4,7), the bottom row: step 4 plays MIDI 48. Tap range-down again: the window cannot go lower, so (4,7) still plays MIDI 48.
steps.title: Jump to the bottom, which is a limit

steps.caption: Tap the centre button at (15,8): the window returns to the root page, with the root on the bottom row. Tap (4,4), degree 3: step 4 plays MIDI 65 and the original phrase 60, 62, 64, 65 is back.
steps.title: Return to the central range

pattern-note-range.title: Shape notes across the grid range

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1-4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Channel editor is open and the Pattern editor has not been opened. On Pattern Velocity the range buttons on row 8 differ from Pattern Note, which has three: here there are two, range-up at (15,8), toward the 127-68 page, and range-down at (16,8), toward the 58-0 page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Pattern (5,8) three times to open Pattern Velocity. Each row of a step's column is a velocity level, 127 at the top. Tap (4,1). Press Play at (1,8), then Stop: step 4 plays at velocity 127 while steps 1-3 keep 127, 117, 107.
steps.title: Make a strong accent

steps.caption: Tap down the column of step 4 and press Play, then Stop, after each tap: (4,2) is 117, (4,3) 107, (4,4) 97, (4,5) 87, (4,6) 78 and (4,7) 68. At (4,7) step 4 plays at 68; the other steps are unchanged.
steps.title: Walk down the velocity column

steps.caption: Tap range-down (16,8): the window moves down one level. Tap (4,1): step 4 plays at 117, the level that was second from the top. Play, then Stop. Tap range-down again and tap (4,1): 107. Then tap range-up (15,8) to move the window up one level and tap (4,1): 117 again.
steps.title: Move the velocity range

steps.caption: Hold range-down (16,8) for about a second: the window jumps to the lower page, 58 at the top down to 0 at the bottom. Tap (4,1): step 4 plays at 58.
steps.title: Jump to the lower page

steps.caption: Tap down the column of step 4 to (4,4), playing after each tap: (4,2) is 48, (4,3) 39 and (4,4) 29. At (4,4) step 4 plays at velocity 29.
steps.title: Go quieter

steps.caption: Tap down to (4,5) and (4,6), playing after each tap: (4,5) is 19 and (4,6) is 9. At velocity 9 step 4 still sounds, only very softly: all four notes are in the MIDI strip.
steps.title: Almost silent

steps.caption: Tap (4,7), velocity 0, and play. Step 4 is silent: the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", shows only three notes, 60, 62 and 64. A velocity of 0 turns the attack into a rest.
steps.title: Turn an attack into a rest

steps.caption: Tap range-down (16,8) again: the window is already at its lowest page, so (4,7) is still velocity 0 and step 4 stays silent. Then hold range-up (15,8) for about a second: the window jumps back to the top page, 127 down to 68. Tap (4,1): step 4 plays again at velocity 127.
steps.title: Restore full velocity

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major through the test MIDI device. The channel range is steps 1-4, the tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Lock all to pentatonic is Off. Lock all to pentatonic forces every note you play onto a five-note subset of the chosen scale, so each scale step below changes which five notes survive.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Open the Pattern editor (5,8), which starts on the trig page. Tap steps 5, 6 and 7 on the trig row, (5,4), (6,4) and (7,4). Press (5,8) again for the note page and press the rising diagonal (1,7), (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2), (7,1): one note per step, scale degrees I-VII, C D E F G A B. The note page now shows a rising diagonal.
steps.title: Extend the pattern to seven steps

steps.caption: Press (5,8) for the velocity page and tap (5,1), (6,2) and (7,3): the velocity bars for steps 5, 6 and 7 light up.
steps.title: Set the velocities of steps 5 to 7

steps.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8), hold step 1 (1,4) and tap step 7 (7,4). Steps 1 to 7 light up and step 8 stays dark, so the channel range is steps 1-7.
steps.title: Set the range to seven steps

steps.caption: Press Play and listen to two loops with Lock all to pentatonic at its default Off: all seven plain C major degrees sound, 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71.
steps.title: Hear the plain major scale

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, scroll to Lock all to pentatonic and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.
steps.title: Turn Lock all to pentatonic on

steps.caption: Scroll down to Lock random to pent. and turn E3 left to Off, then do the same for Lock merged to pent. Both rows read Off, so Lock all to pentatonic is the only option that can change a pitch.
steps.title: Switch off the other two locks

steps.caption: Press K2 to step back, then K1 to close the menu, and play the seven steps again: 60, 62, 64, 64, 67, 69, 72. Major keeps degrees 1/2/3/5/6 (C D E G A). F falls to E and B rises to C because only those five are allowed.
steps.title: Snap major to pentatonic

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent and press K3. The Scale row reads Harmonic Major.
steps.title: Pick Harmonic Major

steps.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Harmonic Major keeps the same degrees as Major, 1/2/3/5/6, but its sixth is A-flat: 60, 62, 64, 64, 67, 68, 72. F falls to E, A-flat stays and B rises to C.
steps.title: Step to Harmonic Major

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Minor and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. The minor family keeps degrees 1/3/4/5/7 (C E-flat F G B-flat): 60, 63, 63, 65, 67, 67, 70. D snaps up to E-flat and A-flat snaps down to G.
steps.title: Minor uses its own five notes

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Harmonic Minor and press K3, return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play. Then open the Scale Editor again, turn E3 one more detent and press K3: the Scale row reads Melodic Minor.
steps.title: Pick Harmonic Minor, then Melodic Minor

steps.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Harmonic Minor and Melodic Minor give the same pitches: 60, 63, 63, 65, 67, 67, 71. Only the top note differs from Minor, B-flat becoming B. In Harmonic Minor A-flat snaps down to G; in Melodic Minor A sits exactly between G and B, and an equal-distance note snaps to the lower pitch, so it also lands on G.
steps.title: Hear Harmonic and Melodic Minor

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Dorian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Dorian keeps degrees 1/2/4/5/7 (C D F G B-flat): 60, 62, 62, 65, 67, 70, 70. E-flat falls to D and A rises to B-flat.
steps.title: Step to Dorian

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Phrygian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Phrygian keeps degrees 1/3/4/6/7 (C E-flat F A-flat B-flat): 60, 60, 63, 65, 68, 68, 70. D-flat falls to C and G rises to A-flat.
steps.title: Step to Phrygian

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Lydian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Lydian keeps degrees 2/3/5/6/7 (D E G A B), so the tonic C snaps down to the B below it: 59, 62, 64, 67, 67, 69, 71.
steps.title: See the lower boundary snap

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Mixolydian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Mixolydian keeps degrees 1/2/4/5/6 (C D F G A): 60, 62, 65, 65, 67, 69, 69. E rises to F and B-flat falls to A.
steps.title: Step to Mixolydian

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 one detent to Locrian and press K3. Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play two loops. Locrian keeps degrees 2/3/4/6/7 (D-flat E-flat F A-flat B-flat), so the tonic C snaps up to D-flat and G-flat snaps down to F: 61, 61, 63, 65, 65, 68, 70.
steps.title: Step to Locrian

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, scroll to Lock all to pentatonic and turn E3 left to Off. The row reads Off.
steps.title: Turn Lock all to pentatonic off

steps.caption: Close the menu and play. All seven plain Locrian pitches return: 60, 61, 63, 65, 66, 68, 70. Musical tip: leave Lock all to pentatonic On when a pattern is random or generative, so every note lands in a five-note set that stays consonant in any scale, and Off when you want the full seven-note colour.
steps.title: All seven Locrian pitches return

steps.title: Open the Device page

steps.caption: Turn E3 until the Device row reads Doubledecker. The footer says “Press K3 to confirm”, so this is still a draft.

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks → Device again. The Device row still reads Doubledecker without a confirmation prompt.

steps.title: Open the Device page

steps.caption: Turn E3 until the Device row reads Oilcan 1. The footer says “Press K3 to confirm”, so this is still a draft.
steps.title: Choose Oilcan 1

steps.caption: Press K3 to apply Oilcan 1. The Device row remains Oilcan 1 and the confirmation prompt clears.

steps.title: Open the Device page

steps.caption: Turn E3 until the Device row reads Polyperc 1. The footer says “Press K3 to confirm”, so this is still a draft.
steps.title: Choose Polyperc 1

steps.caption: Press K3 to apply Polyperc 1. The Device row remains Polyperc 1 and the confirmation prompt clears.

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The sequencer is stopped and the norns shows channel 1's Device screen.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), hold step 1 at (1,4) and tap step 64 at (16,7): the range is now four rows of sixteen steps, bars 1 to 4 on rows 4 to 7. Press Pattern (5,8) and tap steps 2, 3 and 4 to clear those trigs, then tap the first step of each beat: (5,4), (9,4), (13,4), then (1,5), (5,5), (9,5), (13,5), and the same four columns on rows 6 and 7. Step 1 is already lit. Press Channel (3,8): sixteen trigs are lit, four in each row.
steps.title: Set a 64-step range and add the main hits
