Channel 2 (MIDI channel 2) has one anchor trig on step 5 and is channel 1's Interlock leader. Interlock removes channel 1's addition on step 5, so channel 1's grid shows steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 lit. Clock Rate is /1 and Swing is not set (X).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E1 to Channel tasks, select Clock with E2 and press K3. Select the local feel Mode with E2, set Swing with E3 and press K3. Feel source now reports CHANNEL; this row is read-only. Select Swing with E2, turn E3 to 25 and press K3 to apply. Every second step plays a quarter of a step late, while Interlock still removes the addition on step 5.
steps.title: Set Swing to 25

steps.caption: Open Merge Shape > Interlock: Status is still ON and step 5 is still removed (step 7 is lit). Swing did not change the merge.
steps.title: Interlock is still on

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), listen to a loop or two and tap Play again to stop. Step 5 is still silent. Steps 2 and 4 sound a quarter of a step (about 42 ms) late: in the MIDI strip they sit near 208 ms and 542 ms instead of 167 ms and 500 ms, while steps 1 and 3 stay put (0 and 333 ms) and the added step 7 plays quietly (velocity 70) at 1000 ms. Swing moves the notes but the merge result stays the same.
steps.title: Hear the swung notes

swing-interlock-pulse-times.title: Swing a merged part: Interlock still removes step 5

steps.caption: The norns matrix and toolkit mods are installed and enabled, and the norns tempo is 90 BPM. Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) through a CC device with Rate /1, the sequencer is stopped, and the Matrix has no routes yet. The Device page for CH01 is showing.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open MODS > MATRIX. Choose MOSAIC CH 1: CC DEVICE and select Fixed Note, the parameter the LFO will drive. Press K3 to open Fixed Note's sources and turn E2 to lfo 1; its row shows dashes, no depth yet. Hold E3 turning right until lfo 1's depth reads 1.00, so the LFO controls Fixed Note at full strength.
steps.title: Route lfo 1 to Fixed Note at full depth

steps.caption: Open the parameters list, choose toolkit lfo 1 (PARAMETERS / lfo 1) and select clocked, which makes the LFO follow the tempo instead of running in seconds. Press K3 to switch it on: clocked shows a filled marker.
steps.title: Clock the LFO to the tempo

steps.caption: Turn E2 down one row to Beats, the LFO period in beats. It reads 1/4. Turn E3 right until Beats reads 4, a period of four beats. Turn E2 down two rows to Shape, which still reads sine.
steps.title: Set the period and the shape

steps.caption: Turn E3 two detents to choose Pulse. Shape now reads pulse.
steps.title: Choose Pulse

steps.caption: Tap K1 and press Play. The LFO now alternates every two beats, half of its four-beat period: eight steps at MIDI 127, the Fixed Note pitch, then eight steps of the authored phrase, 60, 62, 64, 65, repeating. The MIDI strip lists the notes in that order.
steps.title: Play the phrase

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. The Scale page is open on the transposition fader along the bottom row. Global transposition is +4 (set at (13,8)). Scale-track step 2 has a transposition lock of 0, the fader's centre at (12,8), and step 1 has a lock of -12, the lowest value at (9,8). The MIDI strip reads 48, 62, 64, 65: step 1 sounds an octave below its written note, while steps 2 to 4 ignore the global +4 because the zero lock on step 2 holds for the rest of the loop. This is how you keep one part of a song at its written pitch while the rest is transposed.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and press the right end of the fader, (16,8), twelve times, playing as you go if you like. Each press adds one semitone, from -12 up to 0. A lock of 0 is an explicit lock: it overrides the global +4, so step 1 plays MIDI 60 and not 64.
steps.title: Walk step 1 up to an explicit zero

steps.caption: Keep holding step 1 and press (16,8) twelve more times. Each press adds one semitone, up to +12. The first note jumps an octave to MIDI 72. Steps 2 to 4 still follow the zero lock on step 2 and stay at MIDI 62, 64 and 65.
steps.title: Walk on up to +12

steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and press K2 to remove its lock. Step 1 now follows the global +4 and plays MIDI 64. The zero lock on step 2 is still active for steps 2 to 4, so the loop plays MIDI 64, 62, 64 and 65.
steps.title: Clear the lock on step 1

transpose-explicit-zero-and-clear.title: Lock transposition without losing the global setting

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. The Scale page is open on the transposition fader along the bottom row. Global transposition is +4. Scale-track step 2 has a transposition lock of 0, the fader's centre at (12,8), and step 1 has just been locked to -12 with one tap on the lowest value, (9,8), while it was held. The MIDI strip reads 48, 62, 64, 65.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and tap the centre of the fader, (12,8), once. The lock moves from -12 straight to 0 with no walking. A lock of 0 overrides the global +4, so step 1 plays MIDI 60 and not 64.
steps.title: Jump to an explicit zero

steps.caption: Hold step 1 and tap (15,8) once. The lock jumps to +12, and the first note sounds an octave up at MIDI 72. Steps 2 to 4 still follow the zero lock on step 2, MIDI 62, 64 and 65.
steps.title: Jump up an octave

steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and press K2 to remove its lock. Step 1 follows the global +4 again and plays MIDI 64, so the loop plays 64, 62, 64 and 65.
steps.title: Clear the lock on step 1

transpose-lock-direct-taps.title: Jump a transposition lock straight to a value

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the example MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Global transposition is 0, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8) to open the Scale Editor, then tap Play (1,8). One step lasts about a sixth of a second at 90 BPM, so the four-note phrase repeats about every two thirds of a second; exact timing does not matter. While it loops, press (16,8) on the transposition fader once. The screen shows Scale overview with Transpose +1: the note sounding at that moment keeps its pitch and length, and the next notes play a semitone higher, MIDI 61, 63, 65 and 66, as the MIDI strip lists.
steps.title: Press +1 while it plays

steps.caption: After a few more notes press (9,8) to set -12. Transpose reads -12: again the sounding note is untouched and the next notes drop an octave below the written pitches, 48, 50, 52 and 53.
steps.title: Press -12 a few notes later

steps.caption: Tap Play to stop. Transpose still reads -12, and in the strip every note-on has its own matching note-off.
steps.title: Stop

steps.caption: Both edits changed only the next onset: the notes before the first edit are 60, 62, 64, 65, then 61, 63, 65, 66, then 48, 50, 52, 53, and each held note finished at its own pitch and length.
steps.title: The whole run

transpose-next-onset.title: Transpose the next note without cutting the current one

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the example MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Global transposition is 0, the Song editor holds only slot 1, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Song (6,8) to open the Song editor. Hold slot 1 at (1,1) and press slot 2 at (2,1), then release both, and tap slot 2. Slot 2 is selected and bright, slot 1 is lit: slot 2 holds a copy of the melody.
steps.title: Copy slot 1 to slot 2

steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8). Press the left end of the transposition fader at (9,8) to set -12, then press (16,8) fourteen times to reach +2. The Scale overview shows Transpose +2 for this slot.
steps.title: Raise the copy by two semitones

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen, then tap Play to stop. The copy loops D, E, F sharp, G: MIDI 62, 64, 66 and 67 in the strip below.
steps.title: Hear the copy

steps.caption: Press Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and tap Play (1,8). Slot 1 still loops C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65): the transposition belongs to the copy only. Tap Play to stop.
steps.title: Slot 1 keeps its pitches

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device on OUT 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major at 90 BPM, with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Trig params screen is open on its parameter list, showing Fixed Note; every slot is empty (None).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Fixed Note to the first slot and K2 to return. With no step held, turn E3 to 60 (C3). Play, then stop: the MIDI strip lists C3 (60) on all four steps.
steps.title: Set the channel default

steps.caption: Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 to 63 (D#3) and release. A value set on a held step is a lock. Play, then stop: step 2 plays 63 and the other steps keep the default, 60, 63, 60, 60.
steps.title: Lock one step

steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 down to 0 and release. Play, then stop: 0, 63, 60, 60. Zero is a real note, not Off.
steps.title: Lock a second step

steps.caption: Hold step 4, turn E3 down to X (Off) and release: a step at X has no lock, so it follows the default. Then, with no step held, turn E3 up five detents to 65. Play, then stop: 0, 63, 65, 65. Steps 1 and 2 keep their locks.
steps.title: Raise the default beneath the locks

steps.caption: Hold step 2 at (2,4), press K2 and release: its lock is cleared and step 2 returns to the default. Play, then stop: 0, 65, 65, 65. Step 1 keeps its MIDI 0 lock; steps 2 to 4 follow the default. To lock a CC value the same way, see Brighten the last note with a cutoff lock.
steps.title: Let the default apply again

trig-parameter-locks.title: Lock a value, then clear just that step

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and the Device page for CH01 is showing. Channel 2 is not set up yet: you will route the same pattern to it as a timing reference. Trigless locks is at its default On.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Trigless locks and turn E3 left to Off. The row reads Off.
steps.title: Turn Trigless locks off

steps.caption: Press K2, then K1 to leave the menu. Set up channel 2 as the timing reference: tap (2,1), open Channel tasks > Device, point it at the second MIDI port, give it pattern 1 at (1,2) and range steps 1-4 (hold (1,4), tap (4,4)). Both channels use pattern 1, so pattern-trig edits affect both. Probability and CC locks on channel 1 do not change channel 2. Then tap channel 1 (1,1), open Channel tasks > Trig params and assign CC 1 to the first slot.
steps.title: Assign CC 1

steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm CC 1 and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held. Release the step.
steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24

steps.caption: Do the same on the other steps. Hold step 2 and turn E3 to 48, hold step 3 for 72 and hold step 4 for 96. Slot 1 reads 96 with the L while step 4 is held, so every step now carries its own CC 1 value.
steps.title: Lock steps 2 to 4 to 48, 72 and 96

steps.caption: Assign Trig probability to the second slot, so you can silence channel 1's notes and see only its CC 1 stream beside channel 2's steady notes.
steps.title: Add Trig probability

steps.caption: Set Trig probability to 0 so channel 1's notes never sound, and play two loops. All four steps still have trigs, so CC 1 still goes out at every step (24, 48, 72, 96) even with Trigless locks Off: look for those four CC values each loop in the MIDI strip, beside channel 2's steady notes. A probability of 0 is not a rest: only a removed trig is.
steps.title: Probability 0 silences the notes, not the locks

steps.caption: Open the Pattern editor (5,8), tap step 3 to remove its trig, and return to the Channel editor (3,8). Play. With Trigless locks Off, a lock on a step with no trig is skipped: the MIDI strip shows CC 1 sending 24, 48 and 96 but not 72, the value on step 3. Pattern 1 is shared: channel 2 also loses its E note on step 3 and now plays C, D, F; its timing continues through that rest.
steps.title: Remove the third trig

steps.caption: Hold step 4 and turn E3 to set its Trig probability lock to 100, then play. Step 4's note (F3, 65) now sounds, with its CC 1 lock (96) sent just before it. Steps 1 and 2 stay silent, and step 3 still sends no value. The scene Keep automation on rests plays the same steps with Trigless locks On, for comparison.
steps.title: Keep a lock ahead of its accepted note

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and the Device page for CH01 is showing. Channel 2 is not set up yet: you will route the same pattern to it as a timing reference. Trigless locks is at its default On.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Trigless locks reads On, its default, so locks on steps without a trig will still be sent. Press K2, then K1 to leave the menu. Set up channel 2 as the timing reference: tap (2,1), open Channel tasks > Device, point it at the second MIDI port, give it pattern 1 at (1,2) and range steps 1-4 (hold (1,4), tap (4,4)). Both channels use pattern 1, so pattern-trig edits affect both. Probability and CC locks on channel 1 do not change channel 2. Then tap channel 1 (1,1), open Channel tasks > Trig params and assign CC 1 to the first slot.
steps.title: Check Trigless locks, then set up the channels

steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm CC 1 and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held. Release the step.
steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24

steps.caption: Do the same on the other steps. Hold step 2 and turn E3 to 48, hold step 3 for 72 and hold step 4 for 96. Slot 1 reads 96 with the L while step 4 is held, so every step now carries its own CC 1 value.
steps.title: Lock steps 2 to 4 to 48, 72 and 96

steps.caption: Assign Trig probability to the second slot, so you can silence channel 1's notes and see only its CC 1 stream beside channel 2's steady notes.
steps.title: Add Trig probability

steps.caption: Set Trig probability to 0 so channel 1's notes never sound, and play two loops. All four steps have trigs, so CC 1 goes out at every step (24, 48, 72, 96) even though no note plays: look for those four CC values each loop in the MIDI strip, beside channel 2's steady notes.
steps.title: Probability 0 silences the notes, not the locks

steps.caption: Open the Pattern editor (5,8), tap step 3 to remove its trig, and return to the Channel editor (3,8). Play. With Trigless locks On, a lock on a step with no trig is still sent: the MIDI strip shows CC 1 still sending 72 at step 3, so automation keeps moving through rests, for example a filter sweep under a sparse rhythm. Pattern 1 is shared: channel 2 also loses its E note on step 3 and now plays C, D, F; its timing continues through that rest.
steps.title: Remove the third trig

steps.caption: Hold step 4 and turn E3 to set its Trig probability lock to 100, then play. Step 4's note (F3, 65) now sounds, with its CC 1 lock (96) sent just before it. Steps 1 and 2 stay silent, and step 3 still sends its 72. The scene Skip automation on rests plays the same steps with Trigless locks Off, for comparison.
steps.title: Keep a lock ahead of its accepted note

steps.caption: The selected UI motion option row reads Off.
steps.title: Turn motion Off

steps.caption: With UI motion Off, the header picture stays in its resting pose while the clock continues. Compare the waiting frames: readable values stay in place.
steps.title: Observe the still CLOCK miniature

steps.caption: With motion Off, playback sends C, D, E, F twice, then a final C before Stop. The first eight notes have their usual sixteenth-note lengths; Stop releases the final note early.
steps.title: Hear the same phrase with motion Off

steps.caption: The selected UI motion option row reads On.
steps.title: Turn motion On

steps.caption: With UI motion On, the header picture changes pose as the musical clock advances. The waiting frames show this decoration moving; it does not start playback.
steps.title: Observe the moving CLOCK miniature

steps.caption: With motion On, playback sends the same C, D, E, F phrase twice, then a final C before Stop. The first eight notes retain their usual lengths; Stop releases the final note early, just as with motion Off.
steps.title: Hear the same phrase with motion On

steps.caption: Compare Off and On: the same notes, velocities and note lengths play at the same musical times. Only the screen decoration changes.
steps.title: Compare complete Off and On MIDI

ui-motion-public-frames.title: See screen motion in its pixels

steps.caption: Channel 1 has two patterns assigned with different velocities for four notes: 127, 117, 107, 97 and 100, 100, 100, 100. Its notes come from a third pattern, shown on the screen as Note mode PAT 4 (pattern 4 is not assigned to the channel; all its notes are MIDI 67), so only velocity changes. Velocity merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (16,8).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8). Each velocity is the mean of the two sources, for example (127 + 100) / 2 = 114, so the four notes sound at 114, 109, 104 and 99. Read the velocities in the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step": every note is MIDI 67 and only the velocity changes.
steps.title: Average velocity merging

steps.caption: Tap (16,8) once, without K1 (with K1 held the same button sets length merge instead). The button lights brighter and Velocity mode on the screen reads UP, which is the manual's Higher: the mean plus the gap between the sources.
steps.title: Choose Higher

steps.caption: Tap Play. The four velocities in the MIDI strip are 127, 126, 111 and 102. The first is 114 + 27 = 141, limited to 127. Use Higher to accent a step.
steps.title: Higher velocity merging

steps.caption: Tap (16,8) again. The button changes again and Velocity mode reads DOWN, the manual's Lower: twice the lowest source minus the mean.
steps.title: Choose Lower

steps.caption: Tap Play. The four velocities in the MIDI strip are 86, 91, 96 and 95. The first is 2 x 100 - 114 = 86. Use Lower for ghost notes.
steps.title: Lower velocity merging

steps.caption: Tap (16,8) once more. The modes cycle Average, Higher, Lower and back: tap Play and the MIDI strip shows the velocities 114, 109, 104 and 99 again.
steps.title: Return to Average

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major, stopped. Clock Rate is /1 and no Swing or Shuffle is set. Channel 1 is selected and its Clock page is open. Your goal is to give channel 1 its own shuffle feel. Rate is the first row of a vertical list.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E2 left until Rate is selected, the first row (it reads /1, the default). The list shows Rate, Feel source and Swing type together, so you can read the channel's clock and feel settings at a glance.
steps.title: Read the Clock settings together

steps.caption: Tap K1 twice: the first tap opens the norns menu and the second closes it, and the page keeps your place. Turn E2 to Swing type. It reads X: this channel has no feel of its own yet.
steps.title: Select Swing type

steps.caption: Turn E3 left as far as it goes and press K3. It stays at X. X means this channel follows the global feel set in Song > Tempo and feel.
steps.title: Follow the global feel

steps.caption: Turn E3 right to Shuffle and press K3. Shuffle adds its own rows below Swing type for setting this channel's feel.
steps.title: Choose Shuffle

steps.caption: Keep turning E2 right. The list stops on its last row, Shuffle amount (0), and does not wrap round however far you turn.
steps.title: Reach the end of the list

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Nothing else exists yet: no second pattern, no scale change, no second channel and one song slot. Trig merge modes decide what happens when two patterns on one channel both have a trig on a step: Skip (the default) drops those steps, Only keeps only those steps, and All keeps every step.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Do these in order. 1) Tap Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 2 at (2,1) and tap steps 1 and 3 on Pattern Trig. 2) Tap Pattern (5,8) again for Pattern Note and raise step 1 to (1,3) and step 3 to (3,1): degrees 4 and 6. 3) Tap Scale (4,8), tap slot 2 at (2,3), turn E2 to Root and E3 two detents up to D, then press K3: D major is applied. 4) Tap Channel (3,8) and tap pattern slot (2,2) to assign pattern 2 to channel 1 beside pattern 1. 5) Press Play, then Stop. Skip drops steps 1 and 3, where both patterns have a trig, so only steps 2 and 4 play: E and G of D major (MIDI 64 and 67) at velocities 117 and 97.
steps.title: Build pattern 2 and hear Skip

steps.caption: Tap the trig merge button (14,8) twice to move from Skip through Only to All. The button lights at medium brightness.
steps.title: Move the trig merge to All

steps.caption: Hold the velocity merge button (16,8) and tap pattern 1 at (1,2) to take velocities from pattern 1, then press Play and Stop. All four steps play. Steps 2 and 4 come from pattern 1 alone (E and G, 64 and 67). Steps 1 and 3 have a trig in both patterns, so their notes are the average of the two patterns' scale degrees: step 1 averages D (degree 0) and A (degree 4) to F# (66), and step 3 averages F# and C# to A (69). The result is MIDI 66, 64, 69, 67 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97.
steps.title: Merge all, with pattern 1 velocities

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1), turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device and press K3. The Device page now reads CH02.
steps.title: Select channel 2

steps.caption: On the Device page choose the same device on MIDI port 2 and MIDI channel 2 (turn E3 or E2 to each setting) and press K3 to apply. Tap pattern slot (2,2) for pattern 2, hold step 1 and tap step 4 to give channel 2 the range steps 1-4, then turn E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Masks and press K3. The screen reads Note Masks for CH02.
steps.title: Route channel 2 and open its Masks

steps.caption: On Masks, hold step 3 and play MIDI note 76 at velocity 90 on a MIDI keyboard or controller to lock it to that step. Tap channel 1 at (1,1) and press Play, then Stop. Both channels sound, each on its own port: channel 1 plays 66, 64, 69, 67 as before, and channel 2 plays pattern 2: MIDI 69 (A) on step 1 and your 76 on step 3.
steps.title: Add a keyboard note to channel 2

steps.caption: Do these in order. 1) Tap Song (6,8) and set the global length to 4 steps: tap (2,7), which sets 1, then (8,7) three times. 2) Copy slot 1 to slot 2: hold slot (1,1) and tap (2,1), then tap (2,1) to select slot 2. 3) Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave-up (11,8), so slot 2 plays an octave higher. 4) Tap Song (6,8), select slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play. The four-step phrase plays, then repeats an octave higher in slot 2: MIDI 66, 64, 69, 67, then 78, 76, 81, 79 on channel 1, while channel 2 plays its A and 76 in both slots.
steps.title: Copy slot 1 to slot 2 an octave up

workflow-compose-two-channels.title: Build two channels: merge patterns, route a second part and chain slots

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Nothing else exists yet: no second pattern, no scale change and no second channel.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8) to open Pattern Trig, choose pattern 2 at (2,1) and tap steps 1 and 3. Both steps light on the grid.
steps.title: Add trigs to pattern 2

steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8) again for Pattern Note. Raise step 1 to the cell (1,4) and step 3 to (3,6): these are the scale degrees 4 and 6 that pattern 2 plays on those steps. Both cells light.
steps.title: Raise their notes

steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8) and tap slot 2 at (2,3). Turn E2 to Root, turn E3 two detents up to D and press K3. The Scale screen names slot 2 and D major is applied.
steps.title: Apply D major

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8) and tap pattern slot (2,2). Pattern 2 now plays on channel 1 beside pattern 1, and both slot buttons are lit.
steps.title: Give pattern 2 to channel 1

steps.caption: Press Play, then Stop. By default overlapping trigs are skipped, so steps 1 and 3, where both patterns have a trig, drop out. Only steps 2 and 4 play: look at the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", for E and G of D major, MIDI 64 and 67, at velocities 117 and 97.
steps.title: Hear Skip

workflow-patterns-and-scale.title: Add a second pattern in D major

steps.caption: Channel 1 has patterns 1 and 2 merged in All mode (both patterns contribute their notes, with pattern 1 supplying velocity) in D major. Check the four-step result on port 1/channel 1: MIDI 66, 64, 69, 67 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97. Channel 2 has not been set up yet.
steps.title: Checkpoint 1 — hear the existing phrase

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1), open Channel tasks > Device with E1/E2 and K3. Check the screen header reads DEVICE CH02. A channel is the numbered MIDI route on an output.
steps.title: Checkpoint 2 — select channel 2

steps.caption: On Device, choose the same device on port 2 and MIDI channel 2, then press K3 to apply. A port is a MIDI output; the channel number is the route the receiver listens to. Assign pattern 2 at (2,2), set its range to steps 1–4 by holding step 1 and tapping step 4, then check Merge modes shows CH02 and Patterns 02 and slot (2,2) remains lit.
steps.title: Checkpoint 3 — assign a separate output

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Masks and press K3. Check the screen reads Note Masks for CH02; this is where the channel's note values and held-step masks are edited.
steps.title: Checkpoint 4 — open channel 2 Masks

steps.caption: On Masks, hold step 3 and play MIDI note 76 at velocity 90; a mask is an override stored on the held step. Release the key and step. Select channel 1 at (1,1), press Play (1,8), then Stop. Check the MIDI strip: port 1/channel 1 keeps MIDI 66, 64, 69, 67 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97; port 2/channel 2 plays MIDI 69 (A) on step 1 and MIDI 76 on step 3. The complete route for this scene is [MIDI Keyboard Input](#midi-keyboard-input/workflow-second-channel).
steps.title: Checkpoint 5 — add one note and verify both routes

workflow-second-channel.title: Add one keyboard note and check both channel outputs

steps.caption: Both channels play four steps. Channel 1 plays 66, 64, 69, 67 and channel 2 plays its A (69) and 76. The song has one slot, Song 01, at the full global length of 64 steps.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8). Tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) three times. The Playback screen reads Global length 4: the song is one four-step phrase.
steps.title: Set the song length to 4

steps.caption: Hold slot (1,1) and tap (2,1) to copy slot 1 into slot 2, then tap (2,1) to select slot 2. The Slot setup screen names Song 02 and the footer reads Song sequence 2 selected.
steps.title: Copy slot 1 to slot 2

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). The octave button lights and the footer reads Ch. 1 octave: 1: channel 1 will play one octave higher in this slot.
steps.title: Raise slot 2 an octave

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), select slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play, then Stop. The four-step phrase plays, then repeats an octave higher in slot 2. The MIDI strip shows 66, 64, 69, 67, then 78, 76, 81, 79 on channel 1, while channel 2 plays its A and 76 in both slots.

feature:adding-melodic-notes-over-harmon.human_outcome: All four steps return to G3; the channel default remains after the exceptions clear.
feature:adding-melodic-notes-over-harmon.practice_prompt:
1. With no step held on Note Masks, turn E3 clockwise until Note reads G3 (MIDI 67). All four steps use this channel default.
2. Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 clockwise to C4 (MIDI 72), then release it. Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 clockwise to D4 (MIDI 74), then release it. These two exceptions override the default.
3. Hold step 1 again, press K2 and release the step. Only its exception clears: step 1 returns to G3, while step 2 keeps D4.
4. With no step held, hold K1, press K2 and release K1. All step exceptions clear together; the channel default remains G3.

Use one-step clearing to remove an unwanted variation, or K1 + K2 to restore the common pitch across the channel.

feature:locks:mask-default-exceptions-an.human_outcome: All four steps return to G3; the channel default remains after the exceptions clear.
feature:locks:mask-default-exceptions-an.practice_prompt:
1. With no step held on Note Masks, turn E3 clockwise until Note reads G3 (MIDI 67). All four steps use this channel default.
2. Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 clockwise to C4 (MIDI 72), then release it. Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 clockwise to D4 (MIDI 74), then release it. These two exceptions override the default.
3. Hold step 1 again, press K2 and release the step. Only its exception clears: step 1 returns to G3, while step 2 keeps D4.
4. With no step held, hold K1, press K2 and release K1. All step exceptions clear together; the channel default remains G3.

Use one-step clearing to remove an unwanted variation, or K1 + K2 to restore the common pitch across the channel.

actions.label: Hold the pickup step, choose Velocity, and set 35
Play the phrase with its quiet pickup

modulation-movement-and-interest-level.human_outcome: You hear three beats of C at velocity 80, the D at 50, and a very quiet C pickup at 35 just before the bar restarts; the MIDI strip lists velocity 35 for the step 15 note. After release the screen shows the channel default Vel 80 again. The pickup plays every time. Probability and parameter slides are separate ideas to try after saving this piece.
modulation-movement-and-interest-level.practice_prompt: Shape the dynamics: main beats 80, ending 50, pickup 35.

modulation-movement-and-interest-open-ma.human_outcome: NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X (the pattern notes decide pitch), Vel 80 and Len 1/2: the channel defaults the new trig uses until you give step 15 its own velocity.
modulation-movement-and-interest-open-ma.practice_prompt: Reach the Masks page, where a step can get its own velocity.

actions.label: Add a pickup trig at step 15
Set the pickup to the scale root

modulation-movement-and-interest-pickup.human_outcome: PATTERN NOTE PAT01 shows Step 15 note set to 0, with trigs on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15. The new C falls halfway between the last beat and the next bar. Give it a quieter velocity before listening to the finished pickup.
modulation-movement-and-interest-pickup.practice_prompt: Place a pickup note between the last beat and the next bar.

sequence-composition-bass-open-device.human_outcome: The title row reads DEVICE with CH02. Channel 2 has its own Device row: choose an output that differs from channel 1's in the next stage.
sequence-composition-bass-open-device.practice_prompt: Reach the page where channel 2 is given its own sound.

actions.label: Set the first bass note to the root

sequence-composition-bass-pattern.human_outcome: PATTERN NOTE PAT02 shows Step 9 note set to 4 and a note at (9,3); step 1 stays on the degree-0 baseline at row 7. Only steps 1 and 9 have trigs, so only their pattern notes will sound: C and G in C major. A note shown at a step without a trig does not add an attack.
sequence-composition-bass-pattern.practice_prompt: Write pattern 2: two trigs, one on the root of the scale and one on the fifth.

actions.label: Select MIDI channel 2 and set CC2
Select MIDI port and set OUT 2
Hold the loop start at step 1
Set the loop end at step 16

sequence-composition-bass-route.human_outcome: The screen reads NOTE MASKS CH02 OCT-1 and shows Ch. 2 octave: -1. On the grid, (2,2) is lit on row 2 and (9,8) is lit on the bottom row. Channel 2 now plays pattern 2 an octave down, as MIDI 48 (C2) and 55 (G2) in the default C-major scale, and repeats every 16 steps like channel 1. The output you chose is on its Device page.
sequence-composition-bass-route.practice_prompt: Route channel 2 to its own output, give it pattern 2 and the same 16-step range, then set its octave to -1.

actions.label: Play the phrase above the two-note bass

sequence-composition-both.human_outcome: You hear the phrase above a two-note bass: C on beat 1 and G on beat 3. The strip shows channel 1 on port 1 (60, 60, 60 at velocity 80, 62 at 50) and channel 2 on port 2 (48 and 55 at velocity 100). Each channel keeps its own output, pattern and settings. The two-part result is complete. Continue to Change harmony without changing the rhythm, or try the optional overlap comparison and return to this same phrase before continuing.
sequence-composition-both.practice_prompt: Assign pattern 2 to channel 2, set its loop to steps 1–16, move it down one octave, and play both parts.

actions.label: Play pattern 1 with the bass unchanged

sequence-composition-merge.human_outcome: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 alone, C, C, C, D, and channel 2 keeps its bass (48 and 55). The recorded return leaves Strategy on All; pattern 2 is no longer assigned to channel 1.

actions.label: Choose All for the merge strategy

sequence-composition-merge-all.human_outcome: All four trigs light on row 4 and return in the sound: C, C, C, D. The pitches and velocities come from channel 1's Note and Vel masks, whichever pattern's trig fires.
sequence-composition-merge-all.practice_prompt: Hear that All keeps every trig.

actions.label: Choose Only for the merge strategy

sequence-composition-merge-only.human_outcome: MERGE MODES shows Strategy ONLY with the tooltip ONLY APPLIED, and the (14,8) button changes brightness. Only plays a step only when more than one assigned pattern has a trig there, so on row 4 just steps 1 and 9 stay bright. This example does not play it.

actions.label: Play Skip and compare the shared steps

sequence-composition-merge-skip.human_outcome: With Skip, channel 1 drops overlapping steps 1 and 9. It plays C3 on beat 2 at velocity 80 and D3 on beat 4 at velocity 50. The bass still plays C2 and G2 on beats 1 and 3.
sequence-composition-merge-skip.practice_prompt: Hear why assigning a second pattern to a channel can remove a trig. This detour is optional and you undo it at the end. It edits channel 1 temporarily, so skip it if you would rather not touch the phrase. Merge modes has the full reference.

setup-apply.human_outcome: The DEVICE page lists Device CC Device, MIDI channel CC1 and MIDI port OUT 1 (or your own choices), and the routing is now active for channel 1. You hear it in chapter 3 when the first notes play. If it stays silent, open [No Sound](#no-sound).
setup-apply.practice_prompt: On the Device page, turn E3 once to choose CC Device. Check the Device, MIDI channel, and MIDI port rows, then press K3 to apply; K2 cancels the draft.

setup-route.human_outcome: The title row reads DEVICE with CH01. Only the Device row is listed, set to None: the MIDI channel and MIDI port rows appear once you choose a device. What you change here is only a draft until you press K3.

actions.label: Turn E3 down, then return Tempo to 90 BPM

setup-tempo.human_outcome: GLOBAL FEEL, SONG 01 shows Tempo 90. At the default channel Rate /1, each step is a sixteenth note: four steps make one beat and sixteen steps make one bar.
setup-tempo.practice_prompt: Turn E3 down, then return Tempo to 90 BPM. The page reads 90 before the next lesson.

actions.label: Hold song slot 1 as the copy source

song-composition-copy.human_outcome: Slot 2 holds the same phrase, bass and settings as slot 1. The screen reads SLOT SETUP, SONG 02, the tooltip says Song sequence 2 selected, and (2,1) is the bright slot button.
song-composition-copy.practice_prompt: Make a second section from the complete first section.

actions.label: Set the song length near 16 steps

song-composition-global-length-slot1.human_outcome: SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 01 shows Global length 16. Song mode reads AUTO there, which means Song mode is on and advancing.
song-composition-global-length-slot1.practice_prompt: Make slot 1 one bar long. Global length is how many steps a section lasts before the song moves on; a slot starts at 64.

actions.label: Set the song length near 16 steps

song-composition-global-length-slot2.human_outcome: SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 02 shows Global length 16.
song-composition-global-length-slot2.practice_prompt: Make slot 2 one bar long too, so the song alternates every 2.7 s.

actions.label: Open Slot setup for the song
Choose Song mode, then set Song mode to On

song-composition-length.human_outcome: Slots 1 and 2 form one chain: each plays 16 steps once. After slot 2 the song wraps to slot 1, because slot 3 is empty. The Slot setup screen shows Repeats 1 and Song mode On for SONG 02.
song-composition-length.practice_prompt: Confirm that each section plays once and slot 2 can advance back to slot 1.

song-composition-sparse.human_outcome: The title reads CH01 S02 with no MUTE: channel 1 is audible in slot 2. Slot 1 plays the bass alone; slot 2 plays the bass, the phrase and the pickup.
song-composition-sparse.practice_prompt: Confirm slot 2 keeps the full phrase.

actions.label: Hold K1 as the shift key

song-composition-sparse-muted.human_outcome: The title row shows CH01 MUTE and the tooltip says Channel 1 muted. Slot 1 will play the bass alone.

song-composition-transition.human_outcome: You hear the bass alone, then the bass with the phrase and pickup, then the bass alone, then the bass with the phrase. The screen returns to SLOT SETUP, SONG 01 once you stop.

title: Mosaic manual
